units.summary: Hear the father's warning and stay with the course his words mark out.
units.principle: Listening matures into staying with the instruction we receive.
units.insight: Sound counsel is easier to follow when it is taken seriously before pressure rises.
units.application: Recall one warning from Scripture or a trusted mentor and act on it before the next vulnerable situation.

rel.note: The young man takes the very sort of route to her house that the father tells his son to avoid.

units.notes: Her door is the threshold of the adulterous encounter. Your way refers to the route the son controls.
units.summary: Keep well away from settings that invite adultery.
units.principle: A boundary works best before the moment of greatest pressure.
units.insight: Setting distance early is wise, especially where proximity has repeatedly weakened resolve.
units.application: End a private channel that feeds an inappropriate relationship or change a routine that regularly puts you near it.

rel.note: The warning against adultery there likewise names destruction and lasting dishonor.

units.notes: Honor can include vigor or dignity. The cruel one could be the wronged husband or another merciless person. The text leaves the identity open.
units.summary: Adultery can cost a person dignity and years of life.
units.principle: A brief indulgence can take resources and years that cannot be recovered.
units.insight: When the immediate appeal feels overwhelming, it can help to consider what a decision might cost over years.
units.application: Name a long-term commitment an affair would undermine and protect it with a concrete boundary today.

rel.note: Companionship with prostitutes is likewise shown consuming wealth.

units.notes: Wealth can include strength and working capacity. Labors are what the man has worked to produce.
units.summary: Adultery can cost the resources and fruits of years of work.
units.principle: An unfaithful choice can consume resources that sustain other people.
units.insight: Financial secrecy may hide harm already reaching a household.
units.application: If you are hiding spending tied to an affair, stop the spending and seek accountable help to address the financial harm.

rel.note: The parallel warning describes wounds and dishonor among the consequences of adultery.

units.notes: Mourn has the force of groaning. Flesh and body point to physical wasting, whose exact cause is unspecified.
units.summary: Adultery can leave a person grieving the toll on the body.
units.principle: Choices made for immediate pleasure can carry lasting physical costs.
units.insight: Care for a person in distress can include practical support and appropriate care for the body.
units.application: If a destructive relationship is taking a toll on your health, leave the situation and seek trusted support and appropriate care.

rel.note: Rejecting instruction harms oneself, while heeding correction brings understanding.

units.notes: Instruction is formative discipline. Correction points out where a person has gone wrong.
units.summary: The man grieves that he hated instruction and despised correction.
units.principle: The way we respond to correction can shape the course of our lives.
units.insight: Regret can open a person to counsel they once refused.
units.application: Recall one correction you resented and honestly consider what it asked you to change.

rel.note: A wise son heeds instruction, while a scoffer refuses rebuke.

units.notes: Obeying the voice means heeding it. Inclining the ear recalls the opening appeal of 5:1.
units.summary: The man heard good instruction but failed to heed it.
units.principle: Hearing becomes obedience when it changes the next step.
units.insight: Access to good counsel helps when someone is willing to receive and act on it.
units.application: Tell a trusted teacher or mentor how you will put one piece of sound counsel into practice.

rel.note: The adultery warning likewise emphasizes disgrace and reproach.

units.notes: On the verge means at the brink. Assembly and congregation picture the gathered community. The form of public ruin is unspecified.
units.summary: Secret adultery can bring a person to the brink of public ruin.
units.principle: A private choice can have consequences that reach the whole community.
units.insight: Where wrongdoing has become public, accountability and care can coexist without turning the damage into a spectacle.
units.application: Bring hidden wrongdoing to a trusted, responsible person and begin to address the harm it has caused.

rel.note: The call to rejoice with the wife of one's youth makes the water imagery's marital reference explicit.

units.notes: A cistern stores water, and a well supplies fresh water. The repeated your own marks the marriage relationship.
units.summary: Find refreshment and delight in the intimacy of your own marriage.
units.principle: Sexual intimacy belongs within the faithfulness of marriage.
units.insight: Married love can be cultivated with tenderness, patience, and mutual care, especially in a strained season.
units.application: If you are married, make time to talk with your spouse about how to nurture closeness with mutual care.

rel.note: The following verse makes the exclusivity behind the question explicit.

units.notes: The NKJV treats the line as a question expecting no. The Hebrew also allows a statement, and the precise referent of the scattered waters is debated.
units.summary: Sexual intimacy belongs within marriage, like precious water kept from spilling into the streets.
units.principle: Good desires are to be directed toward their proper relationship.
units.insight: A faithful boundary safeguards intimacy and the trust that allows it to grow.
units.application: Identify an exchange that redirects intimacy away from your marriage and establish a clear boundary around it.

rel.note: The immoral woman forsakes the companion of her youth and forgets her covenant, the opposite of the faithfulness urged here.

units.notes: Only your own intensifies the language of 5:15. Strangers are those outside the marriage.
units.summary: Keep the intimacy of marriage exclusive to husband and wife.
units.principle: Marriage gives sexual intimacy a shared and exclusive home.
units.insight: Faithfulness includes respecting the privacy and trust that spouses share.
units.application: If you are married, discuss a boundary that protects your shared intimacy and agree on how to honor it.

rel.note: Finding a wife is described as a good thing and a gift of the LORD's favor.

units.notes: The fountain continues the water image. The wife of your youth is the spouse with whom the man began married life.
units.summary: Rejoice in the love you share with the wife of your youth.
units.principle: Marriage is a relationship to delight in and cultivate over time.
units.insight: Long familiarity can become a setting for renewed gratitude and affection.
units.application: If you are married, tell your spouse one specific thing you still cherish and set aside time to enjoy each other's company.

rel.note: The next verse uses the same language of being enraptured to question delight in an adulterous embrace.

units.notes: The deer and doe picture grace and beauty. Satisfy carries the sense of drinking one's fill, and enraptured recurs in 5:20.
units.summary: Take lasting delight in the affection and physical intimacy of marriage.
units.principle: Sexual desire has a good place within faithful married love.
units.insight: The invitation to delight calls for tenderness and mutual care, with patience where closeness is painful or difficult.
units.application: If you are married, ask your spouse what helps them feel loved and make room to respond with affection and respect.

rel.note: The preceding verse directs the same capacity for delight toward one's spouse.

units.notes: Enraptured repeats the verb of 5:19. The question contrasts the embrace of a seductress with delight in one's wife.
units.summary: Why let an affair carry away the desire that belongs in faithful married love?
units.principle: Delight in God's good gifts can help guard against destructive substitutes.
units.insight: An attraction can be acknowledged honestly and redirected before it becomes a secret commitment.
units.application: If you are drawn toward an affair, name what you are seeking, cut off the compromising contact, and seek help addressing that desire faithfully.

rel.note: The LORD's eyes are everywhere, watching both the evil and the good.

units.notes: Ways and paths picture a person's choices. Ponders can convey weighing or examining.
units.summary: Every path we take lies open before the LORD and is weighed by Him.
units.principle: Accountability to the LORD reaches every choice, including those made in private.
units.insight: God sees the quiet faithfulness that may go unrecognized by others.
units.application: Bring a private choice before the LORD in prayer and ask what faithfulness would look like in the next step.

rel.note: Confessing and forsaking sin offers a way toward mercy for the person caught in it.

units.notes: Cords are binding ropes. His own puts responsibility on the man whose choices have entrapped him.
units.summary: A person's own sins can become the cords that bind him.
units.principle: Taking responsibility opens the way to confession and change.
units.insight: Those already entangled can turn to Christ for mercy and cleansing and receive help leaving the practice.
units.application: Name the wrongdoing honestly before God, stop the next act that sustains it, and seek trustworthy help to follow through.

rel.note: The young man's fatal course shows in fuller detail where the path of adultery can end.

units.notes: Lack of instruction recalls the discipline he refused in 5:12–13. Go astray repeats the Hebrew verb rendered enraptured in 5:19–20.
units.summary: Refusing instruction lets folly carry a person toward death.
units.principle: A warning about where folly ends is an invitation to turn while we can.
units.insight: Someone who has taken this road can still confess, turn, and receive cleansing in Christ (1 John 1:7–9).
units.application: Receive a correction you have resisted and take a specific step to leave the destructive course it names.

rel.note: The warning against striking hands likewise makes the guarantor's possible loss concrete.

units.notes: Surety is a guarantee of another person's debt. Striking hands sealed a pledge. The exact relationship between the friend and stranger is uncertain.
units.summary: Guaranteeing another person's debt makes their obligation yours if they fail to pay.
units.principle: Understand and weigh the liability before making any pledge.
units.insight: Someone who feels pressure to cosign can offer help within limits they can sustain.
units.application: Avoid cosigning another person's debt. If you choose to help, give only what you are willing and able to lose.

rel.note: The mouth can become a snare for the person who speaks.

units.notes: Snared and taken are pictures of capture. Both lines stress the son's own words.
units.summary: Your own words can trap you in a financial obligation.
units.principle: A promise carries consequences after the moment in which it was made.
units.insight: A pause before answering gives room to weigh a request without yielding to pressure.
units.application: Before agreeing to cover someone else's debt, state plainly what you would owe if they could not pay.

rel.note: The borrower's dependence on the lender illustrates why a debt obligation can put someone in another's power.

units.notes: Falling into a friend's hand means being in another's power. The father urges humility and persistent appeal.
units.summary: Humble yourself and promptly seek release from a rash guarantee.
units.principle: A binding mistake is best addressed through humble and direct action.
units.insight: Admitting a mistaken promise may be the first step toward resolving it honorably.
units.application: If you have made a rash pledge, acknowledge it to the parties involved and ask what would secure an agreed release.

rel.note: The same sleep language describes the sluggard's excuses, while here it stresses urgency.

units.notes: Sleep and slumber repeat the same urgency, in contrast with the sluggard's delay in 6:10.
units.summary: Treat release from a rash guarantee as an urgent priority.
units.principle: Delay can increase exposure to an unresolved obligation.
units.insight: Prompt action can begin with one honest conversation, even if a solution takes time.
units.application: Contact the relevant person today and arrange a time to discuss release.

rel.note: The trouble that comes from guaranteeing a stranger's debt explains the urgency of escape.

units.notes: A fowler catches birds. The gazelle and bird picture creatures struggling to escape capture.
units.summary: Seek release from a rash pledge with the urgency of a creature escaping a trap.
units.principle: A serious entanglement deserves a prompt and sustained effort to resolve it.
units.insight: A difficult obligation can call for energetic follow-through after the first request.
units.application: Follow up on an outstanding release request and agree on the next concrete step.

rel.note: The ant appears again as a small creature whose preparation displays wisdom.

units.notes: Sluggard is the NKJV's word here. Consider calls for careful observation of the ant's habits.
units.summary: Observe the ant and learn habits of diligence.
units.principle: Wisdom learns practical habits from ordinary examples.
units.insight: Illness, disability, depression, and genuine hardship call for support. The rebuke addresses avoidable idleness.
units.application: Identify one task within your ability that you habitually delay and start it at a specific time.

rel.note: The contrast between the diligent and lazy shows different outcomes of taking responsibility for work.

units.notes: Captain, overseer, and ruler name roles of authority. The verse continues the description of the ant.
units.summary: Take initiative without waiting for someone to supervise you.
units.principle: Diligence includes taking responsibility without external pressure.
units.insight: A regular cue can help build self-discipline in a responsibility that otherwise goes unattended.
units.application: Choose a duty you normally wait to be reminded about and complete it before the reminder.

rel.note: The lazy man misses his season to plow and has nothing at harvest.

units.notes: Summer and harvest are seasons when food can be gathered. The ant prepares for later need.
units.summary: Use the available season to prepare for coming needs.
units.principle: Foresight makes use of opportunities before they close.
units.insight: Small preparations made early can ease pressure when options narrow.
units.application: Choose an upcoming need and take one preparatory step while time or supplies are available.

rel.note: The lazy man's turning on his bed pictures movement without getting up to work.

units.notes: How long and when are questions that expose repeated delay. The father assumes the sluggard can rise.
units.summary: The time to end habitual delay is now.
units.principle: An intention to start later needs a time and a first action.
units.insight: It helps to distinguish needed rest from repeatedly putting off a responsibility one can meet.
units.application: Pick an achievable task you have postponed and begin it at a specific time today.

rel.note: The lesson from the neglected field repeats almost the same words.

units.notes: The repeated little makes each delay sound harmless. Folded hands picture inactivity. The thought continues in 6:11.
units.summary: Repeated small delays can become a settled habit of idleness.
units.principle: A habit is built out of choices that may seem insignificant on their own.
units.insight: People can often interrupt the pattern by making the first step easier and more concrete.
units.application: Replace your usual one-more-minute delay with five minutes of starting the task.

rel.note: The same images conclude the warning drawn from the overgrown field.

units.notes: A prowler arrives unexpectedly, and an armed man pictures need that is hard to resist.
units.summary: Habitual neglect can bring need that seems to arrive all at once.
units.principle: Repeated neglect can quietly create consequences that are difficult to reverse.
units.insight: Someone facing poverty deserves care and a fair hearing about their circumstances.
units.application: Look for one neglected obligation whose costs are accumulating and take a manageable step to address it.

rel.note: The learner is told to put away the crooked speech that marks this man.

units.notes: Walking pictures an ongoing way of life. A perverse mouth twists what should be straight.
units.summary: The troublemaker makes crooked speech a way of life.
units.principle: A pattern of speech reveals the direction a person is taking.
units.insight: Repeated distortion can be addressed with truthful clarification before it spreads.
units.application: If you have repeatedly twisted a story to your advantage, correct it with the people who heard it.

rel.note: The wink is likewise pictured as causing trouble in a context of deceitful conduct.

units.notes: Winking, foot movements, and pointing may be covert signals. Their purpose matters more than the gestures themselves.
units.summary: The troublemaker can use gestures as well as words to deceive.
units.principle: Deceit can enlist nonverbal behavior as well as speech.
units.insight: An isolated gesture gives little basis for judging someone's intent. A clear pattern can be addressed directly.
units.application: Refuse to participate in a covert signal meant to mislead or mock someone.

rel.note: Sowing discord closes both the troublemaker's portrait and the list of things the LORD hates.

units.notes: Heart means thought, will, and desire. Sowing discord pictures planting strife that spreads among others.
units.summary: A crooked heart plots harm and plants discord.
units.principle: Repeated discord can begin with deliberate choices in the heart.
units.insight: Conflict can spread through a person who keeps feeding suspicion between others.
units.application: Before repeating a divisive report, check its truth and ask whether speaking directly would serve peace.

rel.note: Repeated refusal to change can likewise end in sudden ruin without remedy.

units.notes: Broken pictures being shattered. Without remedy means without healing or repair.
units.summary: Persistent troublemaking can end in sudden, irreparable collapse.
units.principle: Deliberate harm can have irreversible consequences.
units.insight: The warning gives a person time to stop a pattern before it does damage they cannot undo.
units.application: Stop one scheme or divisive action you are pursuing and make any repair still possible.

rel.note: Agur uses the same rising-number form to introduce a list of things he finds wonderful.

units.notes: Six followed by seven is a rising-number pattern that builds toward the final item.
units.summary: The LORD detests the evils that follow, with sowing discord receiving the final emphasis.
units.principle: God's opposition to evil includes the harm people do to one another's fellowship.
units.insight: Teaching this list can help a community take relational harm seriously alongside more visible wrongs.
units.application: Read 6:17–19 as one list and identify one attitude or action to bring before God.

rel.note: Wisdom likewise names pride and perverse speech among the things she hates.

units.notes: Proud eyes picture arrogance. Shedding innocent blood describes violence against someone who has done no wrong.
units.summary: The LORD hates pride, lying, and the shedding of innocent blood.
units.principle: God judges the arrogance and falsehood that can accompany acts of violence.
units.insight: Confronting contempt and lies early can help protect people who are vulnerable to harm.
units.application: Correct a lie you have told, and take a concrete step to protect someone harmed by it.

rel.note: The violent gang's feet likewise run toward evil and bloodshed.

units.notes: The heart is the source of plans. Feet swift to evil picture eagerness to carry them out.
units.summary: The LORD hates both plotting evil and hurrying to carry it out.
units.principle: Accountability includes the harm we intend as well as the harm we do.
units.insight: A plan can be stopped while it is still possible to spare others its consequences.
units.application: Abandon one plan aimed at harming someone and replace it with an honest way to address the underlying issue.

rel.note: The troublemaker's steady occupation includes the same sowing of discord.

units.notes: A false witness lies in testimony. Brethren are people who belong together. Sowing pictures strife being planted.
units.summary: The LORD hates false testimony and the stirring up of discord among people who belong together.
units.principle: Truthful testimony and peace protect a community from deliberate harm.
units.insight: Peacemaking can begin by refusing to relay a false or divisive account.
units.application: Verify what you report in a dispute and correct a false statement before it spreads further.

rel.note: The opening appeal likewise places the father's instruction beside the mother's teaching.

units.notes: Keep involves guarding and obeying. The mother's law means her instruction.
units.summary: Keep the sound teaching of both father and mother.
units.principle: Parental instruction is meant to be remembered and practiced.
units.insight: Both parents can shape wisdom through what they teach and model.
units.application: Recall one sound lesson from a parent or caregiver and apply it to a current decision.

rel.note: Mercy and truth are likewise bound around the neck and written on the heart.

units.notes: Binding pictures fastening securely. The heart concerns inward conviction and the neck suggests visible conduct.
units.summary: Keep sound instruction close enough to shape both conviction and conduct.
units.principle: What is held in the heart should become visible in practice.
units.insight: A familiar teaching can become a steady guide when brought to mind at the point of decision.
units.application: Put a reminder of one sound instruction where you will see it before a choice it should shape.

rel.note: The safe path and the command to hold fast to instruction show why teaching serves as a guide.

units.notes: Walking, sleeping, and waking span daily life. Instruction is pictured as a companion that leads, guards, and speaks.
units.summary: Internalized instruction guides and guards across the ordinary rhythms of life.
units.principle: Instruction becomes a ready guide when it is carried into daily life.
units.insight: A well-learned truth can steady someone when no adviser is nearby.
units.application: Recall one wise instruction in the morning and apply it as you plan the day.

rel.note: Listening to life-giving reproof places a learner among the wise.

units.notes: An ancient lamp made the next steps visible. Law here continues the parental instruction of 6:20.
units.summary: Faithful instruction lights the path, and correction helps keep us on the way of life.
units.principle: Wise reproof belongs to guidance that leads toward life.
units.insight: Correction can make the next right step visible even when it is hard to receive.
units.application: Identify a sound correction and use it to name the next right step in a choice you face.

rel.note: Wisdom likewise delivers the learner from the seductress who flatters with her words.

units.notes: The protection continues the lamp image in 6:23. The flattering tongue describes persuasive speech.
units.summary: Wise teaching helps you recognize and refuse flattering invitations to adultery.
units.principle: Instruction protects when we use it to recognize and refuse temptation.
units.insight: People can learn to notice when flattering attention starts to ask for secrecy.
units.application: If flattering contact is drawing you toward unfaithfulness, identify the pressure clearly and end the compromising exchange.

rel.note: The general call to direct the gaze becomes concrete here in the face of sexual temptation.

units.notes: Lust after means to desire or covet. Eyelids stand for the alluring gaze.
units.summary: Refuse to cultivate adulterous desire in your heart.
units.principle: Faithfulness involves governing what we allow desire to grow into.
units.insight: Recognizing an attraction early makes it possible to redirect attention and seek help.
units.application: Redirect your attention when it becomes a way of feeding desire for someone outside your marriage.

rel.note: The warning about wasting wealth with prostitutes illustrates the first kind of cost.

units.notes: The NKJV pictures a man brought to a crust of bread. Some translations read that line as a price. Prey upon pictures hunting.
units.summary: Buying sex can drain resources, and adultery puts one's very life at risk.
units.principle: The apparent price of sexual wrongdoing can conceal a far greater cost.
units.insight: The financial and personal costs of sexual wrongdoing can affect an entire household.
units.application: Cut off spending or contact that sustains sexual wrongdoing and seek accountable help to stop the pattern.

rel.note: Keeping away from her door gives a practical response to the danger pictured by fire.

units.notes: Bosom means the chest or the fold of clothing held against it. Fire burns what it touches.
units.summary: Taking adultery close is like holding fire against your clothes.
units.principle: Closeness to a destructive practice brings exposure to its harm.
units.insight: A person can step back when they first see how close they have brought a temptation.
units.application: End an arrangement that keeps an adulterous opportunity close, such as a private meeting or message thread.

rel.note: The young man's deliberate route to her house illustrates a step onto the dangerous path.

units.notes: Hot coals are burning embers. Walking adds the image of taking one deliberate step after another.
units.summary: Walking into adultery is like stepping onto burning coals.
units.principle: Consequences can begin with the steps that lead toward the act.
units.insight: A person who has started down a harmful path can still take a different next step.
units.application: Identify the next step in a compromising pattern and change the route before you take it.

rel.note: The same warning goes on to name adultery as a choice that destroys the person who commits it.

units.notes: Goes in to refers to sexual relations. Shall not be innocent can also carry the sense of incurring punishment.
units.summary: Adultery with a neighbor's spouse brings guilt and violates a marriage.
units.principle: Private agreement cannot erase responsibility for wrong done to others.
units.insight: Betrayal harms people beyond those who choose the affair.
units.application: End contact that is crossing a marital boundary and seek help to take responsibility for any harm already done.

rel.note: Agur recognizes that poverty can tempt a person to steal.

units.notes: Despise means to treat with contempt. To satisfy himself here means to fill a hungry appetite.
units.summary: Hunger can explain a theft and stir sympathy for the person who stole.
units.principle: Understanding a motive helps us respond with compassion and justice together.
units.insight: A just response can address real hunger while taking the loss seriously.
units.application: When you encounter real hunger, offer practical help while respecting the rights of those affected.

rel.note: Restitution is possible for the thief, while the wronged husband refuses payment.

units.notes: Sevenfold most likely stresses full restitution. Substance means the goods of the household.
units.summary: Even a theft driven by hunger can require costly restitution.
units.principle: Understanding someone's need does not erase the obligation to restore what was taken.
units.insight: Mercy toward the person who stole can coexist with taking the loss seriously.
units.application: If you have taken something, return it or arrange to repay the person affected.

rel.note: The sinner is likewise pictured as caught by his own choices.

units.notes: Lacks understanding is literally lacks heart, meaning sound judgment. Soul here means the whole self or life.
units.summary: Adultery is a failure of judgment that brings ruin on the person who chooses it.
units.principle: Sound judgment weighs the outcome of a desire before acting on it.
units.insight: A truthful warning can help a person see beyond the satisfaction an affair promises.
units.application: If an affair has begun, end it and seek trustworthy help to take responsibility and turn back.

rel.note: Mercy for those who confess and forsake sin addresses the question of forgiveness alongside lasting reproach.

units.notes: Wounds point to injury, and reproach is lasting disgrace among people.
units.summary: Adultery can leave lasting wounds and dishonor.
units.principle: Repentance and mercy can coexist with consequences that take time to address.
units.insight: A person can receive God's forgiveness and still need to face the harm patiently and honestly.
units.application: Confess and end the wrongdoing, then seek help taking responsibility without demanding immediate restoration of trust.

rel.note: The counsel to wait for the LORD supplies direction for a reader who feels the desire for retaliation described here.

units.notes: Jealousy here is the wronged husband's fierce anger. The day of vengeance is the time he seeks to respond.
units.summary: Adultery can provoke fierce anger in the spouse whose marriage has been betrayed.
units.principle: The harm of adultery includes a real wrong to the betrayed spouse.
units.insight: Betrayal can produce intense anger that needs a safe, truthful way to be expressed.
units.application: If you are responding to betrayal, seek trustworthy support and address the wrong without threats or retaliation.

rel.note: The thief can make restitution, while the injured husband refuses a financial settlement.

units.notes: Recompense means payment or ransom offered to settle a wrong. Gifts picture repeated attempts to appease the husband.
units.summary: Gifts and payments cannot buy away the harm of adultery.
units.principle: Relational betrayal cannot be settled as though it were only a financial loss.
units.insight: A harmed spouse may need honesty, time, and space more than gestures from the person who caused the harm.
units.application: Take responsibility through truth and changed conduct without using gifts to press for reconciliation.

rel.note: The father repeats the same call to treasure his commands within.

units.notes: Treasure pictures storing something precious within reach.
units.summary: Store wise instruction in your heart before you need it.
units.principle: Instruction protects as it is valued and practiced.
units.insight: A treasured word can come to mind when pressure narrows our choices.
units.application: Choose one warning about faithfulness and rehearse how you will act on it.

rel.note: The father also ties keeping commands to life.

units.notes: The apple of the eye is the pupil, which the body instinctively protects.
units.summary: Guard life-giving instruction as carefully as your sight.
units.principle: What guides life deserves vigilant care.
units.insight: A protective habit can help keep a conviction in view under pressure.
units.application: Put a reminder of a wise boundary where you will see it before a vulnerable decision.

rel.note: The tablet of the heart likewise pictures internalizing mercy and truth.

units.notes: Fingers picture action, and a tablet holds an enduring inscription. The heart includes thought, will, and desire.
units.summary: Let instruction shape both what you do and what you desire.
units.principle: Wise instruction belongs in the heart and at the point of action.
units.insight: Remembering words helps when they are allowed to challenge our motives and choices.
units.application: Connect one instruction about faithfulness to a concrete daily habit.

rel.note: The learner is likewise urged to love Wisdom and stay close to her.

units.notes: Sister and nearest kin are language of affection and trusted closeness.
units.summary: Keep wisdom as close as a trusted family member.
units.principle: Affection for wisdom makes it easier to listen under pressure.
units.insight: People grow teachable when they learn to welcome wise counsel as a friend.
units.application: Make a regular time to seek counsel from someone whose wisdom you trust.

rel.note: The earlier warning uses the same language about the seductress's flattering words.

units.notes: They refers to wisdom and understanding. Flattery makes words smooth and persuasive.
units.summary: Wisdom helps guard against the flattering invitation to adultery.
units.principle: Discernment tests what flattering words invite us to do.
units.insight: The need to feel noticed can make smooth attention harder to assess.
units.application: When attention asks you to cross a marital boundary, name the request plainly and refuse it.

rel.note: Another observer turns what he sees into instruction for the reader.

units.notes: A lattice is a screen across a window.
units.summary: The father watches from his window as the scene unfolds.
units.principle: Wisdom considers the whole course of a decision.
units.insight: An observer may notice a dangerous pattern that someone inside it overlooks.
units.application: Ask a trusted observer what pattern they see in a choice that feels hard to assess.

rel.note: The same expression for lacking judgment describes the person who commits adultery.

units.notes: The simple are uncommitted and easily led. Devoid of understanding literally means lacking heart, or judgment.
units.summary: An uncommitted heart leaves the young man open to being led into adultery.
units.principle: An unsettled conviction leaves room for competing desires to set our course.
units.insight: Inexperience can be met with guidance and a clear commitment before pressure arrives.
units.application: State one commitment to faithfulness and tell a trusted person how you intend to keep it.

rel.note: The father explicitly commands the distance this young man fails to keep.

units.notes: Her corner is the place he passes. He takes the road toward her house himself.
units.summary: The young man takes responsibility for the road he chooses toward her house.
units.principle: Choosing proximity can make a foreseeable temptation harder to resist.
units.insight: A firm boundary works best before the moment of greatest pressure.
units.application: Change the route, routine, or channel that keeps taking you close to a known temptation.

rel.note: Every path remains open to the LORD even when darkness hides it from people.

units.notes: Twilight, evening, and dark night mark fading light and increasing concealment.
units.summary: Darkness gives the young man's approach the cover of secrecy.
units.principle: Secrecy can make a wrong course feel easier to pursue.
units.insight: A choice that feels safer only because it is hidden deserves a fresh look.
units.application: Bring one choice you are keeping hidden into a conversation with a trustworthy person.

rel.note: The father warns against letting a deliberate appeal to the eyes capture the heart.

units.notes: Attire describes her presentation, and crafty heart points to concealed intent. Verse 19 shows she is married.
units.summary: The young man meets an opportunity for adultery along the road he chose.
units.principle: The places we choose affect the opportunities we encounter.
units.insight: Prepare a response for a foreseeable opportunity before it presents itself.
units.application: Decide in advance how you will leave an encounter if it starts to invite unfaithfulness.

rel.note: Personified Folly is also portrayed as clamorous, echoing this scene.

units.notes: Loud and rebellious describe restless defiance. Her feet picture her chosen course.
units.summary: The woman refuses the restraints of marital faithfulness.
units.principle: Restlessness can express a deeper refusal of rightful commitments.
units.insight: A pattern of broken commitments deserves more attention than an isolated impression.
units.application: Name a commitment you have been evading and choose one concrete way to honor it.

rel.note: Wisdom uses public places to call people openly, while the woman uses them to lie in wait.

units.notes: The street and square are public gathering places. Lurking pictures lying in wait.
units.summary: The woman watches for an opportunity wherever people pass.
units.principle: Wise boundaries address patterns as well as particular locations.
units.insight: Recurring pressures may require a consistent boundary across settings.
units.application: Identify where the same compromising invitation appears in more than one setting.

rel.note: The father's warning names the seductive embrace this scene begins to depict.

units.notes: Impudent describes a brazen expression. She seizes and kisses him before speaking.
units.summary: The woman's bold physical advance begins her direct enticement.
units.principle: An advance calls for a response consistent with the commitments already made.
units.insight: Someone facing an unwanted or compromising advance can step away and seek support.
units.application: Decide how you would create distance and ask for help if a physical boundary were crossed.

rel.note: A sacrifice offered with wicked intent shows why religious activity cannot legitimize wrongdoing.

units.notes: Peace offerings could provide meat for a shared meal. Paying vows refers to fulfilling religious obligations.
units.summary: The woman uses the language of worship to make her invitation sound acceptable.
units.principle: A fulfilled religious obligation cannot excuse a wrong choice.
units.insight: Religious activity can coexist with choices that need honest correction.
units.application: Test any religious reason you are using to justify a choice against what God actually asks of you.

rel.note: The shared language of diligent seeking highlights the difference between Wisdom's invitation and the woman's pursuit.

units.notes: Seeking diligently describes eager pursuit. She presents the encounter as personally intended.
units.summary: The woman flatters the young man by telling him she has been looking for him.
units.principle: Personal attention should be weighed by the purpose it serves.
units.insight: A desire to be noticed can make flattering attention especially persuasive.
units.application: When flattery makes a questionable request feel special, state the request plainly before answering.

rel.note: The warning about coveting in the heart addresses the inward response this appeal seeks.

units.notes: Tapestry and Egyptian linen describe decorated, costly bed coverings.
units.summary: The woman uses luxury to make the young man imagine the encounter.
units.principle: What we invite the imagination to dwell on can influence our choices.
units.insight: Repeatedly picturing a forbidden encounter can make it feel easier to pursue.
units.application: Interrupt a recurring fantasy and redirect attention to a constructive action.

rel.note: The earlier contrast between sweetness and bitterness helps weigh this sensory appeal.

units.notes: Myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon are costly fragrances. The prepared bed is the same one described in 7:16.
units.summary: Perfume makes the promised pleasure more vivid in the young man's imagination.
units.principle: An appealing setting can distract us from where a choice leads.
units.insight: A setting that intensifies temptation can be left before it gains more influence.
units.application: Leave a setting that is feeding a compromising desire and redirect your attention.

rel.note: Similar language about satisfaction celebrates delight within marriage there.

units.notes: Take our fill evokes drinking deeply. The woman repeatedly calls her proposal love.
units.summary: The woman calls adultery love to make it easier to accept.
units.principle: Pleasant language cannot change the character of a choice.
units.insight: Naming an act truthfully can interrupt a justification that has begun to feel plausible.
units.application: Replace the flattering label for a compromising relationship with an honest description of what it involves.

rel.note: The LORD sees the paths people think are hidden.

units.notes: The absent man is her husband. His long journey makes her assurance sound plausible.
units.summary: The woman tries to make adultery seem safe because her husband is away.
units.principle: Secrecy cannot remove accountability before God.
units.insight: A choice still deserves honest judgment when discovery seems unlikely.
units.application: Ask whether you would make the same choice if it were brought into the open before God and those affected.

rel.note: Folly likewise sells the pleasure of secrecy while hiding the destination.

units.notes: The money bag and appointed return suggest a planned absence. The appointed day may refer to the full moon.
units.summary: A planned absence gives the young man a false sense of safety.
units.principle: Managing the chance of discovery is different from making a wise choice.
units.insight: Detailed arrangements can conceal a faulty premise about what makes a choice safe.
units.application: Give up a plan whose appeal depends on someone else being away or unaware.

rel.note: The earlier portrait also stresses the persuasive smoothness of the woman's words.

units.notes: Enticing speech is persuasive talk. Flattering lips repeat the picture of smooth words.
units.summary: Persuasive flattery wears down the young man's resistance.
units.principle: Words can move a person toward action when they are allowed to keep shaping the choice.
units.insight: A conversation can be ended when its repeated pressure is weakening resolve.
units.application: End a repeated exchange that presses you to compromise and tell a trusted person what happened.

rel.note: The cords of sin likewise show how one's own choices can become a trap.

units.notes: The ox goes unsuspecting to slaughter. The Hebrew behind the NKJV's fool and stocks image is difficult, and some translations picture a trapped deer.
units.summary: The young man yields suddenly after taking a series of steps toward adultery.
units.principle: Earlier decisions can prepare the ground for a later act of yielding.
units.insight: An apparently sudden fall can be examined by tracing the choices that made it easier.
units.application: Trace a recurring failure back to its earliest avoidable step and put a boundary there.

rel.note: God's sight and sin's cords explain two realities the young man overlooks.

units.notes: The liver wound pictures mortal injury. A bird hurries toward bait without seeing the snare.
units.summary: The young man rushes toward ruin without seeing what it will cost him.
units.principle: The immediate reward can hide a loss far greater than the pleasure offered.
units.insight: A warning about consequences can restore perspective before a pressured choice.
units.application: Before a tempting choice, recall God's instruction, name its likely costs, and remember that He sees the path.

rel.note: The father likewise asks his children to heed his words in the face of sexual temptation.

units.notes: Now therefore draws the lesson from the story. My children broadens the appeal.
units.summary: Give the father's warning your attention while you can still change course.
units.principle: A wise hearer learns from consequences witnessed in another life.
units.insight: Another person's story can make a warning concrete before we face the same pressure.
units.application: Identify one decision in the story you can learn from and act on the lesson today.

rel.note: The earlier appeal likewise joins guarding the heart to governing where the feet go.

units.notes: Turning aside begins with the heart. Straying describes the feet drifting onto another course.
units.summary: Guard both your heart and your steps against the path of adultery.
units.principle: The heart and the path need to be guarded together.
units.insight: A practical boundary is easier to keep when it expresses a commitment already made inwardly.
units.application: Name a desire you need to redirect and place a specific boundary on the route that feeds it.

rel.note: The fire questions likewise challenge the assumption that a person can approach adultery safely.

units.notes: Many were wounded. The NKJV describes the slain as strong men, while some versions stress their number.
units.summary: Even strong people can be brought down by adultery.
units.principle: Personal strength cannot substitute for staying clear of a destructive path.
units.insight: People others look up to also need accountability and safe boundaries.
units.application: Invite a trusted person to ask about one area where you have assumed you are above temptation.

rel.note: Folly's house likewise conceals death behind an invitation to secret pleasure.

units.notes: Hell here renders Sheol, the realm of the dead. Chambers are inner rooms, recalling her prepared bedroom.
units.summary: The house that promises adulterous pleasure leads down to death.
units.principle: Wisdom judges an invitation by its destination and turns toward the life God gives.
units.insight: Those who have walked this path can confess and forsake sin and receive cleansing in Christ (1 John 1:7–9).
units.application: Leave the course that is leading toward ruin, confess what you have done, and seek help to follow through.

rel.note: Wisdom likewise raises her voice publicly in the streets and at the gates.

units.notes: The opening question expects yes. Wisdom is described in the third person through 8:3 and speaks from 8:4.
units.summary: Wisdom raises her voice openly and calls for a hearing.
units.principle: God's wisdom makes its appeal openly.
units.insight: People who feel far from wisdom are among those called to listen.
units.application: Read Wisdom's question slowly and ask Christ where you need to give His instruction a hearing.

rel.note: The young man takes the path toward the woman's house, while Wisdom stations herself at the place of choice.

units.notes: The hilltop makes Wisdom visible. Where paths meet is a crossroads where travelers choose a direction.
units.summary: Wisdom makes herself heard where people choose which way to go.
units.principle: Wisdom belongs at the point of decision.
units.insight: A crossroads can be an occasion to seek wise guidance before taking another step.
units.application: Name a decision you are approaching and seek sound counsel before committing to a route.

rel.note: The earlier portrait also places Wisdom's call at the entrances and city gates.

units.notes: City gates served trade, judgment, and public life. The entrances were places people passed continually.
units.summary: Wisdom calls at the places where the community conducts its affairs.
units.principle: Public life needs sound judgment as much as private life does.
units.insight: Wisdom is needed in ordinary work, transactions, and public responsibilities.
units.application: Bring one public or workplace decision under the same standard of integrity you would apply in private.

rel.note: The same expression for humanity names the people in whom Wisdom delights.

units.notes: Sons of men means human beings. Wisdom starts speaking directly here.
units.summary: Wisdom calls directly to people everywhere.
units.principle: The invitation to wisdom reaches people in ordinary life.
units.insight: A hearer need not wait until they feel qualified to begin listening to Christ.
units.application: Read Wisdom's appeal as addressed to you and respond to one instruction you already understand.

rel.note: Wisdom also invites the simple and those lacking understanding to turn in and learn to live.

units.notes: The simple are uncommitted and easily led. Fools resist wisdom. Heart here means inner sense and judgment.
units.summary: Wisdom invites the simple and fools to gain sound judgment.
units.principle: Teachability can begin wherever a person presently stands.
units.insight: Someone who has resisted correction can still begin listening and learning.
units.application: Name one area where you are easily led or resistant to counsel and ask a wise person for help.

rel.note: The woman's smooth persuasion draws the young man toward harm, while Wisdom speaks uprightly.

units.notes: Excellent things are noble things. What is right is pictured as straight or upright.
units.summary: Listen to Wisdom because her words are noble and right.
units.principle: The worth of counsel depends on its truth and direction.
units.insight: A plain correction may deserve attention even when flattering words feel better.
units.application: Compare an appealing message with sound counsel and choose the advice that leads uprightly.

rel.note: The LORD detests lying lips and delights in people who deal truthfully.

units.notes: Truth here carries reliability. Abomination expresses strong moral revulsion.
units.summary: Wisdom speaks reliable truth and detests wickedness.
units.principle: Faithful speech refuses to enlist falsehood in service of its goals.
units.insight: People can rebuild trust by making their words consistent with what is true.
units.application: Correct one claim you have repeated without checking whether it is true.

rel.note: The learner is urged to put away the crooked speech absent from Wisdom's words.

units.notes: Crooked and perverse picture words twisted out of shape. All makes the claim comprehensive.
units.summary: All Wisdom's words are upright and free of distortion.
units.principle: Righteous speech is straight in both wording and purpose.
units.insight: A true statement can still be misused when its framing hides what is really being asked.
units.application: Revise an explanation that is technically accurate but likely to leave a misleading impression.

rel.note: Knowledge comes readily to the person who has understanding.

units.notes: Plain means straightforward to the person who understands. Right describes what is straight and true.
units.summary: Those who grow in understanding recognize Wisdom's words as straight and right.
units.principle: Growing discernment helps us recognize sound instruction.
units.insight: A difficult saying can be approached patiently with help from an experienced reader.
units.application: Bring a proverb you find difficult to a trusted learner and ask how its context clarifies it.

rel.note: This saying also ranks wisdom and understanding above gold and silver.

units.notes: Instruction includes training and correction. Choice gold is the finest gold.
units.summary: Choose instruction and knowledge ahead of silver and gold.
units.principle: Sound instruction is worth more than the money we might choose in its place.
units.insight: A desire for gain can make an inconvenient correction easy to ignore.
units.application: Make time to learn or receive correction before committing to a profitable opportunity.

rel.note: The father makes the same comparison with precious stones and all other desires.

units.notes: Rubies stand for precious jewels, and the precise stone is uncertain.
units.summary: Wisdom exceeds the worth of anything else we might desire.
units.principle: Wisdom deserves priority because it directs how other goods are used.
units.insight: A strong desire can be named honestly and then weighed before it becomes a decision.
units.application: Identify one desired gain and name the wise commitment you will keep even if it costs you that gain.

rel.note: Wisdom entering the heart brings knowledge, discretion, and understanding together.

units.notes: Dwelling with prudence pictures close association. Discretion includes planning and thinking ahead.
units.summary: Wisdom lives alongside prudence, knowledge, and discretion.
units.principle: Wisdom brings knowledge and foresight into practical decisions.
units.insight: A person can cultivate sound judgment by pausing to understand a situation before reacting.
units.application: Before a difficult decision, identify a fact you still need and one consequence you should consider.

rel.note: Humility, fear of the LORD, and turning away from evil are likewise joined.

units.notes: Fear of the LORD means seeing God rightly. The perverse mouth speaks in ways that twist what is right.
units.summary: To fear the LORD is to hate evil, including pride and twisted speech.
units.principle: Reverence for God changes what we approve in ourselves and others.
units.insight: Seeing God's holiness can help someone recognize pride they have been defending.
units.application: Name one proud habit or dishonest way of speaking and take a step to leave it.

rel.note: Strength, knowledge, and wise counsel are brought together in facing a difficult undertaking.

units.notes: Counsel is sound advice. Sound wisdom is practical judgment that works.
units.summary: Wisdom joins sound counsel and understanding to strength for action.
units.principle: Effective wisdom includes judgment and the capacity to act on it.
units.insight: A sound plan may still require courage and support to carry it out.
units.application: For a decision you already understand, ask what support or courage would help you follow through.

rel.note: A king who practices justice establishes the land.

units.notes: Kings exercise authority, and decrees are rules or judgments issued by rulers.
units.summary: Kings and rulers need wisdom to govern justly.
units.principle: Authority serves its proper purpose when it is directed by wisdom and justice.
units.insight: Those entrusted with authority need accountability and sound judgment.
units.application: Before setting a rule that affects others, seek counsel and test it for fairness.

rel.note: The ruler is urged to use judgment and authority in defense of those who need a hearing.

units.notes: Princes, nobles, and judges broaden the picture to other ranks. Some translations end with those who judge justly.
units.summary: Wisdom is needed wherever people govern or judge.
units.principle: Every level of responsibility calls for just judgment.
units.insight: A small decision made by someone with authority can matter greatly to the person affected.
units.application: Give the person affected by a decision a fair hearing before you decide.

rel.note: The father also describes Wisdom's faithful response to the learner's love.

units.notes: Seeking diligently is eager, attentive pursuit. The poem speaks in the language of mutual love.
units.summary: Wisdom loves those who love her and is found by those who seek her earnestly.
units.principle: Love for Wisdom gives rise to earnest seeking.
units.insight: Seeking Christ can be an expression of affection and trust as well as a response to need.
units.application: Set aside time to seek Christ about a real decision and follow the wisdom you receive in Scripture.

rel.note: Wisdom is likewise pictured holding riches and honor.

units.notes: Riches and honor are joined to righteousness. Enduring describes what holds its worth over time.
units.summary: Wisdom's riches and honor are bound up with enduring righteousness.
units.principle: Wealth has lasting worth when it goes with righteousness.
units.insight: A person of modest means can possess the enduring goods Wisdom commends.
units.application: Choose one way to use money or influence that builds a good you can keep without compromising integrity.

rel.note: Wisdom's proceeds and gain there also surpass silver and fine gold.

units.notes: Fruit and revenue picture the yield of wisdom. Fine gold and choice silver represent costly alternatives.
units.summary: Wisdom's fruit is better than the finest gold and silver.
units.principle: The return on wisdom is measured by the life it produces.
units.insight: Character and a clear conscience can be more valuable than a gain that puts them at risk.
units.application: Evaluate a possible gain by asking what kind of character pursuing it would cultivate.

rel.note: Wisdom is likewise associated with justice and every good path.

units.notes: Traverse means to walk along. The middle of a path pictures remaining squarely within it.
units.summary: Wisdom walks squarely in the paths of righteousness and justice.
units.principle: Wisdom's benefits belong with the righteous paths she walks.
units.insight: When a choice seems efficient but unfair, Wisdom's own course gives a way to test it.
units.application: Review one choice for fairness to those affected and adjust it before proceeding.

rel.note: Wisdom's gifts include riches and honor, while her worth exceeds their value.

units.notes: Inheritance pictures a gift received. Filled storehouses picture abundant provision.
units.summary: Wisdom gives her lovers a rich inheritance along the paths of righteousness.
units.principle: The lasting wealth of wisdom is inseparable from her righteous way.
units.insight: A person can receive the fruits of wisdom gratefully even when material circumstances remain difficult.
units.application: Name one good wisdom has produced in your life and use it to serve someone else.

rel.note: The LORD founded the earth by wisdom, the truth this poem develops through Wisdom's speech.

units.notes: Qanah can mean acquire, possess, or create. The Septuagint reads created, a rendering Arius used to argue that the Son was created.
units.summary: Wisdom belonged to the LORD before His works of old.
units.principle: God's wisdom precedes all the works He has made.
units.insight: Believers can trust the wisdom of Christ as the wisdom of the eternal Son.
units.application: Read this verse with John 1:1–3 and thank Christ for the wisdom with which He made the world.

rel.note: The previous verse also places Wisdom with the LORD before His works.

units.notes: Established conveys being set in place. From everlasting places Wisdom before the earth's beginning.
units.summary: Wisdom was established from everlasting, before there was an earth.
units.principle: Wisdom belongs to God from everlasting.
units.insight: Christ's wisdom can be trusted when the things we usually rely on prove temporary.
units.application: Bring a temporary concern before the eternal Son and ask how His wisdom should order your response.

rel.note: The poem later describes the LORD establishing the fountains that had yet to exist here.

units.notes: Depths and fountains picture ancient waters and springs. Brought forth uses birth imagery.
units.summary: Wisdom was there before the deep waters and springs.
units.principle: Even the oldest features of creation come after the Wisdom of God.
units.insight: The poetic image can deepen reverence for Christ when read alongside the New Testament's clear testimony.
units.application: Read the birth image alongside John 1:1–2 and give thanks for the eternal Son.

rel.note: The earth's foundations are later described as marked out with Wisdom present.

units.notes: Settled suggests mountains set firmly in place. Brought forth repeats the image of 8:24.
units.summary: Wisdom precedes even the mountains and hills.
units.principle: The Wisdom of God is older than the most enduring features of creation.
units.insight: What seems most lasting in our surroundings can remind us of the greater permanence of Christ.
units.application: Let a familiar feature of the landscape remind you to rest your confidence in the eternal Son.

rel.note: The LORD is likewise said to have founded the earth by wisdom.

units.notes: The fields are open lands. Primal dust pictures the earliest material of the inhabited world.
units.summary: Wisdom was present before the earth, the fields, and their first dust.
units.principle: Creation depends on the LORD's wisdom down to its earliest beginnings.
units.insight: Ordinary ground and the work it supports are occasions to remember God's wise ordering.
units.application: Thank God for a basic provision from the earth and use it with care today.

rel.note: The LORD established the heavens by understanding.

units.notes: The circle on the deep pictures an ordered boundary or horizon. I was there marks the move to creation itself.
units.summary: Wisdom was there when the LORD prepared the heavens and marked the deep.
units.principle: God's ordering of creation displays His wisdom.
units.insight: A world made through Christ can be received with attention and gratitude.
units.application: Look at one feature of creation today and thank Christ for His part in making it.

rel.note: The depths and clouds likewise display the LORD's knowledge and provision.

units.notes: Clouds and fountains pair waters above and below. Established and strengthened express God's ordering.
units.summary: Wisdom was present as the LORD established the clouds and deep springs.
units.principle: God's wisdom orders resources people depend on every day.
units.insight: Ordinary provisions such as water can awaken gratitude for the Creator's care.
units.application: Give thanks for the water you use today and choose one way to use it carefully.

rel.note: God's founding of the earth and ordering of the waters likewise display His wisdom.

units.notes: The sea's limit is a boundary. Marking foundations pictures laying out a building.
units.summary: Wisdom was present as the LORD bounded the sea and marked the earth's foundations.
units.principle: The Creator brings order through wise limits.
units.insight: God's ordering of great forces can encourage trust where we feel small.
units.application: Honor one rightful limit in your use of a shared resource as an act of gratitude to God.

rel.note: The LORD's creating by wisdom is developed here into the portrait of Wisdom at His side.

units.notes: The rare word ’amon can be read as master craftsman, nursling, or faithful one. The NKJV follows the craftsman reading.
units.summary: Wisdom was beside the LORD as a master craftsman, His daily delight, rejoicing before Him.
units.principle: The work of creation is portrayed in the setting of delight between the LORD and Wisdom.
units.insight: Creation invites believers to give thanks for the joy and love of the Father and Son.
units.application: Read this verse with Hebrews 1:2 and Matthew 3:17 and thank the Father for His beloved Son.

rel.note: The people in whom Wisdom delights are the same people she calls directly.

units.notes: The inhabited world is the earth as a home. Sons of men means humanity, as in 8:4.
units.summary: Wisdom rejoices in God's world and delights in humanity.
units.principle: Wisdom calls people with delight in them.
units.insight: People who feel overlooked can hear the warmth of Christ's call in this portrait.
units.application: Thank Christ for His delight in people and give attentive care to someone easily overlooked.

rel.note: The father likewise calls the person who finds wisdom happy.

units.notes: Now therefore introduces the conclusion. Blessed names the well-being of those who keep Wisdom's ways.
units.summary: Blessed are those who listen to Wisdom and keep her ways.
units.principle: Wisdom's blessing belongs with listening that becomes a way of life.
units.insight: The person who hears Christ's instruction can begin by taking a concrete step of obedience.
units.application: Name one instruction from the chapter and practice it in a specific situation today.

rel.note: Heeding correction gains understanding, while rejecting instruction harms the learner.

units.notes: Instruction includes discipline and correction. Disdain can include neglecting what one hears.
units.summary: Hear instruction and take it seriously so that you grow wise.
units.principle: Teachability depends on giving instruction a response.
units.insight: A correction worth hearing can be considered patiently even when it stings.
units.application: Revisit one sound correction you have set aside and decide what action it calls for.

rel.note: The promise to those who seek diligently gives a reason to wait attentively.

units.notes: Watching at gates and waiting at doorposts picture daily, expectant attention.
units.summary: Blessed is the person who watches daily and listens for Wisdom.
units.principle: Persistent attention makes room to hear and receive wise instruction.
units.insight: Daily devotion can take a form that fits a person's responsibilities and season of life.
units.application: Choose a regular moment to listen to Christ in Scripture and respond to what you hear.

rel.note: Finding a wife is similarly associated with obtaining favor from the LORD.

units.notes: Whoever opens the invitation widely. Obtains favor recurs in 18:22, and finding also frames the question in 31:10.
units.summary: Whoever finds Wisdom finds life and obtains favor from the LORD.
units.principle: Life and the LORD's favor are found with Wisdom and fulfilled in Christ.
units.insight: A person can seek Christ Himself as the source of life, beyond seeking advice for a particular problem.
units.application: Come to Christ with one area where you need life and take the step of faithfulness He has made clear.

rel.note: A course can appear right to the traveler while its destination is death.

units.notes: Sins against can also carry the sense of missing Wisdom. Soul means the person's own life.
units.summary: Rejecting Wisdom harms one's own life and sets a course toward death.
units.principle: The end of a path reveals what choosing it amounts to.
units.insight: A serious warning can open a way to turn while there is still time.
units.application: Identify one refusal of wise instruction and turn toward Christ with a concrete act of obedience.

rel.note: Wisdom builds here as the wise woman builds up her house in that saying.

units.notes: Hewn pillars are cut and shaped supports. Seven pillars picture a substantial, well-prepared house.
units.summary: Wisdom builds a substantial house ready to receive her guests.
units.principle: Wisdom prepares a place of welcome before calling people in.
units.insight: Christ's invitation brings people into the community He builds.
units.application: Make room for a newcomer to learn alongside others in your congregation.

rel.note: Wisdom prepares her own meal, while Folly offers stolen water and secret bread.

units.notes: Slaughtered meat signals a feast. Wine was mixed before serving. A furnished table is fully set.
units.summary: Wisdom prepares a generous feast and sets the table herself.
units.principle: The giver bears the cost of what guests receive freely.
units.insight: At the Lord's Supper, believers can give thanks for Christ's sacrifice and what He has provided.
units.application: As you prepare to receive the Lord's Supper, take time to thank Christ for His sacrifice.

rel.note: Wisdom also takes a visible place by the paths and calls at the city gates.

units.notes: Maidens are the young women of Wisdom's household. The city's heights give her call a public hearing.
units.summary: Wisdom sends messengers and calls openly from the city heights.
units.principle: A generous invitation is meant to reach the people who need it.
units.insight: Those who carry Christ's invitation can do so plainly and warmly.
units.application: Share one clear invitation to hear or learn about Christ with someone you know.

rel.note: Folly echoes the invitation and addresses the same hearers, but offers a different meal and destination.

units.notes: The simple are uncommitted and easily led. Lacks understanding is literally lacks heart, meaning deficient judgment.
units.summary: Wisdom invites the uncommitted to turn in and learn.
units.principle: Recognizing our need makes us ready to receive wisdom.
units.insight: A person can come to Christ aware of their need and ready to learn.
units.application: Name one area where your judgment is unsettled and seek instruction before choosing a course.

rel.note: Wisdom freely offers food from her table, while Folly promises sweetness through theft and secrecy.

units.notes: Bread can mean food more generally. The mixed wine recalls the table Wisdom prepared in 9:2.
units.summary: Wisdom invites the hungry to receive the food and drink she has prepared.
units.principle: Wisdom's provision is offered to be received and taken in.
units.insight: A person who feels spiritually hungry can come to Christ and receive from Him.
units.application: Bring one spiritual need to Christ in prayer and attend to His instruction in Scripture.

rel.note: The bright and dark paths give context to Wisdom's call to walk in the way of understanding.

units.notes: Forsake means to leave behind. Going in the way of understanding pictures a continuing course.
units.summary: Leave foolishness and walk in understanding so that you may live.
units.principle: Receiving wisdom changes the way we walk.
units.insight: A change of course can begin with a specific habit a person is ready to leave.
units.application: Identify one practice that keeps you in foolishness and replace it with a step of obedience to Christ.

rel.note: The scoffer likewise dislikes correction and avoids people who might offer it.

units.notes: A scoffer treats correction with contempt. Harm can include a blemish or injury to the one who rebukes.
units.summary: Correcting a scoffer can bring insult or harm to the person who speaks.
units.principle: The response a correction receives depends in part on the hearer's disposition.
units.insight: Someone facing hostility can seek counsel about whether and how to continue the conversation.
units.application: Before correcting someone who has repeatedly mocked advice, consider the timing, setting, and likely response.

rel.note: The faithful wounds of a friend help explain why a wise person can value honest rebuke.

units.notes: Correct and rebuke translate the same verb here. The hearers respond in opposite ways.
units.summary: A scoffer resents correction, while a wise person values the one who offers it.
units.principle: Teachability shows in how a person responds to rebuke.
units.insight: A truthful correction may be worth receiving even when it is uncomfortable.
units.application: When you are corrected, ask one sincere question and consider the answer before defending yourself.

rel.note: The prologue likewise says that the wise hear and increase in learning.

units.notes: The first line literally says to give to a wise person. The parallel line makes clear that teaching is meant.
units.summary: The wise and righteous grow by receiving more instruction.
units.principle: Growing wiser includes remaining teachable.
units.insight: Experience gives a person more opportunities to learn from counsel.
units.application: Ask someone to teach you one thing in an area where you already have experience.

rel.note: The opening motto also makes fear of the LORD the beginning, there of knowledge.

units.notes: The Holy One is the LORD. The parallel lines join knowing Him to the fear of the LORD.
units.summary: Wisdom begins with the fear of the LORD, and understanding grows from knowing the Holy One.
units.principle: A right view of God gives right perspective to the rest of life.
units.insight: Seeing God's holiness can expose pride and draw a person toward humble trust.
units.application: Bring one decision before the Holy One in prayer and ask how reverence for Him should shape it.

rel.note: The father's instruction likewise tends toward length of days, years of life, and peace.

units.notes: By me identifies Wisdom as the speaker. Added years echo the language of 3:2.
units.summary: Wisdom generally helps preserve and lengthen life.
units.principle: Life is ordinarily served by the habits Wisdom teaches.
units.insight: An early death gives no grounds for blaming the person who died or those who grieve.
units.application: Put one piece of sound, life-preserving counsel into practice this week.

rel.note: The backslider is filled with his own ways, while the good person receives a different satisfaction.

units.notes: To bear is to carry a load. The singular address makes the consequence personal.
units.summary: You receive the benefit of wisdom and carry the cost of your own scoffing.
units.principle: Personal responsibility accompanies the invitation to become wise.
units.insight: A mentor can help someone face the part of a choice that is theirs to make.
units.application: Name one response to counsel that is yours to own and take the next responsible step.

rel.note: The earlier seductress is described with the same word for loudness.

units.notes: The foolish woman is Folly personified. Clamorous recalls the loud woman in 7:11.
units.summary: Folly is a loud hostess with no understanding to give.
units.principle: A confident voice still needs to be tested by what it offers.
units.insight: The volume or confidence of an invitation can make it seem weightier than it is.
units.application: Test one loud or confident appeal by asking what it teaches you to desire and do.

rel.note: Wisdom calls from the same kind of public place after preparing her feast and sending messengers.

units.notes: The seat can suggest a place of honor. The city heights recall the place of Wisdom's call in 9:3.
units.summary: Folly takes a prominent seat where her call can rival Wisdom's.
units.principle: Prominence tells us little about the worth of an offer.
units.insight: A familiar setting can lend credibility to an invitation that still needs examination.
units.application: Evaluate one prominent invitation by what it asks you to do and where that course leads.

rel.note: The counsel to keep from turning aside answers the diversion Folly seeks.

units.notes: Passersby are already going straight on their way. Folly calls to them from her seat.
units.summary: Folly calls to people who are already going straight and tries to turn them aside.
units.principle: Staying on a wise course takes continued attention.
units.insight: A person can prepare for interruptions even when a routine is going well.
units.application: Decide ahead of time how you will answer an invitation that would draw you away from a good commitment.

rel.note: Wisdom calls the same hearers, then invites them to leave foolishness and live.

units.notes: Folly echoes Wisdom's summons in 9:4. Lacks understanding describes the same vulnerable hearer.
units.summary: Folly copies Wisdom's call and appeals to the same hearers.
units.principle: Similar words can lead to very different ends.
units.insight: A familiar invitation can be examined by asking what response and result it seeks.
units.application: Compare two invitations that sound alike and identify where their commitments and outcomes differ.

rel.note: Bread gained by deceit tastes sweet at first and turns to gravel afterward.

units.notes: Stolen water evokes taking what belongs to another. Secret bread emphasizes concealment.
units.summary: Folly makes stolen pleasure attractive by promising sweetness and secrecy.
units.principle: Secrecy and immediate pleasure give no assurance that a choice is good.
units.insight: A desire that grows more appealing when it must be hidden deserves honest examination.
units.application: Name what a secret pleasure would take from another person and step away from the choice.

rel.note: The seductress's house likewise descends to Sheol and the chambers of death.

units.notes: The dead are the departed. Hell renders Sheol, the realm of the dead. Guests are those who answered her call.
units.summary: Folly hides from her guests that her house leads to death.
units.principle: An invitation must be judged by its destination.
units.insight: Someone already drawn into Folly's course can turn toward the life Christ offers.
units.application: Consider where a hidden choice is taking you and leave it for a course that leads toward life.

rel.note: The first line repeats the joy a wise son brings, and the second likewise shows folly's effect on a parent.

units.notes: The heading opens Solomon's collection of short sayings. Father and mother together represent the parents affected.
units.summary: A child's wisdom brings parents joy, and folly brings them grief.
units.principle: Our choices affect the people who love us.
units.insight: A child's harmful choices can grieve loving parents even when those parents have taught faithfully.
units.application: Consider one choice that affects your family and take a step that shows wisdom or repairs harm.

rel.note: The second line repeats that righteousness delivers from death, while the first limits the usefulness of riches.

units.notes: Treasures of wickedness are gains obtained by wrongdoing. Delivering from death contrasts the ends of the two ways.
units.summary: Dishonest gain cannot rescue a person from ruin, while righteousness leads away from death.
units.principle: Profit cannot do what upright conduct does for a life.
units.insight: People can surrender an ill-gotten advantage without treating it as their only source of security.
units.application: Reject an opportunity that depends on deception, even if it offers a substantial gain.

rel.note: The righteous and wicked are likewise contrasted in terms of satisfied and unsatisfied appetite.

units.notes: Soul can refer to the living person and appetite. The second line speaks of the wicked person's craving.
units.summary: The LORD cares for the righteous and opposes the cravings of the wicked.
units.principle: God's dealings distinguish upright living from wicked craving.
units.insight: A hungry believer deserves practical help and assurance of God's care.
units.application: Trust the LORD for your needs and share food or other practical help with someone who lacks it.

rel.note: The diligent have their desires supplied, while the lazy person's desire goes unmet.

units.notes: The hand stands for work. A slack hand works carelessly or neglects the work, while a diligent hand works steadily.
units.summary: Neglect tends toward poverty, while diligence tends toward gain.
units.principle: Steady work usually serves a person better than recurring neglect.
units.insight: Diligence can be encouraged alongside real support for those whose ability or opportunities are limited.
units.application: Identify a task within your ability that you have neglected and schedule time to do it well.

rel.note: The ant models gathering supplies during the available season.

units.notes: Summer and harvest refer to a limited season for gathering food. Sleeping here depicts missing the opportunity through neglect.
units.summary: Wisdom acts while the harvest is ready, while neglect wastes the opportunity.
units.principle: Diligence includes knowing when a task must be done.
units.insight: A responsibility with a narrow window is worth planning for ahead of time.
units.application: Put an approaching deadline on your calendar and complete one necessary step while the opportunity is open.

rel.note: The second line recurs beside the image of righteous speech as a well of life.

units.notes: Blessings rest on the head in the first image. The compact second line can also be read as the wicked mouth concealing violence.
units.summary: Blessing rests on the righteous, while violence marks the mouth of the wicked.
units.principle: The use of speech belongs to the larger moral course of a life.
