units.insight: Smooth speech should be weighed against the conduct and intentions it may conceal.
units.application: Examine a statement you plan to make and remove any wording that would disguise an intention to harm someone.

rel.note: The wise and fools likewise leave contrasting legacies of honor and shame.

units.notes: A name represents reputation and memory. Rot pictures decay.
units.summary: The righteous leave a memory that blesses, while the name of the wicked decays.
units.principle: Character shapes what a name leaves behind.
units.insight: Remembering a faithful person can encourage others to carry forward the good they did.
units.application: Tell someone about a good practice you learned from a faithful person and put it into use.

rel.note: The wise listen to counsel, while fools trust the rightness of their own way.

units.notes: Wise in heart describes inward wisdom. A prating fool is literally a fool of lips, a person given to chatter.
units.summary: The wise listen to instruction, while the fool talks his way toward a fall.
units.principle: Teachability shows in listening before speaking.
units.insight: A pause can make space to hear a correction that would otherwise be missed.
units.application: When you receive a correction, repeat it back accurately before offering your response.

rel.note: Blameless walking is again contrasted with a crooked course that ends in a fall.

units.notes: Integrity suggests wholeness. Perverting one's ways means twisting conduct toward deceit.
units.summary: Integrity allows a person to walk securely, while crooked conduct risks exposure.
units.principle: Openness gives a kind of security that concealment cannot provide.
units.insight: Someone who has been hiding a wrong can begin addressing it through honest disclosure and repair.
units.application: Correct one discrepancy between what you say publicly and what you do privately.

rel.note: The troublemaker likewise uses covert gestures as part of a pattern that sows discord.

units.notes: The wink is a covert signal in this context. The prating fool repeats the figure from 10:8.
units.summary: Malicious signals cause trouble, and foolish chatter brings a fall.
units.principle: Communication can cause harm through covert signals or careless words.
units.insight: Look at the purpose and pattern of a gesture before drawing conclusions about it.
units.application: Refuse a covert signal or private joke meant to deceive or humiliate someone.

rel.note: Wise instruction is likewise called a fountain of life that turns people from deadly snares.

units.notes: A well of life pictures a reliable source of refreshment. The second line repeats 10:6 and can also be read as concealing violence.
units.summary: Righteous speech gives life, while wicked speech is bound up with violence.
units.principle: The mouth can serve life or help violence do its work.
units.insight: A timely word of truth or encouragement can help someone keep going.
units.application: Offer one truthful word of guidance or encouragement to someone who needs it today.

rel.note: Covering a transgression seeks love, while repeating it divides close friends.

units.notes: Stirring up pictures keeping strife active. Covering means forgiving an offense and refusing to keep broadcasting it.
units.summary: Hatred keeps quarrels alive, while forgiving love refuses to keep reopening offenses.
units.principle: Love seeks peace by refusing to use another person's wrong as fuel for conflict.
units.insight: A person can forgive while seeking protection, accountability, and necessary help.
units.application: Stop repeating a grievance you can forgive, and address any continuing harm through the appropriate channels.

rel.note: The correction of fools there also uses the image of punishment for rejected wisdom.

units.notes: Devoid of understanding literally means lacking heart or judgment. The rod pictures painful discipline.
units.summary: Understanding brings wisdom to the lips, while a lack of judgment invites painful correction.
units.principle: Learning from wise words can spare a person harsher lessons.
units.insight: Correction can be offered firmly and with care for the person's growth.
units.application: Before repeating a mistake, ask someone with sound judgment what their experience can teach you.

rel.note: The fool's own mouth is likewise described as his destruction and snare.

units.notes: Storing up means putting something aside like treasure. Near describes destruction close at hand.
units.summary: The wise store knowledge, while a fool's careless words bring ruin near.
units.principle: Knowledge is worth retaining and using at the appropriate time.
units.insight: Taking time to learn can make a later answer more helpful and accurate.
units.application: Record one useful lesson and pause before speaking about something you have yet to understand.

rel.note: The fortified-city image returns with the qualification that the wall is high in the rich person's own esteem.

units.notes: A strong city is a fortified place. Destruction describes the ruin to which poverty can leave people exposed.
units.summary: Wealth can buffer setbacks, while poverty can make them harder to survive.
units.principle: Recognizing vulnerability gives reason to use resources responsibly and generously.
units.insight: A small setback can become a crisis for someone with no resources to absorb it.
units.application: Use some of the resources you can spare to help someone meet a cost that would otherwise overwhelm them.

rel.note: The wicked person's work is deceptive, while sowing righteousness yields a sure reward.

units.notes: Labor can refer to work or its wages. The wicked person's wages are pictured as the yield of a crop.
units.summary: The righteous use their earnings to serve life, while the wicked use theirs to feed sin.
units.principle: Earnings take on moral significance through the ends they serve.
units.insight: The use of income can reveal priorities that intentions alone do not make visible.
units.application: Review one recurring expense and redirect it if it supports something harmful.

rel.note: Disdaining instruction harms the person who refuses it, while heeding rebuke yields understanding.

units.notes: Keeping instruction means holding to discipline. The verb behind goes astray can also mean leading others astray.
units.summary: Keeping instruction leads toward life, while refusing correction leads astray.
units.principle: Correction helps preserve both our direction and the example we set.
units.insight: The response of a person with influence can shape whether others welcome correction.
units.application: Review one correction you resisted and identify a change that would help you and those who follow your example.

rel.note: The hater there likewise disguises inward deceit with speech.

units.notes: Hiding hatred uses the same covering word as 10:12. Slander spreads a damaging report.
units.summary: Lies can hide hatred, and slander spreads the harm of folly.
units.principle: Honest speech refuses both disguised malice and damaging rumor.
units.insight: A grievance can be named truthfully and addressed with the right person.
units.application: Take a grievance directly to an appropriate person and stop repeating it to people who cannot help.

rel.note: A person with knowledge likewise holds back words.

units.notes: Restraining the lips means keeping speech in check. Multitude emphasizes the increased occasions for careless words.
units.summary: The more we talk, the more opportunity there is to sin, so wisdom restrains speech.
units.principle: Wise restraint serves the right use of words.
units.insight: A short pause can protect another person from a remark that would be hard to take back.
units.application: Before adding a comment, ask whether it is true and whether it needs to be said now.

rel.note: A fitting word is likewise pictured through precious metals.

units.notes: Choice silver is refined silver. The comparison sets righteous speech beside the inner life of the wicked.
units.summary: The speech of the righteous has the worth of refined silver.
units.principle: The value of speech is connected to the heart that produces it.
units.insight: A truthful, well-weighed word can be more valuable to a hearer than a long explanation.
units.application: Offer one carefully weighed and truthful answer where a quick reaction would be easier.

rel.note: A wholesome tongue is likewise pictured as a tree of life.

units.notes: Feed uses the image of a shepherd pasturing a flock. Lack of wisdom is literally lack of heart or judgment.
units.summary: Righteous words nourish many, while fools perish for lack of judgment.
units.principle: Wise speech supplies what helps people live.
units.insight: Giving helpful counsel can be a quiet way of caring for people.
units.application: Share one piece of sound counsel that meets a specific need, and listen to how the person receives it.

rel.note: The warning against trusting riches helps distinguish the LORD's blessing from confidence in wealth.

units.notes: The second line can mean that the LORD adds no sorrow or that painful toil adds nothing to His blessing.
units.summary: The LORD gives true riches without the sorrow that grasping for gain brings.
units.principle: Receive provision as the LORD's gift and refuse the grief-producing pursuit of dishonest gain.
units.insight: A believer can receive God's provision gratefully while living with modest means or hardship.
units.application: Thank God for a concrete provision and turn down a shortcut to gain that would cost your integrity.

rel.note: Fools likewise mock at sin, in contrast with the favor found among the upright.

units.notes: Sport means play or laughter. The compressed second line implies that the discerning person delights in wisdom.
units.summary: Fools enjoy doing evil, while people of understanding take pleasure in wisdom.
units.principle: Our pleasures reveal and reinforce our moral direction.
units.insight: What people laugh about together can shape what they learn to tolerate.
units.application: Stop joining in one joke or pastime that makes harm entertaining and choose a better delight.

rel.note: The hope of the righteous leads to gladness, while the expectation of the wicked perishes.

units.notes: Fear here means dread of an outcome. The contrast pairs that dread with the righteous person's desire.
units.summary: The wicked face the outcome they dread, while the righteous can hope in what God gives.
units.principle: The two ways give different grounds for expectation.
units.insight: Unmet hopes can be brought to God without reading them as a verdict on a person's righteousness.
units.application: Name one desire before God and ask how righteousness should shape what you hope for.

rel.note: The wicked are overthrown, while the house of the righteous stands.

units.notes: The whirlwind pictures sudden disaster. An everlasting foundation pictures lasting stability.
units.summary: Disaster exposes the fragility of wickedness and the enduring foundation of righteousness.
units.principle: Security that lasts is deeper than what a crisis can take away.
units.insight: People who suffer loss deserve support without being judged by what the storm took from them.
units.application: Identify what you rely on in a crisis and take one step to strengthen an upright practice or relationship.

rel.note: A faithful messenger refreshes those who send him, the opposite of the irritation described here.

units.notes: Sour wine sets teeth on edge, and smoke irritates the eyes. The NKJV calls this person the lazy man.
units.summary: Laziness frustrates the people who depend on an assignment being done.
units.principle: Diligence includes being dependable for the people who entrust us with work.
units.insight: A person who cannot complete a task can communicate promptly so others can plan.
units.application: Complete an outstanding assignment or tell the person relying on you what is delaying it and when you can respond.

rel.note: Wisdom likewise associates her way with added years of life.

units.notes: Prolongs means adds. Fear of the LORD is a right view of God that leads away from evil.
units.summary: The fear of the LORD ordinarily preserves life, while wickedness tends to shorten it.
units.principle: Reverence for God directs people away from practices that destroy life.
units.insight: Grieving people deserve care without speculation about why a life ended early.
units.application: Turn from one destructive practice and take a step that shows reverence for God and care for life.

rel.note: The expectation of the wicked likewise perishes when they die.

units.notes: Hope is confident expectation. Perish describes the collapse of what the wicked count on.
units.summary: The hope of the righteous leads to gladness, while wicked expectations perish.
units.principle: Hope is only as lasting as what it rests on.
units.insight: A period of disappointment can coexist with a hope that rests in God.
units.application: Review one expectation and ask whether its fulfillment depends on an upright course or a compromising scheme.

rel.note: The LORD's name is also pictured as a strong tower where the righteous find safety.

units.notes: Strength can mean a stronghold or refuge. The way of the LORD is His ordering of life.
units.summary: The LORD's way is a refuge for the upright and ruin for those who practice evil.
units.principle: The same way of the LORD supports uprightness and opposes evil.
units.insight: An upright course can give steadiness even when following it is costly.
units.application: Choose one action that brings a difficult decision into line with what God asks of you.

rel.note: The upright dwell in the land, while the wicked are cut off and uprooted.

units.notes: Removed means shaken loose or uprooted. Earth can also be rendered land, recalling Israel's dwelling in the land.
units.summary: The righteous have lasting stability, while the wicked do not remain in the land.
units.principle: The lasting security of righteousness rests in God.
units.insight: Someone displaced by hardship can be cared for without treating that loss as a verdict on their conduct.
units.application: Support someone whose circumstances are unstable and practice integrity in a choice that affects your own security.

rel.note: The lips of the righteous also feed many, another image of speech that sustains.

units.notes: Brings forth pictures bearing fruit. Cutting out the perverse tongue continues the picture of removing what does harm.
units.summary: The righteous mouth bears wisdom, while the perverse tongue is cut off.
units.principle: The fruit of speech reflects the character that produces it.
units.insight: Wise speech grows through repeated habits of truth and care.
units.application: Choose one conversation in which your words can give sound direction, and speak with care.

rel.note: A fitting word spoken at the right time is likewise commended.

units.notes: Acceptable means fitting or welcome. The verb knows carries over into the second line.
units.summary: The righteous know what is fitting to say, while the wicked speak what is twisted.
units.principle: Wise speech fits both the truth and the occasion.
units.insight: A fitting word takes account of truth, timing, and the person who needs to hear it.
units.application: Before a difficult conversation, prepare one truthful sentence that fits the person's need and the moment.

rel.note: Unequal weights and dishonest scales are likewise condemned.

units.notes: Balance scales and stone weights measured goods. A false weight could cheat a buyer or seller.
units.summary: The LORD detests cheating in trade and delights in honest measures.
units.principle: Honest trade gives others the full value they were led to expect.
units.insight: Routine accuracy can be an act of faithfulness even where customers cannot check it.
units.application: Check one invoice, measurement, or product claim for accuracy and correct any discrepancy.

rel.note: Pride likewise precedes destruction, and a haughty spirit precedes a fall.

units.notes: Pride and shame are paired as events that arrive together. The humble recognize their limits.
units.summary: Pride brings shame, while humility makes room for wisdom.
units.principle: Teachability grows where people have a modest estimate of themselves.
units.insight: Admitting a limit can make a conversation more honest and productive.
units.application: Ask someone to challenge an assumption you are confident about and hear them out.

rel.note: Integrity also gives security, while crooked conduct invites exposure.

units.notes: Integrity is wholeness of character. Perversity here is crooked dealing that breaks trust.
units.summary: Integrity guides the upright, while crooked dealing destroys the unfaithful.
units.principle: Character can direct a choice before every consequence is visible.
units.insight: Clear commitments make it easier to act honestly under pressure.
units.application: Name the honest course in a difficult decision before weighing what you might gain from bending it.

rel.note: The second line is identical, while the first there names ill-gotten treasure.

units.notes: The day of wrath points to God's judgment, whether encountered in history or at death. The second line repeats 10:2.
units.summary: Riches cannot rescue a person in the day of wrath, while righteousness delivers from death.
units.principle: Uprightness matters where purchasing power cannot help.
units.insight: A person can take stock of whether money has become their ultimate refuge.
units.application: Set aside one advantage you would have to gain dishonestly and choose the upright course.

rel.note: The same straight-path image there emphasizes the LORD's guidance of those who acknowledge Him.

units.notes: Blameless describes sincere, whole conduct. Directing a way aright pictures making a path straight.
units.summary: Righteousness straightens the path, while wickedness trips up the one who practices it.
units.principle: The character of our conduct shapes the road we must walk.
units.insight: A hidden compromise may make future choices harder and can still be addressed early.
units.application: Remove one dishonest shortcut from a recurring decision before it creates further complications.

rel.note: A person's own sins likewise become the cords that catch him.

units.notes: The unfaithful are those who break trust. Lust means a strong craving and can include greed.
units.summary: Righteousness delivers the upright, while the unfaithful are caught by their own cravings.
units.principle: A desire pursued without integrity can become a trap.
units.insight: A craving can be named and addressed before it starts dictating decisions.
units.application: Identify a desire that has been tempting you to break trust and set one practical boundary around it.

rel.note: The expectation of the wicked likewise perishes, in contrast with the hope of the righteous.

units.notes: Expectation and hope refer to what the wicked count on. The second line reinforces the first.
units.summary: The expectations of the wicked perish when they die.
units.principle: A hope built on wicked gains has no lasting foundation.
units.insight: Facing the limits of what we can accumulate can help reorder what we hope for.
units.application: Review one ambition and ask what makes it worth pursuing beyond its immediate reward.

rel.note: The one who leads the upright astray falls into his own pit.

units.notes: In his place pictures one person entering the trouble from which another is rescued.
units.summary: The righteous can be delivered from trouble that instead overtakes the wicked.
units.principle: God's justice can reverse who bears the harm the wicked intended.
units.insight: People in trouble deserve care without pressure to predict how or when relief will come.
units.application: In a conflict, choose an upright response and seek help rather than trying to secure relief through retaliation.

rel.note: The wicked use words to lie in wait, while the mouth of the upright delivers.

units.notes: Hypocrite here can mean godless. The mouth stands for destructive speech.
units.summary: Destructive speech harms neighbors, while knowledge helps the righteous escape it.
units.principle: Truth and discernment provide a defense against manipulation.
units.insight: Careful verification can protect someone who is hearing a persuasive accusation or promise.
units.application: Check a damaging claim with a reliable source before acting on it or passing it along.

rel.note: People likewise rejoice under righteous authority and groan under wicked rule.

units.notes: Jubilation is a public shout of joy. The city represents people affected by others' conduct.
units.summary: A city welcomes the success of the righteous and feels relief when wickedness loses its power.
units.principle: Character shapes whether a person's success helps or harms the wider community.
units.insight: Communities can name relief at the end of oppression while treating people with dignity.
units.application: Use one resource or opportunity you have gained to help your neighbors.

rel.note: The preceding verse shows the city rejoicing or finding relief as it experiences the effects of both ways.

units.notes: The upright person's blessing includes the good they bring. The wicked mouth pictures destructive public speech.
units.summary: The upright build up a city, while wicked speech can tear it down.
units.principle: A community is strengthened or weakened by the conduct and words of its people.
units.insight: Small acts of truthful public speech can help repair trust after a dispute.
units.application: Correct a false report affecting your community or speak a specific truth that helps restore trust.

rel.note: Holding back words is also associated with understanding and discretion.

units.notes: Despising means treating a neighbor with contempt. Devoid of wisdom literally means lacking heart or judgment.
units.summary: Belittling a neighbor shows poor judgment, while understanding knows when to keep quiet.
units.principle: Restraint protects both a neighbor's dignity and the relationship.
units.insight: A real concern can be raised without voicing contempt for the person involved.
units.application: Replace one contemptuous remark with silence or a respectful statement of the actual concern.

rel.note: A talebearer likewise reveals secrets, prompting a warning about trusting such a person.

units.notes: A talebearer goes about spreading stories. A faithful spirit describes inward trustworthiness.
units.summary: Gossip betrays confidences, while a faithful person guards them.
units.principle: Trustworthiness includes knowing when information is ours to share.
units.insight: A confidence can be honored while getting appropriate help when someone is at risk.
units.application: Decline to pass along a private story and seek responsible help if it involves a safety concern.

rel.note: Plans fail without counsel and are established with many counselors.

units.notes: Counsel means direction or guidance. The people are a community or nation.
units.summary: A community needs sound guidance, and several wise counselors can improve safety.
units.principle: Wise counsel tests a plan before others bear its consequences.
units.insight: Leaders can make room for advisers who see a decision from different sides.
units.application: Before a decision affecting others, ask more than one trustworthy adviser to identify what you may have missed.

rel.note: The father shows how a pledge traps the guarantor and urges an honest release.

units.notes: A surety guarantees another person's debt. The warning recalls 6:1–5.
units.summary: Guaranteeing a stranger's debt risks loss, while refusing the pledge avoids that exposure.
units.principle: Generosity can be practiced without assuming another person's debt.
units.insight: Someone under pressure to cosign can respond with clear limits and consider affordable help.
units.application: Avoid cosigning and, if you choose to help, give what you can afford to lose.

rel.note: A good name and favor are preferred to riches.

units.notes: Gracious describes kindness of character. The same verb for retaining applies to honor and riches.
units.summary: Gracious character holds honor, while ruthlessness holds on to riches.
units.principle: Gracious character earns a kind of honor that force cannot secure.
units.insight: Kindness has a lasting worth even where aggressive conduct wins material advantage.
units.application: Choose a gracious response in a situation where forcefulness might get you an immediate advantage.

rel.note: The one who refreshes others also receives refreshment.

units.notes: Merciful describes kindness and loyal love. Soul and flesh point to the person's own well-being.
units.summary: Mercy benefits the one who shows it, while cruelty brings trouble back on the cruel person.
units.principle: Our treatment of others has consequences for our own lives.
units.insight: Practicing kindness can change the tone of a strained relationship.
units.application: Replace one harsh response with a specific act of kindness that still addresses the issue honestly.

rel.note: Sowing iniquity yields sorrow, the opposite of the harvest of righteousness.

units.notes: The words for deceit and reward sound similar in Hebrew. Sowing pictures work done before its fruit appears.
units.summary: Deceptive gain disappoints, while sowing righteousness yields a sure reward.
units.principle: The fruit of righteousness has greater staying power than deceptive gain.
units.insight: Doing right can be worth continuing when results are slow to appear.
units.application: Keep one upright practice that has yet to show results and refuse a deceptive shortcut.

rel.note: The labor of the righteous serves life, while the wicked use their gain to serve sin.

units.notes: Pursuing evil pictures an eager chase. Life is the destination of righteousness.
units.summary: Righteousness leads to life, while pursuing evil leads toward death.
units.principle: A course should be weighed by where it leads.
units.insight: A desire can be judged by the destination it is drawing someone toward.
units.application: Trace one pursuit to its likely end and leave it if it leads away from life.

rel.note: The same pairing of abomination and delight is used for dishonest and honest measures.

units.notes: Perverse means inwardly crooked. Blameless ways describe sincere and upright conduct.
units.summary: The LORD detests a crooked heart and delights in upright ways.
units.principle: The heart and the way of life belong together before God.
units.insight: God takes pleasure in sincere choices that may go unnoticed by others.
units.application: Examine one outwardly correct action for a crooked motive and choose a sincere way to do it.

rel.note: The children of a person who walks with integrity are likewise described as blessed.

units.notes: Join forces is literally hand to hand. Some translations take the phrase as an assurance of certainty.
units.summary: Wrongdoing cannot escape justice through alliances, and uprightness can benefit the next generation.
units.principle: A person's course has consequences that can reach beyond their own lifetime.
units.insight: Families can pass on sound practices while trusting God with outcomes beyond their control.
units.application: Pass on one upright practice to someone younger and refuse to join a group that covers wrongdoing.

rel.note: Charm and beauty are placed beside the lasting worth of fearing the LORD.

units.notes: A gold nose ring was an ornament. The swine makes the comparison deliberately jarring. Discretion means sound moral judgment.
units.summary: Outward beauty without discretion is like a gold ring out of place.
units.principle: Good judgment gives outward gifts a fitting place.
units.insight: People can be encouraged to develop judgment and character beyond what others notice first.
units.application: Give attention to one choice that develops discretion instead of relying on appearance or charm to carry it.

rel.note: Righteous hope leads to gladness, while the expectation of the wicked perishes.

units.notes: Desire and expectation describe what the two groups reach for or look toward. Wrath names the outcome of the wicked course.
units.summary: Righteous desire is directed toward good, while the wicked course ends in wrath.
units.principle: The character of a pursuit matters to its outcome.
units.insight: A hope can be examined by asking what it is training a person to desire.
units.application: Name one desire and ask whether pursuing it would serve what is good for others as well as yourself.

rel.note: The generous person is blessed for sharing bread with the poor.

units.notes: Scattering evokes sowing or giving freely. Withholding more than is right includes keeping what should be given or paid.
units.summary: Generosity can lead to increase, while wrongful withholding can lead to want.
units.principle: Holding resources too tightly can undermine the good they could do.
units.insight: A person can give freely without calculating what they expect to get back.
units.application: Meet one obligation or give something you can spare without expecting repayment.

rel.note: The person who shows mercy also does good to himself.

units.notes: Generous soul literally means a person of blessing. Watering pictures refreshing others.
units.summary: Those who refresh others often receive refreshment themselves.
units.principle: Generosity contributes to the well-being of giver and recipient.
units.insight: A person can offer encouragement, time, or material help according to their means.
units.application: Offer one practical form of refreshment to someone who could use it today.

rel.note: The LORD's judgment of unequal measures gives another example of accountability in trade.

units.notes: Withholding grain pictures keeping needed supplies off the market. Selling releases them to people who need them.
units.summary: People condemn hoarding needed supplies and bless those who make them available.
units.principle: Control of necessities creates an opportunity to serve or exploit others.
units.insight: A fair sale can serve neighbors in need as well as support the seller.
units.application: When people need something you control, make it available on fair terms where you can.

rel.note: The pit and stone images likewise show intended harm returning on the one who sets it in motion.

units.notes: Earnestly seeking pictures a deliberate search. The evil sought comes back upon the seeker.
units.summary: Seeking good tends toward favor, while pursuing evil brings trouble back on the seeker.
units.principle: What we pursue can return to us in ways we did not expect.
units.insight: A change in what someone deliberately seeks can change what they contribute to a relationship.
units.application: Choose one active way to seek another person's good where resentment has been directing your attention.

rel.note: Riches can take wings and fly away, showing why they make an unstable refuge.

units.notes: Trusting riches means depending on them for security. Green foliage pictures living growth.
units.summary: Trusting riches leads to a fall, while the righteous are pictured flourishing like foliage.
units.principle: Money can be used wisely while ultimate confidence rests in God.
units.insight: Financial loss can expose misplaced trust, and people facing it deserve care.
units.application: Name one decision that shows where your security rests and use your resources in a way consistent with trust in God.

rel.note: Greed for gain likewise brings trouble on one's own household.

units.notes: Inheriting wind pictures receiving nothing substantial. Wise of heart describes inward judgment.
units.summary: Troubling one's household can leave a person empty-handed and dependent on others.
units.principle: Household stability depends in part on how its members use their influence and resources.
units.insight: Repairing a destructive pattern at home can preserve good that has taken years to build.
units.application: Change one practice that creates needless harm or waste in your household.

rel.note: Wisdom is likewise a tree of life, and that earlier passage develops the image's connection to Christ.

units.notes: Fruit is the result of a life. Wins souls literally means takes lives or people, an expression that can mean killing elsewhere and whose precise sense here is debated.
units.summary: A righteous life bears life-giving fruit, and winning people calls for wisdom.
units.principle: The fruit of righteous conduct can sustain people beyond the one who produces it.
units.insight: A person's patient example and wise words can draw others toward the life Christ gives.
units.application: Offer one life-giving act or word to someone and look for a natural opportunity to point them toward Christ.

rel.note: The earlier saying likewise affirms that the wicked will not escape punishment.

units.notes: Recompensed means repaid. Peter quotes the Greek form in 1 Peter 4:18, which says scarcely saved where Proverbs speaks of repayment on earth.
units.summary: If even the righteous are repaid in this life, the ungodly have all the more reason to reckon with judgment.
units.principle: God's justice gives every person reason to take their conduct seriously.
units.insight: Hardship should not be used to assign blame, but the prospect of God's judgment calls for humility.
units.application: Examine one practice you would hesitate to bring before God and take a step of repentance where needed.

rel.note: Heeding rebuke gains understanding, while rejecting instruction harms the learner.

units.notes: Instruction includes discipline and correction. Stupid pictures the dullness of refusing to learn.
units.summary: Loving knowledge means welcoming the correction that helps us learn.
units.principle: Teachability depends on how we respond when corrected.
units.insight: A person can face a mistake without being reduced to it.
units.application: Ask a trusted person for one specific correction and consider it before defending yourself.

rel.note: The LORD likewise delights in upright conduct and detests inward crookedness.

units.notes: Favor is the LORD's goodwill. Wicked intentions include plans that may remain hidden from people.
units.summary: The LORD favors goodness and condemns deliberate schemes to harm.
units.principle: God judges what people intend as well as what they do.
units.insight: A hidden motive is worth examining even when the outward choice looks acceptable.
units.application: Examine one plan for a harmful motive and revise it before acting.

rel.note: The righteous have an enduring foundation, while the wicked are swept away.

units.notes: Established means made firm. The root pictures the stability of a tree anchored in the ground.
units.summary: Wickedness gives no lasting footing, while righteousness has a root that holds.
units.principle: Lasting stability grows from the character of the life it supports.
units.insight: A person shaken by trouble can still be deeply rooted in God's ways.
units.application: Strengthen one upright habit that can steady you when circumstances change.

rel.note: The later portrait develops the qualities of the woman of strength and worth.

units.notes: The published study notes that excellent wife and virtuous wife in 31:10 render the same Hebrew phrase. A crown signifies honor, while rottenness pictures decay from within.
units.summary: A wife of strength and worth honors her husband, while shame eats away at the marriage.
units.principle: Character within a marriage has lasting effects on the other spouse.
units.insight: Both spouses can examine how their conduct builds up or injures the person closest to them.
units.application: If married, name one strength you appreciate in your spouse and change one behavior that undermines trust.

rel.note: That saying also examines the course set by people's plans.

units.notes: Right can mean just or fair. Counsel is the advice the wicked put forward.
units.summary: The righteous plan justly, while the wicked give deceptive counsel.
units.principle: Fair action begins with fair intentions.
units.insight: A persuasive recommendation can be weighed by whose interests it serves.
units.application: Review a recommendation you are about to give and disclose any interest that could distort it.

rel.note: Destructive speech harms a neighbor, while knowledge provides a way of escape.

units.notes: Lying in wait for blood pictures an ambush. The mouth stands for words used to harm or rescue.
units.summary: Wicked words set an ambush, while upright words can rescue.
units.principle: Words have consequences for the safety of other people.
units.insight: Speaking truth for someone at risk can be an act of protection.
units.application: Correct a false claim that puts someone at risk, using an appropriate channel.

rel.note: The house of the wicked falls, while the dwelling of the upright flourishes.

units.notes: House includes the household, beyond the building itself. Standing pictures endurance.
units.summary: The wicked are overthrown, while the household of the righteous stands.
units.principle: The foundation of a household matters more than appearances of strength.
units.insight: A household in trouble deserves support without assumptions about its character.
units.application: Practice one dependable act of integrity that strengthens your household.

rel.note: Mercy and truth likewise lead toward favor and good esteem.

units.notes: Wisdom includes sound judgment in living. A perverse heart is inwardly crooked.
units.summary: Sound judgment earns esteem, while a crooked heart brings contempt.
units.principle: Honor is shaped over time by the judgment a person practices.
units.insight: A good reputation can grow through repeated wise conduct.
units.application: Handle one ordinary responsibility with the sound judgment you would want others to learn from.

rel.note: This saying likewise contrasts apparent wealth or poverty with actual resources.

units.notes: Being slighted means having little public esteem. Lacking bread exposes the cost of self-importance.
units.summary: Modest means with real provision are better than a show of importance without bread.
units.principle: Substance matters more than the appearance of status.
units.insight: A person can speak honestly about need without giving up dignity.
units.application: Reduce one expense aimed at keeping up appearances and put the resources toward a genuine need.

rel.note: The owner is likewise urged to know the condition of the flocks and attend to them.

units.notes: Regarding an animal's life means attending to its needs. Tender mercies highlights the irony of kindness that is cruel.
units.summary: The righteous care for their animals, while even the wicked person's supposed kindness can be cruel.
units.principle: Kindness is measured in part by what the dependent actually receives.
units.insight: Care for a dependent creature reveals habits that other people may rarely see.
units.application: Check the food, water, rest, or shelter of an animal entrusted to you and meet a need you find.

rel.note: Tilling the land and pursuing worthless things are contrasted again, with bread and poverty as outcomes.

units.notes: Tilling one's land pictures steady ordinary work. Frivolity can refer to worthless pursuits or companions.
units.summary: Steady work tends to provide bread, while chasing empty pursuits shows poor judgment.
units.principle: Diligence invests effort in work that can meet real needs.
units.insight: Someone whose work is limited by circumstances can still be helped to identify a realistic next step.
units.application: Replace time spent on one empty shortcut with a concrete step in useful work.

rel.note: The fruit of the righteous is pictured there as life-giving to others.

units.notes: Catch can refer to plunder gained through a trap, though the Hebrew is difficult. Root recalls 12:3.
units.summary: The wicked covet illicit gain, while the righteous bear fruit from a sound root.
units.principle: Lasting fruit comes from what a life is rooted in.
units.insight: Seeing dishonest gain can tempt people to undervalue slow, upright growth.
units.application: Refuse one shortcut patterned after another person's dishonesty and continue an upright practice instead.

rel.note: The fool's mouth is likewise described as a snare to the person speaking.

units.notes: Transgression of the lips means wrongdoing in speech. The snare pictures a trap made by one's own words.
units.summary: Wrongdoing in speech can trap a person, while upright conduct helps a person escape trouble.
units.principle: Speech can either complicate a crisis or help resolve it.
units.insight: A person caught in a lie can begin repair by telling the truth clearly.
units.application: Correct a misleading statement before you have to invent another to sustain it.

rel.note: A person is likewise satisfied by the fruit of the mouth.

units.notes: Fruit of the mouth means the results of speech. The hands represent what a person does.
units.summary: Good words bear fruit, and people receive the results of their actions.
units.principle: Both speech and work produce consequences worth considering.
units.insight: A truthful word and a helpful act can reinforce each other.
units.application: Pair one encouraging or truthful word with a helpful action that follows through on it.

rel.note: Being wise in one's own eyes likewise leaves a person resistant to wisdom.

units.notes: Right in his own eyes means relying on one's own assessment. The folly lies in refusing to question it.
units.summary: The fool assumes his course is right, while the wise heed counsel.
units.principle: Wisdom invites informed scrutiny of one's own judgment.
units.insight: A person can reconsider a confident judgment without treating it as a humiliation.
units.application: Ask a trustworthy person what you may be overlooking before acting on a firm opinion.

rel.note: Discretion slows anger, and overlooking a transgression is commended.

units.notes: At once pictures an immediate reaction. Covering shame here means letting a personal insult pass without escalating it.
units.summary: A fool displays anger immediately, while a prudent person can let a slight pass.
units.principle: A person can choose a proportionate response to an offense.
units.insight: Restraint can help with a personal insult, and serious or continuing harm can still be addressed.
units.application: Pause after a slight and decide whether silence or a calm private response would serve the situation.

rel.note: The true witness delivers lives, while the deceitful witness speaks lies.

units.notes: The contrast likely has a testimony setting. Declaring righteousness means bringing what is right into view.
units.summary: A truthful witness helps justice, while a false witness deals in deceit.
units.principle: Justice depends on honest accounts of what happened.
units.insight: Speaking only to what one knows can protect someone whose standing is at risk.
units.application: Distinguish what you saw from what you inferred before reporting a disputed event.

rel.note: A wholesome tongue gives life, while perverseness in speech breaks the spirit.

units.notes: Sword piercings picture the wounds caused by rash speech. Promotes health describes healing.
units.summary: Rash words wound like a sword, while wise words bring healing.
units.principle: Wisdom considers what words will do to the person who hears them.
units.insight: Someone hurt by cutting speech may need a specific apology and time to recover.
units.application: Replace a cutting criticism with a truthful, specific statement that helps the other person improve.

rel.note: The false witness perishes, while the second line contrasts speech that endures.

units.notes: Established means made firm. For a moment contrasts a brief advantage with lasting truth.
units.summary: Truthful speech endures, while a lie offers only a momentary advantage.
units.principle: Reliability rests on truth that can stand over time.
units.insight: Even if a lie remains concealed for some time, a person can begin repair by telling the truth.
units.application: Correct a false account now rather than relying on its temporary advantage.

rel.note: The troublemaker likewise devises evil from the heart and sows discord.

units.notes: Devising evil involves planning harm. Counselors of peace actively advise or plan for peace.
units.summary: Those who plot harm harbor deceit, while those who counsel peace find joy.
units.principle: The aims of our plans shape the life they produce.
units.insight: Peacemaking can be active work that begins with sound counsel.
units.application: Offer one honest proposal that could reduce a conflict without ignoring the issue.

rel.note: The righteous have lasting stability, while the wicked do not remain.

units.notes: Grave trouble is serious harm. Being filled with evil pictures trouble crowding the wicked person's life.
units.summary: The righteous have lasting security, while wickedness fills a life with trouble.
units.principle: God's keeping and the end of a person's course are deeper than any single circumstance.
units.insight: Severe suffering gives no grounds for accusing someone of wrongdoing.
units.application: Offer practical help to someone facing disaster and resist drawing conclusions about their character.

rel.note: The LORD likewise detests dishonest measures and delights in fair ones.

units.notes: Abomination expresses what the LORD detests. Dealing truthfully includes faithful conduct as well as words.
units.summary: The LORD detests lying and delights in trustworthy conduct.
units.principle: Integrity joins honest words to dependable actions.
units.insight: A truthful statement gains credibility when the speaker follows through faithfully.
units.application: Correct one inaccurate statement and follow through on a commitment connected with it.

rel.note: The wise store knowledge, while the mouth of the foolish brings ruin near.

units.notes: Concealing knowledge here means holding it until it is useful. Proclaiming pictures broadcasting what is in the heart.
units.summary: The prudent hold knowledge for the right moment, while fools broadcast folly.
units.principle: Discretion governs when and why knowledge is shared.
units.insight: Keeping quiet for a time can preserve the usefulness of what someone knows.
units.application: Before displaying something you know, ask whether it would help to share it now.

rel.note: The ant models the initiative and foresight that the diligent hand practices.

units.notes: The hand represents work. Forced labor pictures work performed under compulsion or tribute.
units.summary: Diligence tends toward responsibility, while laziness can bring work under compulsion.
units.principle: Self-discipline helps people carry responsibilities with greater freedom.
units.insight: Someone with genuine limitations deserves support suited to their circumstances.
units.application: Complete one duty within your ability without waiting for someone else to enforce it.

rel.note: A word spoken at the right time is likewise commended for its goodness.

units.notes: Depression in the NKJV describes heaviness of heart. A good word is a fitting word of encouragement, comfort, or hope.
units.summary: Anxiety weighs down the heart, and a good word can lift it.
units.principle: Words of comfort can be a real part of caring for someone under strain.
units.insight: Listen to the burden before offering encouragement, and make room for other forms of care.
units.application: Send a specific word of encouragement to someone carrying a burden and offer to listen.

rel.note: Walking with the wise brings wisdom, while companionship with fools brings harm.

units.notes: The first line is difficult. The NKJV reads it as choosing friends carefully. Some translations read it as giving guidance to a neighbor.
units.summary: Choose companions carefully because the way of the wicked can lead people astray.
units.principle: Companionship influences direction over time.
units.insight: A trustworthy friend can help someone see where a choice is taking them.
units.application: Spend time with someone who encourages an upright course, and reconsider a pattern of company that draws you away from it.

rel.note: The lazy man likewise begins an easy action and fails to carry it through.

units.notes: Roasting turns a catch into food. The rare Hebrew verb is rendered roast in the NKJV.
units.summary: Diligence finishes what laziness leaves unusable.
units.principle: Follow-through turns effort into something that can serve a purpose.
units.insight: An unfinished task may need only one defined step to make the earlier work useful.
units.application: Choose one useful task you have already started and complete the next step needed to make it usable.

rel.note: Righteousness likewise leads to life, while pursuing evil leads to death.

units.notes: The compact Hebrew of the second line is debated. The NKJV reads it as no death, which can suggest life beyond death.
units.summary: The way of righteousness leads to life.
units.principle: The value of a course is seen in where it ultimately leads.
units.insight: The life God gives can sustain hope even in the face of mortality.
units.application: Name one choice that leads toward the life God gives and take that step today.

rel.note: The scoffer resists rebuke, while a wise person receives it and grows.

units.notes: Instruction includes a father's training and correction. Rebuke names a fault plainly.
units.summary: The wise son listens to instruction, while the scoffer refuses rebuke.
units.principle: Teachability shows in the willingness to hear correction.
units.insight: A person who has rejected counsel before can still begin to listen.
units.application: Ask a trusted person to name one thing you could improve and listen before responding.

rel.note: Good speech likewise produces fruit that benefits the speaker.

units.notes: Fruit pictures what words produce. The unfaithful are those who break trust.
units.summary: Good words bear good fruit, while the unfaithful feed on violence.
units.principle: What we feed and what we speak shape the fruit we receive.
units.insight: Truthful, constructive words can help rebuild trust in a strained relationship.
units.application: Choose one honest, constructive word in a conversation that has grown hostile.

rel.note: Guarding the mouth and tongue likewise keeps a person from troubles.

units.notes: Guarding the mouth pictures keeping watch over what goes out. Opening the lips wide pictures unchecked speech.
units.summary: Guarding speech protects life, while reckless words can bring ruin.
units.principle: Speech deserves deliberate restraint because of what it can set in motion.
units.insight: A moment of silence can prevent a lasting injury.
units.application: Pause before making a promise or repeating a report you have not checked.

rel.note: The ant illustrates the initiative the lazy man lacks.

units.notes: The NKJV says lazy man. Made rich evokes being well fed or satisfied.
units.summary: Craving alone accomplishes little, while diligent effort tends toward satisfaction.
units.principle: Desire becomes productive when joined to steady work.
units.insight: A person facing real limitations may need support and a manageable next step.
units.application: Choose one goal within reach and put a specific period of work toward it today.

rel.note: The LORD likewise detests lying and delights in faithful conduct.

units.notes: Loathsome carries the image of an offensive smell. Shame is the disgrace that accompanies wicked conduct.
units.summary: The righteous hate lies, while wicked conduct brings offense and shame.
units.principle: Truthfulness grows from a settled refusal to approve falsehood.
units.insight: An honest correction of a false story can begin to restore trust.
units.application: Correct a false claim you have repeated and tell the people who heard it.

rel.note: Righteousness straightens the blameless person's way, while the wicked fall by their own wickedness.

units.notes: Blameless describes integrity of conduct. Guarding pictures a watchman, and overthrowing pictures being brought down.
units.summary: Righteousness guards an upright life, while wickedness brings down the sinner.
units.principle: Character can protect a life or undermine it from within.
units.insight: A small dishonest habit can be addressed before it gains power over later choices.
units.application: Remove one recurring compromise that is making an upright course harder to keep.

rel.note: A show of honor likewise conceals the lack of basic provision.

units.notes: Making oneself rich or poor can describe the way a person presents themselves.
units.summary: Appearances can reverse the truth about who has wealth and who lacks it.
units.principle: Financial appearance is a poor measure of actual resources.
units.insight: A person can live within their means without giving an account of their status to everyone.
units.application: Compare one status-driven expense with what your resources can actually support.

rel.note: Wealth can act like a defensive wall, though that image is qualified by the rich person's own estimate.

units.notes: Ransom is payment that can secure release. The second line is debated and likely means the poor person hears no such threat.
units.summary: Wealth can pay a ransom and can also attract the threat that demands it.
units.principle: Wealth changes the dangers a person faces as well as the means available to respond.
units.insight: Money can be useful while bringing pressures that are easy to overlook.
units.application: Consider one vulnerability created by publicizing what you own and choose a prudent limit.

rel.note: The wicked person's lamp likewise goes out, and evil offers no lasting prospect.

units.notes: Light pictures life and well-being. An extinguished household lamp pictures life or continuity coming to an end.
units.summary: The righteous are pictured with a joyful light, while the lamp of the wicked goes out.
units.principle: The two ways differ in what endures.
units.insight: Hope can remain even when a righteous person's circumstances grow difficult.
units.application: Give time to one upright practice that can bring good beyond an immediate advantage.

rel.note: Pride brings shame, while wisdom is found with the humble.

units.notes: The NKJV reads pride. The Book Brief draws out the related posture of presumption, including overconfidence in one's own judgment.
units.summary: Pride breeds strife, while wisdom belongs with those who receive counsel.
units.principle: Humility makes room for counsel and a more peaceable response.
units.insight: A conflict can change when someone admits that their own account may be incomplete.
units.application: Ask a trusted adviser what you are presuming in a disagreement, then revisit one assumption.

rel.note: A faithful person abounds with blessings, while haste to get rich brings consequences.

units.notes: The first line evokes wealth gained from something empty or insubstantial. Gathering by labor pictures steady accumulation by hand.
units.summary: Dishonest gain tends to shrink, while steady labor tends to build resources.
units.principle: How gain is acquired affects how well it can endure.
units.insight: Gradual progress can be easier to value when people have realistic expectations about time.
units.application: Refuse one questionable shortcut and put the effort into a legitimate source of income or savings.

rel.note: The earlier tree-of-life saying develops Wisdom's life-giving fruit and the image's connection to Christ.

units.notes: Deferred means drawn out or prolonged. The tree of life pictures renewed vitality when the longing is fulfilled.
units.summary: Prolonged waiting can make the heart sick, while fulfilled longing brings renewal.
units.principle: Wisdom takes both the pain of waiting and the joy of fulfillment seriously.
units.insight: A person worn down by waiting needs compassion and companionship. Christ gives hope even while a particular longing remains unmet.
units.application: Listen to someone who has been waiting a long time and offer specific support without predicting the outcome.

rel.note: Keeping the commandment preserves life, while despising one's ways leads toward death.

units.notes: The word parallels the commandment. Fearing the commandment means taking it with the reverence due its giver.
units.summary: Despising instruction leads toward ruin, while reverently heeding it brings reward.
units.principle: Reverence becomes visible in how we respond to God's instruction.
units.insight: Someone who has ignored a command can begin by giving it honest attention and changing course.
units.application: Read a command you have been putting aside and act on one concrete implication.

rel.note: The same fountain and snares language there describes the fear of the LORD.

units.notes: Law here means teaching. A fountain supplies life, while snares are hidden traps.
units.summary: Wise instruction gives life by turning people away from deadly traps.
units.principle: The guidance of the wise serves life by changing the route a person takes.
units.insight: Good counsel can name a danger someone has yet to recognize.
units.application: Act on one piece of wise counsel that identifies a hazard in your present course.

rel.note: Loyal love and faithfulness likewise tend toward favor and good esteem.

units.notes: Good understanding is practical insight. The unfaithful are people who act treacherously.
units.summary: Good judgment wins favor, while treachery makes the road hard.
units.principle: The way people treat others helps shape the road they have to travel.
units.insight: Restoring trust usually requires steady, dependable conduct over time.
units.application: Keep a promise that another person is depending on and address any obstacle honestly.

rel.note: The prudent person considers their steps, while the simple believe every word.

units.notes: Prudence is practical good sense. Laying open folly pictures spreading it out for others to see.
units.summary: The prudent act on knowledge, while fools put their folly on display.
units.principle: Sound judgment seeks knowledge before deciding.
units.insight: A pause to gather facts can prevent a public mistake.
units.application: Verify one important fact before acting on a claim that seems convincing.

rel.note: A faithful messenger likewise refreshes those who sent him.

units.notes: A messenger carries another person's words. Health here means healing or restoration.
units.summary: An unreliable messenger falls into trouble, while a faithful envoy brings healing.
units.principle: Trustworthy messengers serve the people who depend on the message.
units.insight: Accurate communication can lower the temperature of a dispute.
units.application: Before relaying a sensitive message, check that you have preserved its meaning and tone.

rel.note: A wise person receives rebuke and grows by instruction.

units.notes: Disdaining correction means neglecting or rejecting training. Regarding rebuke means taking it to heart.
units.summary: Ignoring correction can bring loss and shame, while heeding it leads toward honor.
units.principle: A rebuke can protect against losses when it is received in time.
units.insight: A setback may offer a chance to consider counsel without assuming every loss came from a fault.
units.application: Revisit one warning you dismissed and make a specific change if it was sound.

rel.note: The earlier saying likewise depicts the renewal that comes when a desire is fulfilled.

units.notes: Sweetness pictures the inward satisfaction of fulfilled desire. Abomination expresses the fool's revulsion at turning from evil.
units.summary: Fulfilled longing is sweet, yet fools hate turning from evil.
units.principle: Good desires call for a willingness to turn from what prevents their fulfillment.
units.insight: The appeal of an old practice can survive even when a person sees the good of leaving it.
units.application: Name one good you want and leave one practice that keeps you from pursuing it wisely.

rel.note: The sharpening image likewise shows one person shaping another through close interaction.

units.notes: Walking with someone means sharing their company and course. Companion denotes sustained association.
units.summary: Regular company with the wise fosters wisdom, while companionship with fools brings harm.
units.principle: The company we keep helps form the course we take.
units.insight: A person can care about others and still choose whose example will shape their habits.
units.application: Spend regular time with someone whose conduct you want to learn from.

rel.note: Seeking evil brings trouble back on the seeker, while seeking good tends toward favor.

units.notes: Evil here includes trouble or disaster. The verse pictures it pursuing sinners.
units.summary: Trouble pursues the wicked, while the righteous are repaid with good.
units.principle: Our chosen course has consequences that may catch up with us over time.
units.insight: A person can stay with an upright course even when its good is slow to appear.
units.application: Stop one practice that repeatedly brings trouble and choose an upright replacement.

rel.note: Wealth gathered by exploitative lending is described as passing to someone who shows pity to the poor.

units.notes: Inheritance often meant family land passed down. Children's children extends the view to grandchildren.
units.summary: Good stewardship looks beyond one generation, while sinful gain can pass out of its owner's hands.
units.principle: Stewardship considers how today's use of resources will affect those who come after us.
units.insight: A legacy can include sound practices and faithful provision even when resources are modest.
units.application: Identify one resource or practice you can preserve and pass on for the good of a later generation.

rel.note: The LORD opposes those who exploit the poor or deny them justice.

units.notes: Fallow ground is tillable farmland. The compressed second line associates the loss with lack of justice.
units.summary: Injustice can waste the food and livelihood a poor person's land could provide.
units.principle: Justice includes protecting people's ability to benefit from their labor.
units.insight: Listen to what has prevented someone from keeping the fruit of their work before judging their situation.
units.application: Identify one unfair practice that deprives people of their earnings or produce and take a fairer course where you have influence.

rel.note: The LORD's correction comes from the love of a father who delights in his child.

units.notes: The rod was a tool of correction in the ancient household. Promptly can also convey diligent or early attention.
units.summary: Loving parents take responsibility for timely, consistent correction.
units.principle: Discipline serves a child's growth through patient, consistent guidance.
units.insight: A parent who is angry can regain composure before addressing the child's conduct and follow correction with reassurance and repair.
units.application: Set a clear expectation, explain it calmly, and use a proportionate, safe consequence if it is broken.

rel.note: The LORD's care for the righteous and opposition to wicked craving give another perspective on the contrast.

units.notes: Soul here includes appetite or the whole person. The stomach pictures bodily hunger.
units.summary: The righteous are pictured eating with satisfaction, while the wicked go hungry.
units.principle: Satisfaction is a good to receive with gratitude and share with others.
units.insight: A person who lacks food deserves practical care without judgment about their character.
units.application: Share food or practical help with someone who needs it and give thanks for what you receive.

rel.note: Personified Wisdom also builds a house.

units.notes: House means household.
units.summary: Wisdom builds what folly tears down.
units.principle: Our habits leave their mark on what we build.
units.insight: Use the condition of what you are building for self-examination, with care for those in troubled homes.
units.application: Choose one habit that will strengthen your household, work, or ministry.

rel.note: Fear of the LORD leads a person to turn from evil.

units.notes: Walk means daily conduct.
units.summary: Daily conduct shows whether a person fears the LORD.
units.principle: Reverence for God takes visible form in upright conduct.
units.insight: Private honesty matters before God even when nobody checks.
units.application: Make one private decision in a way you could openly account for.

rel.note: The fool's speech likewise becomes a source of his own ruin.

units.notes: The rod pictures a blow produced by proud speech.
units.summary: Proud speech brings blows, while wise speech protects.
units.principle: Humility guards the use of words.
units.insight: An apology can interrupt the damage done by a boast or insult.
units.application: Replace one cutting remark with a measured account of the issue.

rel.note: Careful attention to livestock supports a household's provision.

units.notes: A manger is a feeding trough. Oxen supplied plowing power.
units.summary: Productive work often requires upkeep and expense.
units.principle: Consider the value of a tool alongside its cost.
units.insight: Some mess is part of doing work that yields something worthwhile.
units.application: Review whether the upkeep of a tool is justified by what it helps you produce.

rel.note: The same contrast returns with the effect of testimony on lives.

units.notes: Faithful means reliable in testimony.
units.summary: A faithful witness tells the truth, while a false witness speaks lies.
units.principle: Justice requires reliable testimony.
units.insight: A person's standing may depend on the accuracy of another's account.
units.application: Separate what you know from what you assume when giving an account.

rel.note: The wise receive correction and grow, while the scoffer resists it.

units.notes: A scoffer rejects correction. Easy describes how knowledge is received by the discerning.
units.summary: Scoffing frustrates the search for wisdom, while understanding helps knowledge take root.
units.principle: Teachability makes further learning possible.
units.insight: A learner can begin again by setting aside contempt for instruction.
units.application: Hear out one piece of counsel you would usually dismiss.

rel.note: The company of fools can bring harm, while the wise help others grow.

units.notes: Lips stand for what a person communicates.
units.summary: Step away from company whose words offer no wise guidance.
units.principle: Companionship shapes what counsel we receive.
units.insight: Care for someone need not make them a trusted adviser.
units.application: Limit the influence of a conversation that repeatedly promotes folly.

rel.note: The prudent also consider their steps before acting.

units.notes: Way means a person's course of life.
units.summary: The prudent examine their course, while fools are misled by deceit.
units.principle: Sound judgment includes examining one's own direction honestly.
units.insight: An outside perspective can reveal what we have been explaining away.
units.application: Ask a trusted person what outcome they see in a pattern you are following.

rel.note: The fool likewise treats doing evil as sport.

units.notes: The word rendered sin can also refer to guilt or a guilt offering.
units.summary: Fools mock wrongdoing, while goodwill is found among the upright.
units.principle: Taking responsibility protects relationships from the effects of dismissed wrongdoing.
units.insight: Repair becomes possible when harm is taken seriously.
units.application: Acknowledge an offense you have made light of and offer a concrete repair.

rel.note: Outward laughter likewise may conceal sorrow of the heart.

units.notes: Heart names the inner person. A stranger is someone outside that experience.
units.summary: The heart's deepest grief and joy cannot be fully shared.
units.principle: Give another person's account of their own experience room to stand.
units.insight: Companionship can matter even where complete understanding is impossible.
units.application: Listen to someone describe a loss or joy without assuming you know exactly how it feels.

rel.note: The overthrow of the wicked is contrasted with the righteous household standing.

units.notes: A house looks permanent beside a tent. Flourishing pictures growth.
units.summary: The wicked person's house falls, while the upright person's tent flourishes.
units.principle: Outward strength is a poor substitute for uprightness.
units.insight: A modest household can be a place of real vitality.
units.application: Strengthen a practice of honesty or care in your household.

rel.note: This is the identical saying in the project NKJV.

units.notes: The NKJV repeats this saying word for word at 16:25.
units.summary: A way can seem right and still end in death.
units.principle: Judge a course by God's wisdom and where it leads.
units.insight: A sincere person can reconsider their course without dismissing conscience.
units.application: Test one course that feels right against Scripture and trustworthy counsel.

rel.note: The heart's own bitterness is likewise known most fully from within.

units.notes: Mirth is outward gladness or festivity.
units.summary: Laughter can coexist with sorrow, and mirth can end in grief.
units.principle: Outward expression tells only part of what the heart carries.
units.insight: A cheerful appearance leaves room for a compassionate check-in.
units.application: Ask someone how they are doing and allow time for a candid answer.

rel.note: Wisdom benefits the one who chooses it, while the scoffer bears the consequences of scoffing.

units.notes: Backsliding begins inwardly. The final phrase can also be read as the good person receiving the fruit of their own conduct.
units.summary: An inward turning shapes what ultimately fills a life.
units.principle: The heart's course bears consequences.
units.insight: An inward change of direction can be addressed before it is obvious to others.
units.application: Identify a private habit of thought pulling you from God and take a step back toward Him.

rel.note: Proverbs is written to give prudence to the simple.

units.notes: Simple means uncommitted and easily led. The prudent weigh their steps.
units.summary: The simple believe readily, while the prudent consider their steps.
units.principle: A claim deserves testing before it directs action.
units.insight: Someone easily swayed can learn to check claims and seek sound counsel.
units.application: Check a persuasive claim against reliable evidence before acting on it.

rel.note: The prudent see danger and hide, while the simple continue and suffer.

units.notes: Rages can convey angry or arrogant forward movement.
units.summary: The wise turn away from evil, while fools charge ahead confidently.
units.principle: Confidence gives no protection on an evil course.
units.insight: Early caution can spare a difficult struggle later.
units.application: Step away from a situation you have assumed you can handle despite its risks.

rel.note: An angry person stirs up strife and commits many transgressions.

units.notes: Wicked intentions are deliberate schemes.
units.summary: Quick anger acts foolishly, and calculated malice brings hatred.
units.principle: Harm can arise from impulse or from a plan.
units.insight: A pause can help someone distinguish a hot reaction from a response worth choosing.
units.application: Delay an angry response and discard any plan to harm the person involved.

rel.note: The earlier verse shows the habits that lead to the two outcomes.

units.notes: Inheritance pictures what comes to someone. A crown pictures honor.
units.summary: The simple inherit folly, while knowledge crowns the prudent.
units.principle: Prudence actively receives knowledge that drift leaves behind.
units.insight: A person who has drifted can make a deliberate choice to learn.
units.application: Seek sound instruction in one area where you have been following others uncritically.

rel.note: The wicked can fall into the trouble from which the righteous are delivered.

units.notes: Bowing and waiting at gates picture submission or dependence.
units.summary: The proverb pictures evil eventually bowing before good.
units.principle: Present power does not decide the final standing of good and evil.
units.insight: A person can remain upright while unjust power appears secure.
units.application: Keep one upright commitment in a situation where wrongdoing seems to have the advantage.

rel.note: Wealth attracts friends, while the poor are separated from their company.

units.notes: Hated can describe being shunned. The many friends of the rich may be drawn by advantage.
units.summary: People often shun the poor and attach themselves to the rich.
units.principle: Social popularity can reflect advantage more than loyalty.
units.insight: Someone shunned for having little deserves the same attention as someone who can offer a benefit.
units.application: Give time to a neighbor without considering what they can offer in return.

rel.note: Mercy to the needy is also described as honoring their Maker.

units.notes: Mercy here is active kindness. Happy also conveys blessing.
units.summary: Despising a neighbor is sin, while showing mercy to the poor is blessed.
units.principle: Neighborly mercy puts respect into action.
units.insight: People facing need deserve practical help and dignity.
units.application: Ask a neighbor in need what practical help would serve them and offer what you can.

rel.note: Mercy and truth are likewise joined and associated with favor.

units.notes: Devise means work out a plan. Mercy and truth describe loyal love and faithfulness.
units.summary: Planning evil leads astray, while planning good belongs with loyalty and faithfulness.
units.principle: The moral direction of a plan matters before it is carried out.
units.insight: Care for others can be planned as deliberately as any other responsibility.
units.application: Plan one concrete good for someone instead of leaving the intention vague.

rel.note: Working the land produces food, while following empty pursuits shows poor judgment.

units.notes: Labor suggests effort that costs something. Idle chatter is talk without action.
units.summary: Work brings benefit, while mere talk leads toward want.
units.principle: Plans produce benefit when someone acts on them.
units.insight: A modest next step can turn a long discussion into useful action.
units.application: Turn one repeated conversation about a task into a dated action you can take.

rel.note: Riches and honor are also pictured among Wisdom's gifts.

units.notes: The crown pictures fitting honor. The repetition of folly emphasizes what it produces.
units.summary: Riches can adorn the wise, while fools produce more folly.
units.principle: Wisdom gives resources a fitting purpose.
units.insight: The use of resources often reveals more than their amount.
units.application: Use one resource you already have to support a worthwhile need.

rel.note: The faithful and false witnesses are contrasted earlier in the chapter.

units.notes: Souls here means lives. The witness is likely in a judicial setting.
units.summary: A true witness can save lives, while a false witness speaks lies.
units.principle: Truthfulness protects people who depend on testimony.
units.insight: An accurate account can be a practical defense for someone vulnerable.
units.application: Speak accurately when another person's safety or standing depends on your account.

rel.note: The LORD's name is also pictured as a refuge for the righteous.

units.notes: Refuge is a place of shelter. The pronoun can also be read as referring to the children of the one who fears the LORD.
units.summary: The fear of the LORD gives strong confidence and a place of refuge.
units.principle: Seeing God rightly gives a sound place to rest confidence.
units.insight: Reverence and trust can coexist when a person faces uncertainty.
units.application: Bring a fear before the LORD and name one faithful step you can take under His care.

rel.note: The same fountain and snares wording describes the teaching of the wise.

units.notes: A fountain gives ongoing refreshment. Snares are hidden traps.
units.summary: The fear of the LORD gives life and turns people away from deadly traps.
units.principle: A right view of God changes which paths we take.
units.insight: Reverence can help someone recognize danger before it becomes a crisis.
units.application: Name a course reverence for God calls you to leave and choose a different next step.

rel.note: Justice in government establishes the land that a king serves.

units.notes: A multitude of people is the community a king governs. Ruin pictures the collapse of his position.
units.summary: A ruler's honor depends on the people who make up the kingdom.
units.principle: Authority depends on the people it is meant to serve.
units.insight: Leadership can be assessed by how people fare under it.
units.application: Ask how one decision affects the people whose participation your work depends on.

rel.note: Being slow to anger and governing oneself are prized above military strength.

units.notes: Exalting folly pictures lifting it into view. Slow anger gives time for judgment.
units.summary: Patience shows understanding, while impulsive anger puts folly on display.
units.principle: A delayed response can be a sign of understanding.
units.insight: Waiting can make room to hear a side of the story you missed.
units.application: Before replying in anger, wait and ask one question about what happened.

rel.note: A merry heart and a broken spirit are likewise pictured as affecting the body.

units.notes: A sound heart is calm or healthy. Rot in the bones pictures inward decay.
units.summary: Inner peace supports well-being, while envy corrodes from within.
units.principle: What we cultivate inwardly can affect our whole life.
units.insight: Someone who is ill deserves care without speculation about their motives.
units.application: Name an envy you are feeding and replace one comparison with gratitude for a concrete good.

rel.note: Mocking the poor likewise reproaches their Maker.

units.notes: Oppression includes exploiting the poor through personal actions or unjust practices. Maker refers to God.
units.summary: Oppressing the poor insults their Maker, while mercy honors Him.
units.principle: The Maker's dignity is honored in the treatment of people He made.
units.insight: Worship can take concrete form in how a person responds to need and unfair treatment.
units.application: Meet a need and examine one practice under your influence that could treat vulnerable people more fairly.

rel.note: The fear of the LORD is already described as giving a place of refuge.

units.notes: Banished pictures being thrust away. The ancient Greek reads the second line differently, locating refuge in integrity.
units.summary: The wicked are brought down, while the righteous find refuge even in death.
