units.principle: The righteous person's refuge can be trusted at the point of greatest vulnerability.
units.insight: A grieving person can be offered the hope of God's keeping with gentleness.
units.application: Bring a fear of mortality before God in prayer and offer quiet companionship to someone grieving.

rel.note: The prudent hold back knowledge, while fools broadcast folly.

units.notes: Resting pictures wisdom settled in the heart. The second line is difficult and translations differ.
units.summary: Wisdom rests quietly in the discerning heart, while folly readily shows itself.
units.principle: Understanding does not need constant display.
units.insight: The quiet person in a discussion may have insight worth hearing.
units.application: Give a quieter person room to speak before offering everything you know.

rel.note: Justice establishes a land, while bribery overthrows it.

units.notes: Exalts means raises to honor. Any people makes the principle broadly applicable.
units.summary: Righteousness honors a nation, while sin disgraces any people.
units.principle: A community's honor depends on how it practices righteousness.
units.insight: Public conduct is subject to the same moral scrutiny as personal choices.
units.application: Choose one civic or community responsibility you can carry out with fairness and honesty.

rel.note: A wise servant is contrasted with a son who causes shame.

units.notes: A wise servant acts with practical insight. Causing shame means bringing disgrace through one's conduct.
units.summary: Wise service earns favor, while disgraceful conduct provokes anger.
units.principle: Entrusted responsibility calls for sound judgment and faithfulness.
units.insight: Dependable service can build trust over time.
units.application: Carry out one responsibility with the care you would want in someone acting on your behalf.

rel.note: A person slow to anger calms quarrels, while a wrathful person stirs them up.

units.notes: Soft describes a gentle reply. A harsh word causes pain.
units.summary: A gentle reply can calm anger, while a harsh word inflames it.
units.principle: We can govern our reply even when another person's response is beyond our control.
units.insight: Gentleness can go together with clear boundaries and seeking safety.
units.application: Lower the temperature of one disagreement with a calm, truthful reply, and seek safety if the exchange is threatening.

rel.note: The prudent hold knowledge back when appropriate, while fools broadcast folly.

units.notes: Using knowledge rightly involves presenting it well. Pours forth pictures uncontrolled speech.
units.summary: Wise speech makes knowledge useful, while foolish speech pours out unchecked.
units.principle: Sound judgment includes choosing how knowledge is shared.
units.insight: A hearer may benefit more from a short, well-timed explanation than from everything a speaker knows.
units.application: Choose one useful point and a fitting moment to explain it.

rel.note: All human paths are likewise open before the LORD.

units.notes: Eyes and keeping watch picture God's continuous awareness.
units.summary: The LORD keeps watch over both the evil and the good everywhere.
units.principle: Every place is open to the LORD's sight.
units.insight: Quiet faithfulness is visible to God even when nobody else sees it.
units.application: Bring one private choice before God and act with integrity in it.

rel.note: The earlier tree-of-life saying develops the image of Wisdom giving life and its connection to Christ.

units.notes: Wholesome can mean healing. Breaking the spirit pictures injury to the inner person.
units.summary: Healing words give life, while twisted speech can crush the spirit.
units.principle: Wise speech can nourish what cruel or deceitful speech harms.
units.insight: A person hurt by words can be served by truthful encouragement and patient care.
units.application: Offer one specific word of encouragement or repair a harm caused by your speech.

rel.note: Disregarding correction brings loss and shame, while heeding rebuke leads toward honor.

units.notes: Instruction includes a father's training and correction. Receiving it involves keeping it in mind and acting on it.
units.summary: Folly despises instruction, while prudence takes correction to heart.
units.principle: Prudence shows in the response to correction.
units.insight: A person can learn to hear a correction without making it a contest over pride.
units.application: Revisit one sound correction you dismissed and decide what it asks you to change.

rel.note: Greed for gain is also said to bring trouble upon a household.

units.notes: Treasure includes stored resources and lasting household good. Trouble accompanies the wicked person's income.
units.summary: Righteousness brings lasting good to a home, while wicked income brings trouble.
units.principle: The worth of income depends in part on how it is gained and what accompanies it.
units.insight: A family's strength can include trust and stability even when it has modest means.
units.application: Review one source of gain and ask what it is bringing into your household alongside money.

rel.note: The righteous likewise use their lips to nourish many.

units.notes: Disperse means scatter, like seed. The second line contrasts what comes from the fool's heart.
units.summary: Wise people spread knowledge, while the fool's heart supplies little that helps others learn.
units.principle: What we cultivate inwardly affects what we have to give through speech.
units.insight: A useful lesson can be shared generously and simply.
units.application: Share one reliable piece of knowledge with someone who can put it to use.

rel.note: A sacrifice brought by the wicked, especially with evil intent, is likewise detestable.

units.notes: Sacrifice was a formal act of worship. Abomination and delight express opposite responses from God.
units.summary: The LORD rejects worship joined to persistent wickedness and delights in upright prayer.
units.principle: Worship and the moral course of life belong together.
units.insight: A person who recognizes a wrong can bring it to God honestly and turn from it.
units.application: Bring a practice that conflicts with your worship before God and take a step of repentance.

rel.note: The LORD likewise detests crookedness and delights in blameless ways.

units.notes: Way means the whole course of life. Following righteousness conveys eager pursuit.
units.summary: The LORD detests the wicked way and loves the pursuit of righteousness.
units.principle: God cares about the direction a person actively pursues.
units.insight: A person can begin pursuing what is right through a change in today's conduct.
units.application: Put one upright intention into practice before the day ends.

rel.note: Repeated resistance to rebuke likewise leads toward sudden ruin.

units.notes: Forsaking the way means abandoning the right course. Harsh discipline points to severe correction or consequences.
units.summary: Abandoning the right way brings hard consequences, and rejecting correction can end in death.
units.principle: Correction offers a chance to change course while there is time.
units.insight: A warning heard now can prevent a harder lesson later.
units.application: Act on one credible warning about a destructive pattern before it deepens.

rel.note: The earlier saying presents the same divine watchfulness over every place.

units.notes: Hell renders Sheol, the realm of the dead. Destruction renders Abaddon, associated with that realm.
units.summary: If even the realm of the dead lies open to God, so does every human heart.
units.principle: No part of the inner life lies beyond God's knowledge.
units.insight: Being fully known by God gives room for honest prayer about hidden motives and pain.
units.application: Name a motive or fear candidly before God in prayer.

rel.note: The scoffer's hatred of rebuke contrasts with the wise person's welcome of it.

units.notes: The scoffer treats correction with contempt and avoids those likely to offer it.
units.summary: The scoffer resents correction and avoids the wise.
units.principle: Avoiding correction keeps a person from the wisdom others could offer.
units.insight: Someone who notices their avoidance can choose to reenter a conversation with humility.
units.application: Speak with one wise person whose honest questions you have been avoiding.

rel.note: A merry heart and broken spirit likewise have different effects on the whole person.

units.notes: Countenance is the face. A broken spirit pictures grief reaching deep within.
units.summary: Joy can brighten the face, and deep sorrow can break the spirit.
units.principle: The burdens of the heart deserve attention and care.
units.insight: Someone burdened by grief may need patient presence and practical support.
units.application: Ask someone who is grieving what would make today easier and offer specific help.

rel.note: The discerning heart acquires knowledge and the ear of the wise seeks it.

units.notes: Feeding pictures steady grazing. The heart seeks, while the mouth takes in what it feeds on.
units.summary: The discerning seek knowledge, while fools feed on folly.
units.principle: What we seek and consume trains our judgment.
units.insight: Recurring habits of attention can shape what someone wants to learn next.
units.application: Replace one regular source of foolish talk with a source that helps you learn.

rel.note: The other saying also acknowledges that outward experience and inward sorrow can differ.

units.notes: Afflicted can include the oppressed or burdened. A continual feast pictures repeated enjoyment.
units.summary: Affliction can make every day hard, while a merry heart finds continual enjoyment.
units.principle: The quality of our days involves both real circumstances and the condition of the heart.
units.insight: Take the reality of another person's burden seriously before talking about joy.
units.application: Offer concrete relief to someone whose days are burdened and make room to enjoy a good they value.

rel.note: A little with righteousness is also preferred to great revenues without justice.

units.notes: A little means modest resources. Trouble describes turmoil that can accompany wealth.
units.summary: A little with the fear of the LORD is better than great treasure with turmoil.
units.principle: Money cannot replace the good of living before God in reverence.
units.insight: Contentment can grow alongside honest efforts to meet material needs.
units.application: Choose one way to honor the LORD even if it means accepting a smaller gain.

rel.note: A dry morsel with quiet is likewise preferred to feasting with strife.

units.notes: A meal of herbs is plain fare. A fatted calf represents a feast.
units.summary: A simple meal with love is better than a feast with hatred.
units.principle: The quality of a relationship matters more than the display around it.
units.insight: Hospitality can be meaningful without an expensive table.
units.application: Share a simple meal and give more attention to the people than to the menu.

rel.note: An angry person likewise stirs up strife and multiplies wrongdoing.

units.notes: Wrathful describes a person given to angry reactions. Calming strife means quieting a quarrel.
units.summary: Hot temper stirs up strife, while patience helps calm it.
units.principle: Self-control can serve the peace of a whole conversation.
units.insight: Pausing can make space for a response that lowers tension.
units.application: Before answering in a tense exchange, wait and ask one calm question.

rel.note: The lazy man's claim of a lion outside gives an example of using an obstacle to avoid action.

units.notes: A hedge of thorns obstructs travel. A highway is a raised, cleared road.
units.summary: Laziness leaves a thorny path, while uprightness makes a clearer road.
units.principle: The habits we practice can clear a course or make it harder to travel.
units.insight: A person can distinguish an avoidable delay from a barrier they need help to overcome.
units.application: Address one avoidable obstacle you have left in the way of a responsibility.

rel.note: The first line likewise joins a wise son to his father's joy, and the second shows folly's effect on his mother.

units.notes: The first line echoes 10:1. The foolish man may be a grown son who looks down on his mother.
units.summary: A wise child brings joy, while a fool treats his mother with contempt.
units.principle: Wisdom shows in how people treat those who raised them.
units.insight: Honoring a parent can take a practical form suited to the relationship.
units.application: Offer a sincere word of respect or a practical act of care to a parent or caregiver.

rel.note: The fool likewise treats evil as sport, in contrast to the person of understanding.

units.notes: Destitute of discernment literally lacks heart or judgment. Walking uprightly pictures taking a straight course.
units.summary: Folly delights the undiscerning, while understanding keeps a person on a straight course.
units.principle: Enjoyment alone cannot establish that a course is wise.
units.insight: An enjoyable practice can be examined honestly for where it is taking us.
units.application: Assess one pastime by the conduct it encourages and change it if needed.

rel.note: Plans are likewise established through counsel.

units.notes: Counsel involves consultation. Established means made firm.
units.summary: Sound counsel helps establish plans that might otherwise fail.
units.principle: Wise planning makes room for other people's insight.
units.insight: A leader can welcome questions before a decision becomes difficult to change.
units.application: Ask two trustworthy people to identify weaknesses in an important plan.

rel.note: A fitting word is likewise pictured as something of great worth.

units.notes: Due season means the fitting time. The answer brings joy to the person who gives it.
units.summary: A fitting answer brings joy, and a timely word does good.
units.principle: Timing is part of wise speech.
units.insight: A listener may be ready for the same truth at one moment and unable to receive it at another.
units.application: Choose an appropriate time to offer a truthful word of encouragement or guidance.

rel.note: The adulterous woman's house is pictured as a descent to Sheol.

units.notes: Upward pictures the path toward life. Hell renders Sheol, the realm of the dead.
units.summary: The path of the wise leads upward toward life and away from death.
units.principle: Where a road leads matters more than how inviting it first appears.
units.insight: A wise change of direction can begin with a small step away from danger.
units.application: Choose a concrete step toward life in an area where you are being pulled downward.

rel.note: The fatherless have a strong Redeemer who pleads their cause against those who cross their boundary.

units.notes: A boundary stone marked land ownership. Widows were vulnerable to people who moved such markers.
units.summary: The LORD opposes the proud and defends the widow's property.
units.principle: God's justice protects people who are easily dispossessed.
units.insight: Care for a vulnerable person can include defending what belongs to them.
units.application: Check whether a person with little leverage is being treated fairly in a matter you can influence.

rel.note: The LORD likewise detests a crooked heart and delights in upright ways.

units.notes: Thoughts can refer to plans or schemes. The second line connects purity and pleasant words.
units.summary: The LORD detests evil schemes and welcomes words that flow from purity.
units.principle: Words and motives both matter before God.
units.insight: Gracious words have substance when they agree with the speaker's intentions.
units.application: Check the motive behind a pleasant thing you plan to say and speak without manipulation.

rel.note: The person who troubles their own household likewise faces loss.

units.notes: Greedy gain includes profit obtained unjustly. Bribes bend judgment for advantage.
units.summary: Greed troubles a household, while rejecting bribes leads toward life.
units.principle: Dishonest gain carries costs beyond the person receiving it.
units.insight: A household is better served by integrity than by gain that brings hidden harm.
units.application: Decline a benefit that would compromise a fair decision and account openly for any conflict of interest.

rel.note: The fool likewise pours out folly, while the wise use knowledge well.

units.notes: Studies means weighs how to answer. Pours forth pictures an uncontrolled flow.
units.summary: The righteous weigh their answers, while the wicked pour out evil.
units.principle: Good answers begin with judgment in the heart.
units.insight: A thoughtful delay can be kinder than an immediate reply.
units.application: Pause before a difficult reply and consider the truth, tone, and timing of what you intend to say.

rel.note: The prayer of the upright likewise delights the LORD.

units.notes: Far describes relational distance. Hearing prayer means attending favorably to it.
units.summary: The LORD is far from those who persist in wickedness and hears the prayers of the righteous.
units.principle: Prayer belongs with a heart willing to walk uprightly before God.
units.insight: A person convicted of wrongdoing can respond with confession and prayer.
units.application: Bring a request to God and confess any wrong you are unwilling to leave.

rel.note: Good news from a distant country likewise refreshes like cold water.

units.notes: Light of the eyes may refer to a cheerful look or to seeing something good. Healthy bones picture deep refreshment.
units.summary: A bright look cheers the heart, and good news refreshes deeply.
units.principle: Encouragement can reach a person through what they see and hear.
units.insight: Warm attention and honest good news can be real gifts to someone who is weary.
units.application: Share a specific piece of good news with someone who could use refreshment.

rel.note: Giving instruction to a wise person makes that person wiser still.

units.notes: Hearing includes heeding. The rebukes of life are corrections that lead toward life.
units.summary: Those who heed life-giving correction find their place among the wise.
units.principle: Receiving sound correction is part of learning to live wisely.
units.insight: A correction can become a means of belonging among people who value growth.
units.application: Ask a wise person for a correction that would help you grow and act on it.

rel.note: Love of instruction likewise goes with knowledge, while refusal produces dullness.

units.notes: Disdains means lets go or treats as worthless. Gaining understanding literally pictures acquiring heart.
units.summary: Rejecting instruction harms oneself, while heeding rebuke grows understanding.
units.principle: Correction helps the learner gain judgment they cannot get by dismissing it.
units.insight: Receiving a sound correction can be an act of care for one's future.
units.application: Identify one rebuke you overlooked and make the change it calls for if it is sound.

rel.note: The same line about humility before honor follows a warning about haughtiness before destruction.

units.notes: Instruction includes training and correction. The final line recurs at 18:12.
units.summary: The fear of the LORD trains in wisdom, and humility comes before honor.
units.principle: Humility belongs to reverence for God and leaves honor in His hands.
units.insight: Christ's example gives people reason to humble themselves even when recognition does not follow immediately.
units.application: Serve someone in a way that requires humility and leave the recognition to God.

rel.note: The closing saying likewise attributes the decision to the LORD.

units.notes: Preparations are arrangements made inwardly before speaking.
units.summary: We prepare our words, while the answer is from the LORD.
units.principle: Human preparation is real and belongs under God's direction.
units.insight: Preparation can go together with prayer and openness to a changed response.
units.application: Prepare for a difficult conversation and pray for wisdom in the answer you give.

rel.note: A person sees their own way as right, while the LORD weighs the hearts.

units.notes: Weighing spirits pictures measuring inward motives on a scale.
units.summary: We can approve our own ways while God weighs our motives.
units.principle: God's assessment reaches deeper than our own approval.
units.insight: A trusted question can help uncover a motive we have been excusing.
units.application: Ask God to expose one motive you have been reluctant to examine.

rel.note: Human planning and divine direction appear together again.

units.notes: Commit pictures rolling a burden onto the LORD. Thoughts are plans and purposes.
units.summary: Entrust your work to the LORD, who can establish your plans.
units.principle: Dependence on God shapes both the work and how we receive its outcome.
units.insight: A changed plan can still be part of God's answer to prayer.
units.application: Pray over a planned task, take the next responsible step, and stay open to redirection.

rel.note: Even an alliance cannot make the wicked escape punishment.

units.notes: For Himself can also be read as for its purpose. The day of doom is a day of disaster or judgment.
units.summary: Even the end of wickedness falls within the LORD's rule.
units.principle: Wickedness remains answerable to God's rule.
units.insight: God's goodness remains a ground for trust when evil appears unchecked.
units.application: In the face of wrongdoing, pursue an upright response and entrust judgment to God.

rel.note: The same joining-forces wording shows that the wicked cannot escape punishment.

units.notes: Proud in heart describes settled self-exaltation. Joining forces evokes hand joining hand.
units.summary: The LORD detests inward pride, and alliances cannot shield it from judgment.
units.principle: God weighs the heart even when others endorse its posture.
units.insight: Collective approval can make arrogance harder to recognize.
units.application: Identify one assumption of superiority that your peers reinforce and bring it honestly before God.

rel.note: The same pairing joins fear of the LORD with turning from evil.

units.notes: Mercy and truth are steadfast love and faithfulness. Whose qualities are in view is debated.
units.summary: God's mercy and truth provide atonement, and reverence leads people to turn from evil.
units.principle: God's provision for forgiveness belongs with a changed direction of life.
units.insight: A person can receive forgiveness with gratitude and take a real step away from wrongdoing.
units.application: Confess a wrong to God and remove one practice that keeps drawing you back to it.

rel.note: Gentle speech can serve peace, and this saying attributes reconciliation to the LORD.

units.notes: Ways are habitual conduct. The LORD is the one who brings about peace.
units.summary: The LORD can bring enemies to peace with someone whose ways please Him.
units.principle: Peace with others is an outcome God can give.
units.insight: Someone mistreated can remain upright without carrying blame for the other person's hostility.
units.application: Take an upright step toward peace where it is safe, and entrust the response to God.

rel.note: Another better-than saying places reverence for God above wealth with turmoil.

units.notes: Vast revenues are large proceeds. Without justice describes how gain is obtained or held.
units.summary: A little gained righteously is better than great income gained unjustly.
units.principle: Justice matters more than the size of a return.
units.insight: A modest honest gain can be received without shame.
units.application: Decline one profitable arrangement that would require treating someone unfairly.

rel.note: Many human plans stand alongside the enduring counsel of the LORD.

units.notes: The heart plans the route. Steps are the actual course traveled.
units.summary: A person plans the way, and the LORD directs the steps.
units.principle: Sound planning belongs under trust in God's direction.
units.insight: A redirected plan can be received with patience and examined prayerfully.
units.application: Make a responsible plan and hold its timing and outcome open before the LORD.

rel.note: Justice in royal judgment is part of what establishes the land.

units.notes: Divination here conveys the weight of an authoritative verdict. The second line can express an obligation.
units.summary: A king's authoritative verdict calls for just judgment.
units.principle: Greater authority carries greater responsibility for justice.
units.insight: People who decide disputes need care because others live with their verdicts.
units.application: Before judging a dispute, hear both sides and check the grounds for your decision.

rel.note: A just weight delights the LORD, and dishonest scales are detestable to Him.

units.notes: Stone weights were kept in a merchant's bag and used on balance scales.
units.summary: Fair measures in commerce belong to the LORD's order.
units.principle: Integrity in trade requires the same standard behind the counter as in public.
units.insight: God takes ordinary accuracy seriously even where a customer cannot check it.
units.application: Check a measurement, invoice, or price you control for fairness and accuracy.

rel.note: Removing wicked influence from a king's presence establishes the throne in righteousness.

units.notes: Throne means the ruler's position and government. The first line can include kings detesting wrongdoing in themselves and others.
units.summary: Righteousness establishes a throne, and wrongdoing undermines it.
units.principle: Justice is a foundation of stable authority.
units.insight: People in authority can examine their own conduct before condemning wrongdoing elsewhere.
units.application: Correct one unfair practice within a responsibility you oversee.

rel.note: Graceful speech and purity of heart also commend a person to the king.

units.notes: Righteous lips are the truthful speech of advisers or servants.
units.summary: A wise ruler welcomes truthful speech.
units.principle: Just authority needs truthful counsel.
units.insight: People speak more candidly when a leader shows they welcome inconvenient truths.
units.application: Invite one adviser to tell you what you may be overlooking and thank them for speaking plainly.

rel.note: The king's wrath is likewise pictured as dangerous, in contrast to his refreshing favor.

units.notes: Messengers of death picture officers who can carry out a royal sentence. Appease means to pacify.
units.summary: Royal anger can be deadly, and wise conduct can help calm it.
units.principle: Wisdom weighs how to respond when anger is backed by power.
units.insight: Careful speech can coexist with prudent protection where authority is angry.
units.application: In a tense exchange with someone in authority, choose a calm and truthful reply and seek help if needed.

rel.note: The king's favor is similarly compared to dew on the grass.

units.notes: The light of a king's face is his favorable expression. Latter rain was spring rain that ripened crops.
units.summary: A king's favor can give life like timely spring rain.
units.principle: Authority can use its favor to protect and sustain others.
units.insight: The approval of a person in authority can give others room to thrive.
units.application: Use whatever authority you have to give timely support to someone who needs it.

rel.note: Wisdom's proceeds are better than silver and her gain better than fine gold.

units.notes: The exclamation compares wisdom and understanding with gold and silver.
units.summary: Wisdom and understanding are worth more than gold and silver.
units.principle: Wisdom gives direction to whatever resources a person gains.
units.insight: Money is better used when judgment has already set its priorities.
units.application: Give time to gaining understanding before committing resources to an important pursuit.

rel.note: The father urges careful attention to the path and a deliberate departure from evil.

units.notes: A highway is a raised or cleared road. Preserving one's soul means guarding one's life.
units.summary: The upright turn away from evil, and guarding one's course preserves life.
units.principle: Life is guarded by attention to the course we take.
units.insight: A small correction in direction can keep a wrong turn from becoming a habit.
units.application: Remove one recurring opportunity that pulls your steps toward wrongdoing.

rel.note: Haughtiness likewise comes before destruction, while humility comes before honor.

units.notes: Destruction pictures shattering. Haughty describes a spirit that lifts itself high.
units.summary: Pride sets a person on the course that ends in a fall.
units.principle: Refusing correction leaves pride free to prepare its own fall.
units.insight: A person can acknowledge limits without treating humility as self-contempt.
units.application: Ask what you may be presuming about yourself, others, or God and act on one sound correction.

rel.note: A modest portion with the fear of the LORD is likewise preferred to great wealth with trouble.

units.notes: The lowly can include the poor and afflicted. Spoil is plunder shared by those who took it.
units.summary: A humble spirit with the lowly is better than sharing the spoil of the proud.
units.principle: Gains that require sharing in pride carry the cost of that allegiance.
units.insight: People can stand alongside those with little status without seeking a return in prestige.
units.application: Decline an advantage that depends on arrogant conduct and stand with someone overlooked.

rel.note: Wholehearted reliance on the LORD goes with guidance for one's course.

units.notes: The word can mean instruction or a matter to be handled.
units.summary: Wise attention finds good, and those who trust the LORD are blessed.
units.principle: Good judgment and trust in the LORD belong together.
units.insight: A person can seek reliable instruction while resting confidence in God.
units.application: Pay close attention to sound instruction about a current decision and bring the decision before God.

rel.note: The wise heart likewise makes the lips more effective in teaching.

units.notes: Sweetness of the lips means gracious speech. Learning can also convey persuasiveness.
units.summary: Wisdom earns a reputation for discernment, and gracious speech helps people learn.
units.principle: The manner of teaching can support the good of what is taught.
units.insight: A truthful lesson can be made more accessible by changing its tone.
units.application: Explain one difficult point with words that are clear, gracious, and suited to the learner.

rel.note: Wise instruction is likewise a life-giving fountain that turns people from snares.

units.notes: A wellspring keeps supplying water. Folly can itself be the painful correction fools receive.
units.summary: Understanding sustains life, while folly becomes a fool's harsh lesson.
units.principle: Receiving understanding early can spare the correction brought by folly.
units.insight: A painful consequence can prompt someone to become teachable.
units.application: Take sound counsel seriously before repeating a mistake whose outcome you already know.

rel.note: The righteous heart likewise considers how to answer before speaking.

units.notes: The heart teaches the mouth. Adding learning can mean making speech more persuasive.
units.summary: The wise heart trains the mouth and makes its speech more effective.
units.principle: The quality of our speech grows from what the heart has learned.
units.insight: A considered answer often begins well before the conversation itself.
units.application: Reflect on a truth before trying to explain it and choose words that make it clearer.

rel.note: A wholesome tongue likewise gives life to the person who hears it.

units.notes: Honeycomb evokes sweetness. Health to the bones pictures deep refreshment.
units.summary: Gracious words refresh like honey and give strength to the hearer.
units.principle: Pleasant speech is good when it genuinely refreshes another person.
units.insight: Specific, truthful encouragement can meet someone in a weary moment.
units.application: Offer one truthful word of appreciation to someone who needs encouragement.

rel.note: The earlier verse is identical in the project NKJV.

units.notes: The project NKJV repeats 14:12 word for word on the other side of the 16:1 boundary.
units.summary: A way can seem right and still end in death.
units.principle: The end of a path matters more than its first appearance.
units.insight: A sincere conviction can be examined with care and corrected when needed.
units.application: Use the earlier treatment at 14:12 to test one course against Scripture and sound counsel.

rel.note: Working one's land is similarly connected to having food.

units.notes: The hungry mouth stands for the worker's appetite and need for food.
units.summary: The need for food can spur a person to keep working.
units.principle: A clear connection between work and need can motivate effort.
units.insight: Meeting basic needs is a worthy purpose for ordinary work.
units.application: Name the concrete need one task helps meet and complete it with care.

rel.note: The earlier troublemaker likewise joins crooked speech to deliberate plans that sow discord.

units.notes: Ungodly man is an expression for a corrupt troublemaker. Digging pictures searching out or plotting harm.
units.summary: A troublemaker digs up harm and spreads it with scorching words.
units.principle: What someone seeks out can become the harm their speech carries.
units.insight: Refusing to pass on a damaging story can stop some of its spread.
units.application: Stop circulating a report gathered to embarrass someone and correct it if you have already shared it.

rel.note: Repeating a matter likewise separates friends.

units.notes: Sowing strife pictures spreading discord. A whisperer passes damaging talk quietly.
units.summary: Crooked talk spreads strife, and gossip can divide close friends.
units.principle: Divisive talk can undo trust built over years.
units.insight: A friendship can be protected by checking a report directly with the person concerned.
units.application: Refuse to relay a private accusation and encourage direct, truthful conversation.

rel.note: The father warns the son to refuse when sinners entice him.

units.notes: Enticing means persuading someone to come along. The way is the course that follows.
units.summary: A violent person can lure a neighbor onto a harmful path.
units.principle: Consider where an invitation leads before agreeing to join it.
units.insight: A request that sounds like loyalty can be examined for the harm it asks someone to share.
units.application: Decline an invitation that would make you a participant in hurting someone.

rel.note: The troublemaker there also uses signals as part of a plan to do harm.

units.notes: The wink and pursed lips belong to a specific picture of plotting. Their meaning depends on the situation.
units.summary: A schemer's gestures can serve a plan already directed toward harm.
units.principle: Conduct should be understood in light of its purpose and pattern.
units.insight: A single expression gives little grounds for judging someone without context.
units.application: Refuse to join any covert signal meant to deceive or harm another person.

rel.note: Gray hair is also named as the splendor of older people.

units.notes: Silver hair represents age. The NKJV links its honor to a righteous course.
units.summary: Silver hair is a crown of honor when found in a righteous life.
units.principle: A righteous course gives the years a fitting honor.
units.insight: People can honor a lifetime of faithfulness without measuring faithfulness by age alone.
units.application: Ask an older person about one upright practice that has sustained them and consider learning from it.

rel.note: Lack of self-control is pictured as a city with broken walls.

units.notes: Ruling the spirit means governing one's reactions. Capturing a city represents a major outward victory.
units.summary: Governing one's spirit is greater than capturing a city.
units.principle: Strength is measured in part by how well a person governs themselves.
units.insight: Restraint under provocation can require real courage.
units.application: Pause before responding to a provocation and choose a measured reply.

rel.note: The chapter opens and closes with an outcome described as from the LORD.

units.notes: Casting a lot was an ancient practice for seeking a decision. The lap held the lot.
units.summary: Even the decision of a cast lot is from the LORD.
units.principle: What appears beyond human control remains within God's rule.
units.insight: Uncertain outcomes can be entrusted to God after responsible choices are made.
units.application: Take the responsible step you can identify and entrust the unknown outcome to the LORD.

rel.note: A simple meal with love is likewise better than a feast with hatred.

units.notes: A dry morsel is plain bread. Feasting pictures a table supplied with plenty.
units.summary: A plain meal with peace is better than a feast with strife.
units.principle: Peace matters more to a household than the richness of its table.
units.insight: People can build a welcoming home with modest means.
units.application: Protect the peace of one shared meal by addressing a dispute at a more fitting time.

rel.note: A ruler likewise favors a wise servant and reacts against conduct that causes shame.

units.notes: A son normally inherited, while a servant worked under the household. The saying reverses those expectations.
units.summary: Wise service can receive honor and responsibility that birth alone cannot secure.
units.principle: Responsibility is fittingly entrusted to people who show sound judgment.
units.insight: A person's work can be recognized even when their position makes them easy to overlook.
units.application: Recognize one person whose dependable work merits more trust or responsibility.

rel.note: The same metalworking image introduces a different test involving praise.

units.notes: A crucible and furnace test metals by heat. Hearts include thoughts, motives, and desires.
units.summary: The LORD tests hearts as fire tests precious metal.
units.principle: God sees and tests what outward appearance cannot disclose.
units.insight: A difficult season can be brought before God without assuming it is punishment.
units.application: Ask God to reveal a motive you cannot readily see and respond honestly to what comes to light.

rel.note: The harm of whispered gossip shows why an eager audience matters.

units.notes: Giving heed is deliberate attention. A spiteful tongue aims to harm.
units.summary: The speech a person eagerly hears can reveal what they are disposed to approve.
units.principle: Listening can become participation when it welcomes deceit.
units.insight: Refusing an audience can help interrupt the spread of malice.
units.application: Stop giving attention to a source of malicious reports and refuse to pass them on.

rel.note: Oppression of the poor likewise reproaches their Maker, while mercy honors Him.

units.notes: Reproaching the Maker means insulting God through contempt for someone He made.
units.summary: Mocking the poor dishonors God, and gloating over calamity brings consequences.
units.principle: How we respond to another person's hardship matters before God.
units.insight: A person in hardship deserves dignity, even when their situation is the subject of public talk.
units.application: Interrupt a contemptuous joke about someone in need and offer practical help where possible.

rel.note: The upright conduct of a parent can bless children after them.

units.notes: A crown is a sign of honor. The two lines look in opposite directions across generations.
units.summary: Grandchildren honor the old, and children can take pride in their fathers.
units.principle: Character and affection can bless a family in both directions across generations.
units.insight: Intergenerational care can be cherished without measuring a person's worth by family circumstances.
units.application: Share a story of faithfulness with someone from another generation and invite them to share one too.

rel.note: A ruler's authoritative words carry a responsibility to judge rightly.

units.notes: Excellent speech means fine or noble speech. The second line strengthens the comparison.
units.summary: Noble speech ill suits folly, and lying is especially unfitting in a ruler.
units.principle: The responsibilities of authority heighten the importance of truthful speech.
units.insight: People with influence can repair some harm by acknowledging a false statement plainly.
units.application: Correct one statement in which your position may have led others to trust an inaccurate claim.

rel.note: The later saying explicitly condemns accepting a secret payment to pervert justice.

units.notes: The word rendered present also means bribe at 17:23. The stone pictures a gift that seems to secure favor.
units.summary: A gift used for influence can look like a sure way to gain favor.
units.principle: A method's apparent success gives no assurance that it is just.
units.insight: An offered benefit can be assessed for what it expects in return.
units.application: Decline or disclose a gift that could improperly influence a decision you control.

rel.note: Love likewise covers offenses, while hatred keeps strife active.

units.notes: Covering a transgression means forgiving it and letting it rest. Repeating can mean telling others or repeatedly reopening it.
units.summary: Forgiveness seeks love, while repeatedly bringing up an offense can divide friends.
units.principle: Love gives up using an offense as a weapon.
units.insight: A person can forgive while seeking protection and accountability.
units.application: Stop repeating a forgiven grievance and bring any ongoing harm to someone able to address it responsibly.

rel.note: The wise welcome correction and grow through it.

units.notes: More effective pictures a rebuke sinking in. A hundred blows is deliberate exaggeration.
units.summary: A rebuke reaches a discerning person more readily than severe consequences reach a fool.
units.principle: Willingness to learn gives correction its opportunity to work.
units.insight: Clear, patient correction can help a person who is ready to hear it.
units.application: Take one sound rebuke seriously before consequences have to teach you the same lesson.

rel.note: Repeated resistance to correction can likewise bring sudden ruin.

units.notes: Rebellion is defiance of rightful authority. A cruel messenger may picture an officer sent to enforce judgment.
units.summary: Persistent rebellion can bring a severe reckoning.
units.principle: Habitual defiance exposes a person to consequences they may no longer control.
units.insight: A person can change course before defiance becomes their settled response.
units.application: Address one pattern of defying a rightful obligation and take a concrete step to meet it.

rel.note: The learner is likewise told to leave the fool's company.

units.notes: A bear deprived of cubs pictures fierce danger. The comparison deliberately heightens the warning.
units.summary: A fool in full pursuit of folly is more dangerous than a bear robbed of her cubs.
units.principle: Active folly deserves to be taken seriously as a danger.
units.insight: Some situations call for distance before a conversation can help.
units.application: Leave a situation where another person's escalating folly is putting people at risk.

rel.note: Troubling one's own household likewise produces lasting loss.

units.notes: Reward here means repay. House refers to the household as well as the dwelling.
units.summary: Repaying good with evil can bring lasting trouble to a household.
units.principle: Returning harm for kindness damages the bonds that sustain a household.
units.insight: Trust is especially wounded when kindness is answered with harm.
units.application: Acknowledge a kindness you have answered badly and take a concrete step to repair the harm.

rel.note: Patience calms quarrels, while wrath stirs them up.

units.notes: Releasing water evokes a breach that can widen as water flows through it.
units.summary: Stop strife early, before it breaks out like released water.
units.principle: Early restraint can prevent a quarrel from growing beyond control.
units.insight: A pause can keep an argument from gaining momentum.
units.application: Stop one escalating exchange and return to the issue when you can discuss it calmly.

rel.note: Showing partiality to the wicked and overturning the righteous in judgment are likewise condemned.

units.notes: Justifying and condemning are terms for verdicts. Both unjust reversals are called detestable.
units.summary: The LORD detests verdicts that clear the guilty or condemn the innocent.
units.principle: Justice requires verdicts that accord with truth.
units.insight: Pressure to favor an ally can be resisted by giving the same attention to evidence in every case.
units.application: Review a judgment you are making and apply the same standard to every person involved.

rel.note: The call to buy truth and wisdom shows the deliberate commitment missing from the fool's purchase.

units.notes: Purchase price represents access or opportunity. Having no heart means lacking the will or desire to learn.
units.summary: Resources cannot buy wisdom for someone unwilling to learn.
units.principle: Wisdom requires a willing heart alongside access to instruction.
units.insight: A person can begin to learn by naming why they have avoided making use of a good opportunity.
units.application: Use one opportunity you already have to seek and practice sound instruction.

rel.note: The later saying also portrays faithful friendship, including a friend who stays closer than a brother.

units.notes: At all times includes adversity. Brother names the family bond the second line brings into view.
units.summary: A faithful friend loves in every season, especially when adversity calls for help.
units.principle: Loyalty is made visible by remaining present in adversity.
units.insight: Showing up in difficulty can mean listening or offering practical help within your means.
units.application: Contact a friend facing hardship and offer one specific form of help.

rel.note: The earlier passage explains the trap of becoming surety and urges seeking release.

units.notes: Striking hands sealed a pledge. A surety agrees to pay if another person defaults.
units.summary: Friendship does not require guaranteeing another person's debt.
units.principle: Loyalty and prudent financial boundaries can coexist.
units.insight: A friend can offer help honestly within limits they can sustain.
units.application: Avoid cosigning and consider direct help you can afford to give.

rel.note: Pride likewise sets a person on the course toward a fall.

units.notes: Exalting a gate likely pictures an ostentatious entrance. Some readers take it as boastful speech.
units.summary: Loving conflict and displaying pride put a person on a course toward harm.
units.principle: Strife and self-display can invite consequences their pursuer overlooks.
units.insight: The urge to win publicly can reveal a deeper investment in the conflict itself.
units.application: Let go of a public display of superiority and address the actual disagreement plainly.

rel.note: Crooked ways likewise expose the person who practices them.

units.notes: A deceitful heart is inwardly crooked. Evil can mean the trouble a person falls into.
units.summary: A crooked heart finds no good, and twisted speech leads into trouble.
units.principle: Deceit undermines the good a person hopes to gain from it.
units.insight: Someone who has been misleading others can begin repair with a candid account.
units.application: Correct a misleading account and deal directly with the concern it was hiding.

rel.note: The later saying names the grief of both father and mother.

units.notes: Begetting stresses the bond between father and child. The word rendered scoffer here is often translated fool.
units.summary: A child's folly can bring deep grief to a father.
units.principle: The choices of a child can deeply affect those who raised them.
units.insight: A grieving parent deserves compassion without assumptions about their faithfulness or care.
units.application: Take one step to repair needless hurt you have caused a parent or caregiver.

rel.note: A sound heart and inward decay are likewise pictured as affecting the body.

units.notes: Medicine pictures a benefit to the whole person. Dry bones picture strength wearing away.
units.summary: Joy can refresh the whole person, while a crushed spirit can wear someone down.
units.principle: Care for the inner life belongs alongside care for the body.
units.insight: A person who is suffering can receive companionship and appropriate care together.
units.application: Offer a weary person practical support and listen to what would bring them some comfort.

rel.note: The person who hates bribes chooses a course that leads toward life.

units.notes: Behind the back pictures a concealed payment. Perverting justice means bending a verdict away from what is right.
units.summary: Accepting a secret bribe bends justice away from what is right.
units.principle: Fair judgment requires refusing benefits that buy influence.
units.insight: An unexplained benefit can be brought into the open before it distorts a decision.
units.application: Refuse or disclose an offered benefit that could compromise a fair decision.

rel.note: The learner is urged to keep sound wisdom and discretion in sight.

units.notes: Wisdom before one's face pictures a clear focus. The ends of the earth picture a wandering gaze.
units.summary: The discerning keep wisdom in view, while the fool's attention wanders.
units.principle: Wisdom requires attention to the decision actually before us.
units.insight: A nearby responsibility can be a practical place to begin learning wisdom.
units.application: Act on sound counsel about one present duty before chasing a distant possibility.

rel.note: The first saying of Solomon's collection contrasts parental gladness and grief.

units.notes: Grief includes sorrow and vexation. Her who bore him emphasizes the mother's personal bond.
units.summary: A foolish child's course can grieve both parents deeply.
units.principle: Folly can harm people bound to us by lasting affection.
units.insight: Parents can be supported in their grief without being assigned blame for another person's choices.
units.application: If your conduct has brought grief at home, name the wrong and begin one concrete repair.

rel.note: Condemning the just is already named as detestable to the LORD.

units.notes: Punish can mean impose a fine. Striking nobles pictures misuse of coercive power against those acting uprightly.
units.summary: Punishing people for upright conduct is unjust.
units.principle: Authority is accountable for whom it penalizes and why.
units.insight: A person can help protect others from retaliation for doing what is right.
units.application: Check whether a proposed penalty is responding to a real wrong or retaliating against upright conduct.

rel.note: Restraining the lips is likewise commended as wise.

units.notes: Sparing words means holding them back. A calm spirit describes a steady temper.
units.summary: Knowledge speaks with restraint, and understanding keeps a steady temper.
units.principle: Wise restraint governs both words and reactions.
units.insight: A calm pause can give someone room to choose what deserves a reply.
units.application: When provoked, pause and answer only what needs to be addressed.

rel.note: The prudent hold back knowledge, while fools ordinarily make their folly public.

units.notes: Counted and considered describe how others perceive the silent person.
units.summary: Silence can make even a fool appear perceptive.
units.principle: Restraint can prevent folly from being put on display.
units.insight: Someone unsure of the facts can choose to listen before offering a judgment.
units.application: In a discussion you understand poorly, ask a question or listen before offering an opinion.

rel.note: The fool trusts his own judgment, while the wise heed counsel.

units.notes: The Hebrew is difficult. The NKJV pictures withdrawal that serves one's own desire and resists sound judgment.
units.summary: Withdrawing to protect our own desires can make us hostile to wise counsel.
units.principle: A desire needs examination when keeping it depends on avoiding honest counsel.
units.insight: Solitude and time to grieve can be good. The danger here is shutting out anyone who might challenge a choice.
units.application: Invite a trustworthy person to question a decision you have been keeping to yourself.

rel.note: The fool's heart likewise broadcasts folly.

units.notes: Heart here includes opinions, desires, and judgment. The contrast turns on what the fool enjoys.
units.summary: The fool would rather express his opinions than gain understanding.
units.principle: Understanding grows when listening matters more than self-display.
units.insight: Someone can change the tone of a conversation by becoming curious about what they have missed.
units.application: Ask a sincere question and hear the answer before offering your view.

rel.note: Wicked conduct likewise becomes offensive and brings shame.

units.notes: Contempt and reproach describe the scorn and disgrace that accompany dishonor.
units.summary: Wickedness brings contempt, and dishonor brings disgrace.
units.principle: How people treat what is honorable shapes the reproach their conduct brings.
units.insight: A contemptuous attitude can be addressed before it becomes a settled pattern of conduct.
units.application: Replace a contemptuous response with a direct, respectful account of the issue.

rel.note: The mouth of the righteous is likewise pictured as a well of life.

units.notes: Deep waters suggest a source hidden below the surface. A flowing brook pictures the continuing supply of wisdom.
units.summary: Speech rises from within, and wisdom supplies a flowing stream of words.
units.principle: The source of speech affects what it can supply to others.
units.insight: Helpful words often grow out of reflection that others never see.
units.application: Reflect on sound counsel before trying to give useful words to someone else.

rel.note: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the just are both detestable to the LORD.

units.notes: Showing partiality means giving someone favor because of who they are. Overthrowing the righteous means denying them justice.
units.summary: Partiality to the wicked denies justice to the righteous.
units.principle: A fair judgment turns on the merits of the case.
units.insight: Someone with influence can help ensure that an overlooked person receives a fair hearing.
units.application: Apply the same standard to a person you favor and to the person whose claim they dispute.

rel.note: The gentle answer helps reduce the anger that harsh words stir up.

units.notes: Contention means a quarrel. Calling for blows pictures words inviting a violent response.
units.summary: Reckless words invite quarrels and can provoke blows.
units.principle: Words can intensify a conflict beyond what the speaker intended.
units.insight: Someone can end an escalating exchange and seek safety before replying further.
units.application: Leave an escalating argument and return to the issue when it can be addressed safely.

rel.note: Wrongdoing in speech likewise becomes a snare for the person who practices it.

units.notes: A snare is a hidden trap. Soul here means the person's life.
units.summary: A fool can be caught and ruined by his own words.
units.principle: Unchecked speech can make a trap for the speaker.
units.insight: Telling the truth early can keep someone from compounding a false statement.
units.application: Correct a boast, false statement, or careless promise before it creates more harm.

rel.note: The project NKJV repeats the saying word for word.

units.notes: A talebearer carries gossip. Tasty trifles picture delicacies, and the inmost body pictures where words settle.
units.summary: Gossip goes down easily and can settle deeply in the hearer.
units.principle: What makes gossip appealing also helps give it influence.
units.insight: An unverified story can keep affecting a relationship even after the conversation ends.
units.application: Decline to hear or repeat a damaging story about someone who is absent.

rel.note: The overgrown field shows concretely what neglect can destroy.

units.notes: Brother describes a family likeness between neglect and destruction.
units.summary: Neglect can do the same kind of damage as active destruction.
units.principle: Leaving necessary work undone can have serious consequences for others.
units.insight: A person who cannot meet a responsibility can seek help before it is left unattended.
units.application: Identify one neglected task within your ability and take the step that prevents further damage.

rel.note: Wealth appears to the rich person as a high wall, while the LORD is the refuge of the righteous.

units.notes: The LORD's name stands for His revealed character and presence. Safety pictures being set high out of reach.
units.summary: The righteous run to the LORD as their strong tower.
units.principle: Refuge rests in the LORD Himself.
units.insight: Prayer can express trust in God's character while a person takes practical steps toward safety.
units.application: Bring a specific danger to the LORD in prayer and take a prudent step under His care.

rel.note: The earlier saying describes the real buffer wealth can give, and this verse qualifies that picture.

units.notes: Strong city repeats 10:15. In his own esteem points to the rich person's imagined defense.
units.summary: Wealth offers some protection, but its owner can imagine it to be an unassailable refuge.
units.principle: Resources are useful within limits that ultimate trust must recognize.
units.insight: A change in finances can expose what a person was counting on for security.
units.application: Use your resources responsibly and name one concern that requires trust beyond what money can secure.

rel.note: Pride and a haughty spirit likewise prepare a fall.

units.notes: Haughtiness begins in the heart. The second line also appears in 15:33.
units.summary: Haughtiness comes before destruction, and humility comes before honor.
units.principle: The posture of the heart shapes the course that follows.
units.insight: Accepting a limit can be an act of sound judgment.
units.application: Receive one correction without trying to protect your standing in the conversation.

rel.note: The first account can seem right until another person examines it.

units.notes: Hearing the matter means listening to it fully before responding.
units.summary: Answering before listening is folly and shame.
units.principle: Sound answers require a fair hearing.
units.insight: A listener can show care by making sure they have understood the matter first.
units.application: Summarize what the other person said and ask if you understood before giving your answer.

rel.note: A merry heart and a broken spirit likewise affect the whole person.

units.notes: A broken spirit is an inward life wounded or crushed. The closing question stresses how heavy that burden can be.
units.summary: Inner strength can carry someone through sickness, but a broken spirit is hard to bear.
units.principle: The inner life deserves care because it can bear or deepen a burden.
units.insight: People who are crushed need patient companionship and practical support alongside whatever care they need.
units.application: Offer concrete help to someone under strain and listen to what is hardest for them now.

rel.note: The wise likewise hear and increase in learning.

units.notes: The heart acquires and the ear seeks. Both images describe active learning.
units.summary: The prudent gain knowledge, and the wise actively listen for it.
units.principle: Wisdom continues to seek knowledge.
units.insight: Experience can deepen curiosity about what another person knows.
units.application: Ask someone with relevant experience to teach you one thing you do not yet know.

rel.note: A secret payment to bend justice shows how a gift can become corrupt.

units.notes: Makes room means opens access. The word for gift is a general term for a present.
units.summary: A gift can open doors and bring the giver before people of influence.
units.principle: Access gained through a gift calls for attention to integrity.
units.insight: A customary gift can be considered in light of what the giver expects in return.
units.application: Check whether a gift you are considering could compromise a fair decision.

rel.note: Answering before hearing the matter is likewise called folly.

units.notes: Pleading a cause evokes a dispute. Examining means questioning an account closely.
units.summary: The first account seems right until the other side is heard and examined.
units.principle: A fair hearing tests a convincing account against other evidence.
units.insight: Taking a first report seriously can go together with withholding a final judgment.
units.application: Hear the other person's account and check one disputed fact before deciding.

rel.note: The lot is also described as a decision ultimately under the LORD's rule.

units.notes: Casting lots was an ancient way to make a decision neither party controlled. Keeping the mighty apart means preventing rivals from fighting.
units.summary: An impartial means of deciding can keep powerful rivals from fighting.
units.principle: A fair procedure can settle a dispute that strength alone would decide unjustly.
units.insight: An agreed process can help where both sides are wary of the other's influence.
units.application: Agree on a fair decision process with the other party before choosing an outcome.

rel.note: Stopping strife early can prevent the barriers pictured here from growing.

units.notes: Brother can be a close relative or companion. Castle bars picture a relationship closed against further injury.
units.summary: A wrong can make a close relationship harder to repair than a fortified city is to win.
units.principle: Reconciliation starts by taking the injury seriously.
units.insight: A hurt person can be given time and room without being pressed to restore trust immediately.
units.application: Name the harm you caused without minimizing it and allow the other person time to respond.

rel.note: A person's mouth likewise bears fruit the speaker can receive.

units.notes: Fruit and produce picture a harvest from speech. Eating it means receiving the results.
units.summary: A person receives the results of what their words produce.
units.principle: Speech has consequences for the speaker as well as the hearer.
units.insight: A truthful apology can begin a different pattern after harmful speech.
units.application: Review the effect of something you said recently and repair it if it caused avoidable harm.

rel.note: Rash words wound, while the tongue of the wise brings healing.

units.notes: Power is literally hand. Eating the fruit means experiencing the consequences of habitual speech.
units.summary: Words can serve life or death, and speakers receive the fruit of how they use them.
units.principle: The real power of speech calls for responsibility and care.
units.insight: A truthful word can protect someone, and a damaging report can have consequences long after it was spoken.
units.application: Use your words to defend someone truthfully or to correct a damaging claim you have made.

rel.note: A prudent wife is likewise described as coming from the LORD.

units.notes: The Hebrew reads a wife. Obtains favor from the LORD echoes 8:35, and the theme of finding recurs at 31:10.
units.summary: Finding a good wife is a good gift from the LORD.
units.principle: Receive a good marriage as a gift and treat one's spouse accordingly.
units.insight: Marriage can be received with gratitude, and single people can be honored in their own circumstances.
units.application: If married, name a good you have received through your spouse and thank them and the LORD for it.

rel.note: Poverty can bring social contempt, which the following saying calls sin.

units.notes: Entreaties are earnest appeals. The rough answer is a harsh or blunt response.
units.summary: The poor often have to plead, while the rich can answer roughly.
units.principle: Power creates responsibility for how we answer vulnerable people.
units.insight: A person who can grant or deny help can still respond with dignity and patience.
units.application: Give a respectful, considered reply to someone who cannot insist on your help.

rel.note: Faithful friendship likewise remains loving in adversity.

units.notes: The first line is debated. The NKJV stresses showing friendliness. Other translations warn that having many companions can lead to ruin. Sticks means holds fast.
units.summary: A loyal friend can hold closer than a brother.
units.principle: The depth of a friendship is seen in its faithful presence.
units.insight: Christ's faithful friendship gives believers grounds for trust when human companionship falls short.
units.application: Thank Christ for His faithful friendship and show up in a specific way for a friend who needs you.

rel.note: The poor person of integrity is preferred to a rich person whose ways are crooked.

units.notes: Integrity is wholeness in conduct.
units.summary: An honest life is better than a life marked by crooked speech.
units.principle: Character has greater worth than social advantage.
units.insight: A person's income gives little basis for assessing their integrity.
units.application: Refuse one gain that would require misleading someone.

rel.note: Diligent planning and haste lead to different outcomes.

units.notes: Soul can include desire. Hurrying feet picture acting before one knows the way.
units.summary: Desire needs knowledge, and haste can lead a person astray.
units.principle: Sound knowledge should guide the pace of action.
units.insight: A pause can protect someone from acting on an attractive but poorly understood plan.
units.application: Check one important fact before committing to a rushed decision.

rel.note: Folly likewise deceives the person who fails to examine their course.

units.notes: Frets means rages or resents. Folly first twists the person's own course.
units.summary: Folly can wreck a person's course and then blame God for the result.
units.principle: Owning our choices allows us to correct what lies within our responsibility.
units.insight: Someone can bring pain honestly to God while examining their own choices where relevant.
units.application: Name one consequence you helped bring about and take a step to repair it.

rel.note: The parallel observation is followed by a warning against despising one's neighbor.

units.notes: Friends here include people drawn by material advantage.
units.summary: Wealth attracts company, while poverty can lead to isolation.
units.principle: Faithfulness is tested when companionship offers little advantage.
units.insight: A friend whose resources have dwindled may especially need dependable companionship.
units.application: Keep in touch with someone whose changed circumstances have left them isolated.

rel.note: The first line repeats, and the second intensifies the outcome.

units.notes: A false witness gives dishonest testimony. The second line extends the warning to lies more broadly.
units.summary: False testimony and lies bring accountability.
units.principle: Justice requires honesty from those who give evidence.
units.insight: A truthful correction can protect someone harmed by an inaccurate account.
units.application: Correct a misleading account you have given before anyone relies on it further.

rel.note: Wealth similarly attracts friends, while poverty can cost companionship.

units.notes: Nobility can refer to rank or generosity. Entreating favor means seeking goodwill.
units.summary: People seek the favor of the influential and gather around gift-givers.
units.principle: The benefits a person offers can attract company without creating loyalty.
units.insight: A generous person can value friends who remain when there is nothing to gain.
units.application: Do one good for a friend from whom you expect no return.

rel.note: Faithful friendship remains present precisely in adversity.

units.notes: Hate can mean shun or reject. The Hebrew of the third line is difficult.
units.summary: Poverty can bring abandonment even by family and friends.
units.principle: Need tests the faithfulness of family and friendship.
units.insight: The person whose appeals go unheard deserves attention and practical care.
units.application: Answer a request for help that others have overlooked, within your means.

rel.note: Holding firmly to instruction likewise serves life.

units.notes: Gets wisdom is literally acquires heart or judgment. Soul here means one's life.
units.summary: Seeking and keeping wisdom serves one's own life.
units.principle: Wisdom benefits those who retain and practice it.
units.insight: Seeking sound counsel can be a constructive act of care for oneself.
units.application: Choose one piece of sound counsel to retain and practice this week.

rel.note: The earlier saying says that the liar will not escape.

units.notes: The first line repeats 19:5. Perish intensifies its warning.
units.summary: The course of false testimony and lying ends in ruin.
units.principle: Falsehood is a destructive way to seek escape.
units.insight: A lie can still be confessed and corrected before it causes further damage.
units.application: Withdraw a claim you know to be false and correct it with the people who heard it.

rel.note: A wise servant can rightly receive authority that a shameful son fails to merit.

units.notes: Luxury pictures ease or indulgence. A servant ruling princes pictures an unexpected reversal of rank.
units.summary: Resources and authority require character suited to their use.
units.principle: A role or privilege is fitting when its holder can carry it wisely.
units.insight: Someone can be evaluated for responsibility by judgment and conduct as well as position.
units.application: Assess one assignment by the judgment it requires and the character of the person entrusted with it.

rel.note: The prudent person likewise covers a slight rather than immediately displaying anger.

units.notes: Overlook literally means pass over. Discretion slows the onset of anger.
units.summary: Discretion slows anger, and overlooking an offense can be honorable.
units.principle: Patience gives room for a proportionate response.
units.insight: A minor slight can be let go, and ongoing harm can be addressed responsibly.
units.application: Pause after an offense and decide whether to release it or address it calmly.

rel.note: Royal favor is likewise pictured as rain that gives life.

units.notes: A lion's roar signals danger. Dew sustains vegetation in a dry climate.
units.summary: A king's anger can be dangerous, while his favor can refresh like dew.
units.principle: Power magnifies both anger and favor.
units.insight: A person with authority can choose to use it in ways that sustain others.
units.application: Use your influence to give timely help rather than venting anger at someone who depends on you.

rel.note: The same dripping image describes the wear of persistent contention.

units.notes: Continual dripping pictures the steady wear of repeated conflict.
units.summary: Folly and persistent conflict can wear down a household from within.
units.principle: Repeated contention can do damage beyond any one quarrel.
units.insight: Both spouses can examine what they contribute to a recurring conflict.
units.application: Address one recurring source of friction calmly and take responsibility for your part in it.

rel.note: Finding a wife is described as receiving a good gift and the LORD's favor.

units.notes: Houses and riches can pass by inheritance. Prudent describes a person of insight and good judgment.
units.summary: Property can be inherited, while a prudent wife is a gift from the LORD.
units.principle: The value of a wise spouse exceeds what material inheritance can supply.
units.insight: Gratitude for a spouse can take the form of recognizing their judgment and care.
units.application: If married, thank your spouse and the LORD for one way their judgment has helped you.

rel.note: Repeated extensions of sleep likewise lead toward poverty.

units.notes: Deep sleep pictures the grip of habitual inactivity. An idle person is pictured as slack in will.
units.summary: Habitual idleness can deepen inactivity and lead to hunger.
units.principle: Repeated neglect can become harder to interrupt over time.
units.insight: Needed rest and genuine inability deserve care, while an avoidable delay can be addressed in small steps.
units.application: Begin one task within your ability at a specific time today.

rel.note: Treating the commandment with reverence is contrasted with despising instruction.

units.notes: Keeping the commandment and keeping one's soul use the same verb. Soul means life.
units.summary: Keeping God's instruction guards life, while neglecting one's course leads toward death.
units.principle: Obedience serves life by directing the way we walk.
units.insight: A person can recover direction by giving attention to a command they have set aside.
units.application: Act on one command you have been neglecting in a recurring choice.

rel.note: Mercy to the needy likewise honors their Maker.

units.notes: Lending to the LORD pictures God taking a gift to the poor as done to Him.
units.summary: The LORD receives kindness to the poor as service to Himself.
units.principle: God honors practical mercy toward people in need.
units.insight: Someone can give freely without putting pressure on the recipient to return the favor.
units.application: Meet a concrete need within your means without expecting repayment from the recipient.

rel.note: Loving a child includes taking responsibility for timely discipline.

units.notes: Chasten includes training and correction. The second line may warn against neglect that leads to ruin or anger that causes harm.
units.summary: Give timely correction that serves a child's growth and safety.
units.principle: Loving correction is consistent, proportionate, and directed toward growth.
units.insight: A parent can regain composure before addressing a child's conduct.
units.application: State an expectation calmly and choose a safe, proportionate consequence that helps the child learn.

rel.note: Habitual anger likewise stirs up strife and leads to repeated wrongdoing.

units.notes: Great wrath means a hot, uncontrolled temper. Repeated rescue pictures shielding someone from recurring consequences.
units.summary: Repeatedly shielding a hot-tempered person from consequences leaves the pattern intact.
units.principle: Help is most useful when it addresses the conduct that keeps creating the crisis.
units.insight: People can offer help that supports change while preserving safety and accountability.
units.application: Set one boundary that protects others and leaves a recurring consequence with the person responsible.

rel.note: The wise hear and increase in learning.

units.notes: Counsel is advice. Latter days means the later years of life.
units.summary: Receive counsel today so that you grow wiser over time.
units.principle: A teachable present prepares for a wiser future.
units.insight: A correction can be valued for what it will build well beyond the present moment.
units.application: Ask a trusted adviser about one habit that will matter over the long term and act on the answer.

rel.note: Human planning likewise stands alongside the LORD's direction of actual steps.

units.notes: The heart holds plans and purposes. Stand means endure or prevail.
units.summary: People make many plans, and the LORD's counsel will stand.
units.principle: Plan faithfully while leaving the outcome in God's hands.
units.insight: A change in plans can be met with prayer and a responsible next step.
units.application: Commit one plan to the LORD and identify the step you can take while remaining open to redirection.

rel.note: The poor person of integrity is likewise preferred to someone whose lips are crooked.

units.notes: Kindness includes loyal love. The first line can describe what people desire or what makes a person desirable.
units.summary: Loyal kindness is desirable, and a poor person is better than a liar.
units.principle: Truthful loyalty matters more than material advantage.
units.insight: A person of modest means can be valued for their faithful kindness.
units.application: Honor someone for a specific kindness and keep a promise they are relying on.

rel.note: The fear of the LORD likewise gives refuge and turns people away from deadly traps.

units.notes: Abide can mean lodge or spend the night. Satisfaction describes contented rest.
units.summary: The fear of the LORD leads toward life and contented rest.
units.principle: Reverence gives a sound basis for trust and contentment amid uncertain circumstances.
units.insight: Hardship gives no reason to accuse someone of lacking reverence for God.
units.application: Bring one worry before the LORD and practice one act of obedience within your control.

rel.note: The same picture describes a lazy man wearied by lifting his hand to his mouth.

units.notes: The bowl and the unmoving hand form a deliberate exaggeration.
units.summary: The lazy man leaves even a simple task unfinished.
units.principle: Starting a task does little good if avoidable neglect prevents completion.
units.insight: A task within reach can become useful once its last step is taken.
units.application: Finish one small task you have already started.

rel.note: Punishing a scoffer teaches the simple, while instruction brings knowledge to the wise.

units.notes: The simple are uncommitted and can learn from what happens to others.
units.summary: The simple can learn from another's consequences, while the discerning learn from rebuke.
units.principle: Teachability allows a person to learn before harder consequences arrive.
units.insight: People can learn without having to repeat someone else's mistake.
units.application: Draw one concrete lesson from a rebuke or from a consequence you have seen.

rel.note: Robbing a father or mother is likewise treated as destructive wrongdoing.

units.notes: Mistreat can include assaulting or plundering. Chasing away pictures driving a mother from her place of security.
units.summary: Mistreating parents and driving them away brings shame.
units.principle: Family ties heighten the responsibility to treat vulnerable relatives justly.
units.insight: A parent harmed by a child may need protection and practical support.
units.application: Take a concrete step to protect or restore what a vulnerable parent is being denied.

rel.note: The learner is likewise urged to hold on to instruction.

units.notes: The NKJV reads this as a warning about ceasing to listen. The Hebrew has another possible reading about misleading instruction.
