units.summary: When you stop listening to sound instruction, you can drift away from knowledge.
units.principle: Continued attention helps keep the learner on course.
units.insight: A person who has drifted can resume learning through one regular habit.
units.application: Restore one regular occasion to listen to sound teaching and put it into practice.

rel.note: A true witness saves lives, while a deceitful witness speaks lies.

units.notes: A disreputable witness is corrupt. Devouring iniquity pictures taking in wrongdoing greedily.
units.summary: A corrupt witness scorns justice, and the wicked take in wrongdoing eagerly.
units.principle: Truthful evidence protects justice from people who treat it as an obstacle.
units.insight: A disputed claim calls for careful verification when a witness has reason to twist it.
units.application: Check whether the evidence you plan to give is complete and accurate.

rel.note: A discerning person can learn from a rebuke that a fool may resist even after severe consequences.

units.notes: Judgments are penalties. Beatings picture severe consequences faced by fools.
units.summary: Scoffing and persistent folly face consequences even when correction is refused.
units.principle: Scorn cannot put a person beyond accountability.
units.insight: A person can still turn and receive correction before the pattern deepens.
units.application: Act on one sound correction before repeating the conduct it addresses.

rel.note: The fuller portrait traces the wounds, confusion, and repeated craving of drunkenness.

units.notes: Wine and strong drink are pictured as a mocker and a brawler.
units.summary: Being led astray by alcohol is folly.
units.principle: Wisdom takes seriously whatever weakens judgment and provokes harm.
units.insight: Someone who repeatedly loses judgment when drinking can seek support and set a firm boundary.
units.application: Identify a situation where alcohol has impaired your judgment and decide how you will avoid repeating it.

rel.note: The king's wrath is likewise compared to the roar of a lion.

units.notes: A lion's roar signals danger. Sinning against one's own life means putting it in jeopardy.
units.summary: Provoking royal anger can put a person's life in danger.
units.principle: Wisdom weighs the stakes of a confrontation.
units.insight: Caution around volatile authority can coexist with speaking truth through a safe channel.
units.application: Before confronting someone with coercive power, consider the safest responsible way to raise the issue.

rel.note: The earlier saying urges stopping contention before it breaks out.

units.notes: Ceasing from strife can mean avoiding or ending a quarrel.
units.summary: Avoiding a quarrel is honorable, while any fool can start one.
units.principle: Restraint is a better claim to honor than picking a fight.
units.insight: Letting an argument end can preserve dignity even when disagreement remains.
units.application: Stop one escalating exchange and return to the issue when it can be addressed calmly.

rel.note: The ant gathers supplies while the opportunity is open.

units.notes: Winter here is the cooler plowing season after the early rains.
units.summary: Skipping work in its season can leave a person empty-handed at harvest.
units.principle: The right time to prepare comes before the need is visible.
units.insight: Genuine obstacles call for support, while an avoidable delay can be addressed now.
units.application: Start one necessary preparation before its opportunity closes.

rel.note: Human words are likewise pictured as coming from deep waters.

units.notes: Counsel can mean a purpose or plan. Deep water pictures a motive that is hard to reach.
units.summary: Understanding draws out purposes that lie deep in the heart.
units.principle: Good listening makes room for what is beneath the first answer.
units.insight: People may explain their concerns more clearly when given time and a thoughtful question.
units.application: Ask a patient follow-up question about what a person hopes to achieve and listen fully.

rel.note: The faithful friend shows loyalty by remaining present in adversity.

units.notes: Goodness here includes loyal love. The question highlights the rarity of proven faithfulness.
units.summary: Many advertise loyalty, while proven faithfulness is harder to find.
units.principle: Faithfulness is demonstrated over time.
units.insight: A quiet record of keeping commitments can matter more than an impressive claim.
units.application: Keep a specific promise without drawing attention to yourself for doing it.

rel.note: The benefits of the righteous course likewise reach their descendants.

units.notes: Walking pictures sustained conduct. After him points to the next generation.
units.summary: A life of integrity can bless the next generation.
units.principle: Integrity leaves an example others can build on.
units.insight: A caregiver can model a faithful choice without trying to control every outcome.
units.application: Show a younger person one way to keep a promise when it costs something.

rel.note: The wise king likewise winnows the wicked, then acts on what he discovers.

units.notes: The king sits as judge. Scattering evokes winnowing grain to remove chaff.
units.summary: A king exercising just judgment separates wrongdoing from what is right.
units.principle: Authority serves justice through careful examination.
units.insight: Those who review a decision can protect people by scrutinizing the evidence fairly.
units.application: Check one claim closely before deciding a matter under your authority.

rel.note: Confessing and forsaking sin opens the way to mercy.

units.notes: The question expects the answer no one. Made clean stresses the claim of self-produced purity.
units.summary: No one can honestly claim to have made their own heart clean.
units.principle: Cleansing is received from God rather than claimed as a personal achievement.
units.insight: An upright life can include candid confession and humble dependence on God's mercy.
units.application: Confess a specific sin to God and take a step to forsake it.

rel.note: Dishonest scales are detestable to the LORD, and a just weight delights Him.

units.notes: Diverse weights and measures mean inconsistent standards used to cheat.
units.summary: The LORD detests dishonest standards in trade.
units.principle: Fair trade uses the same honest standard on both sides.
units.insight: People who cannot independently check a transaction still deserve a fair measure.
units.application: Check one quantity, fee, or measure you set for accuracy and consistency.

rel.note: The adult's steady walk of integrity can bless children who see it.

units.notes: Being known by deeds means conduct makes character recognizable.
units.summary: Even a child's conduct gives evidence of their developing character.
units.principle: Actions give clearer evidence than labels or appearances.
units.insight: A single mistake can be addressed without treating it as the child's settled identity.
units.application: Name a specific upright action you saw a child take and encourage them to repeat it.

rel.note: The ear of the wise actively seeks knowledge.

units.notes: Ear and eye name the faculties for listening and seeing.
units.summary: The LORD made the faculties by which people hear and see.
units.principle: God's gifts are meant to be used attentively.
units.insight: Paying attention can be an act of gratitude for capacities God gives.
units.application: Use one capacity God has given you to notice a need or receive instruction today.

rel.note: The repeated choice of more sleep likewise leads toward want.

units.notes: Loving sleep pictures preferring ease to needed work. Opening the eyes pictures alertness.
units.summary: Habitual neglect can lead to poverty, while alert effort helps provide bread.
units.principle: Diligence begins by attending to what needs doing.
units.insight: Needed rest can be planned alongside work a person is able to do.
units.application: Set a workable time to rise and begin one neglected responsibility.

rel.note: The LORD's concern for fair measures likewise applies to honesty in the marketplace.

units.notes: The buyer repeats bad to disparage the goods. Boasting after leaving reveals a changed account.
units.summary: A buyer can belittle goods to win a bargain and praise the deal once it is done.
units.principle: A bargain does not justify misrepresenting the goods.
units.insight: A fair negotiation can acknowledge real value while stating what one can pay.
units.application: Describe the value and any flaws honestly in your next negotiation.

rel.note: Righteous speech is likewise compared to choice silver.

units.notes: Gold and rubies represent wealth. Lips of knowledge means informed, useful speech.
units.summary: Knowledgeable speech is a jewel of great value.
units.principle: Good judgment gives speech lasting worth.
units.insight: A brief, reliable word can help someone more than an expensive gift.
units.application: Share one accurate, helpful insight with someone who needs direction.

rel.note: The same advice about taking a garment as security recurs there.

units.notes: A surety guarantees another person's debt. A garment could serve as collateral. The second line has a textual alternative about foreigners.
units.summary: A rash guarantee exposes the guarantor's own property to loss.
units.principle: Pledging for another person can put one's own necessities at risk.
units.insight: A friend can be helped directly within one's means without a guarantee of their debt.
units.application: Avoid a rash guarantee and consider help you can afford to give directly.

rel.note: Folly likewise offers sweet stolen food and hides the deadly outcome.

units.notes: Bread means food or gain. Gravel pictures the painful aftermath of deceit.
units.summary: Dishonest gain tastes sweet at first and turns painful afterward.
units.principle: The first pleasure of deceit gives a poor account of its final cost.
units.insight: The attraction of a quick gain can be admitted honestly while its cost is weighed.
units.application: Give up a gain that depends on a dishonest account and make restitution where needed.

rel.note: Plans likewise fail without counsel and are established with many advisers.

units.notes: Established means made firm. War raises the stakes of the need for advice.
units.summary: Sound counsel strengthens plans, especially when much is at stake.
units.principle: The greater the stakes, the more a plan needs careful counsel.
units.insight: Inviting another perspective early can reveal a risk before it becomes costly.
units.application: Ask trusted advisers to test a major decision before committing to it.

rel.note: A gossip exposes confidences, while a faithful person guards them.

units.notes: A talebearer spreads confidential stories. The final phrase can describe flattery or loose speech.
units.summary: A talebearer reveals secrets, so be careful about what you entrust to them.
units.principle: Trust should be informed by how a person handles confidences.
units.insight: A person's pattern with others' information can help you judge whether they will protect yours.
units.application: Decline to share private information with someone who repeatedly spreads it.

rel.note: Harming one's parents likewise brings shame and reproach.

units.notes: Cursing a parent expresses contempt or wishes harm. An extinguished lamp pictures the loss of life or hope.
units.summary: Cursing one's parents sets a course toward darkness.
units.principle: Family bonds give words a weight that contempt ignores.
units.insight: Respectful speech can coexist with boundaries where family relationships are unsafe.
units.application: Replace a contemptuous remark about a parent with a truthful, measured statement.

rel.note: Hastening to be rich likewise brings consequences.

units.notes: Inheritance is family property. The wording can emphasize haste or grasping greed.
units.summary: An inheritance seized in haste can end without blessing.
units.principle: The manner of acquiring wealth affects the good it can do.
units.insight: Family resources can be handled patiently and transparently even when people want an immediate outcome.
units.application: Slow down a decision about shared family resources and seek a fair process before claiming a share.

rel.note: The later saying likewise rejects a decision to repay another person in kind.

units.notes: Recompense here means pay back a wrong. Waiting means entrusting the matter to the LORD.
units.summary: Leave personal vengeance to the LORD and trust Him for deliverance.
units.principle: Justice is served by responsible action rather than private revenge.
units.insight: Someone who has been harmed can seek protection and accountability without retaliating.
units.application: Set aside a plan to retaliate and take a lawful step toward protection or accountability if needed.

rel.note: The earlier verse condemns dishonest weights and measures together.

units.notes: Diverse weights are unequal standards kept for dishonest use.
units.summary: The LORD detests unequal standards and dishonest scales.
units.principle: Integrity in commerce requires honest measurement.
units.insight: Accurate dealing matters even when a discrepancy would probably go unnoticed.
units.application: Correct one hidden discrepancy in a transaction you control.

rel.note: People make real plans, and the LORD directs their actual steps.

units.notes: Steps are the course actually taken. The question stresses the limits of a person's understanding.
units.summary: The LORD directs our steps beyond what we can fully understand.
units.principle: Human judgment is limited within God's direction.
units.insight: Uncertainty can be brought to God while a person still takes the next responsible step.
units.application: Make the best responsible decision you can and entrust what you cannot foresee to the LORD.

rel.note: Seeking counsel before carrying out a plan illustrates the value of reflection before commitment.

units.notes: Devoting something as holy means setting it apart to God. The snare is the commitment made before reflection.
units.summary: Consider a vow to God before making it.
units.principle: Reverence includes care for what we promise.
units.insight: A pause can protect a sincere commitment from being made in a moment of pressure.
units.application: Think through the cost and terms of a commitment before you make it to God.

rel.note: The king already appears winnowing evil through discerning judgment.

units.notes: Sifting separates grain from chaff. A threshing wheel pictures forceful judgment.
units.summary: A wise ruler identifies wrongdoing and acts against it.
units.principle: Just authority separates wrongdoing from the people it protects.
units.insight: Decisive action is best grounded in a careful judgment about what actually happened.
units.application: Review the evidence before taking proportionate action against wrongdoing under your responsibility.

rel.note: The LORD likewise weighs inward motives that people may overlook.

units.notes: Spirit here can refer to human breath or inner awareness. The lamp searches by bringing hidden things to light.
units.summary: The human spirit is the LORD's lamp for bringing the inner life to light.
units.principle: God's searching reaches the hidden parts of the inner life.
units.insight: An uneasy conscience can prompt honest examination before God.
units.application: Bring a troubling motive to God and examine it in light of His instruction.

rel.note: Righteousness is likewise said to establish a throne.

units.notes: Mercy and lovingkindness both express loyal love. Truth includes faithfulness.
units.summary: Loyal love and faithfulness uphold a ruler's throne.
units.principle: Stable leadership depends on character as well as power.
units.insight: People in authority can build trust by keeping commitments and treating others with care.
units.application: Keep a commitment to the people affected by a decision you oversee.

rel.note: Gray hair is also called a crown when found in the way of righteousness.

units.notes: Strength pictures the vigor of youth. A gray head marks the years of older people.
units.summary: Youth has the glory of strength, and age has its own splendor.
units.principle: Honor fits the real gifts of different stages of life.
units.insight: Different generations can value what each has to contribute.
units.application: Use one strength you have to serve someone of another generation and learn from what they offer.

rel.note: A wise person can learn from a rebuke more readily than a fool learns from blows.

units.notes: The Hebrew wording is difficult. The NKJV pictures painful blows or stripes reaching the inner person.
units.summary: Painful correction can reach deeply enough to change a person's course.
units.principle: Good correction seeks inward change and restoration.
units.insight: A painful consequence can be faced honestly with help rather than used to justify causing pain.
units.application: Reflect on one painful consequence and change the conduct that helped bring it about.

rel.note: The LORD likewise directs the steps of people who make their own plans.

units.notes: Rivers here evoke irrigation channels a farmer can redirect.
units.summary: The LORD can direct even a king's heart.
units.principle: Human authority remains under God's authority.
units.insight: People living under powerful leaders can pray and act faithfully without treating those leaders as ultimate.
units.application: Pray for a leader's decision and take a responsible step where you can influence it.

rel.note: The LORD likewise weighs the spirits of those who see their own ways as pure.

units.notes: Weighing pictures an exact assessment. The heart includes motives.
units.summary: Our ways may seem right to us, while the LORD weighs our hearts.
units.principle: God's assessment goes deeper than self-approval.
units.insight: A trusted question can help bring a hidden motive into view.
units.application: Ask God to show you the motive behind one decision you have been defending.

rel.note: The later saying exposes sacrifice brought by someone persisting in wickedness.

units.notes: Sacrifice was an appointed act of Israel's worship.
units.summary: Doing righteousness and justice pleases the LORD more than sacrifice.
units.principle: Worship belongs with upright conduct.
units.insight: A worshiper can bring a specific injustice before God and begin addressing it.
units.application: Correct one unfair practice that conflicts with what you profess in worship.

rel.note: A proud look is listed among the things the LORD hates.

units.notes: Haughty eyes express arrogance. The word rendered plowing can also be read as lamp.
units.summary: Pride and wickedness can mark both a person's appearance and everyday work.
units.principle: Inward pride affects the conduct it governs.
units.insight: Ordinary responsibilities give a person a place to notice and correct contempt.
units.application: Examine one routine task for a way you are treating someone as beneath you.

rel.note: Hasty steps likewise lead astray when desire runs ahead of knowledge.

units.notes: The diligent combine steady effort with forethought. Haste describes rushing without it.
units.summary: Diligent planning tends toward plenty, while haste tends toward want.
units.principle: Diligence includes planning before acting.
units.insight: Some setbacks can be prevented by slowing down enough to ask a good question.
units.application: Before rushing a decision, write down its likely costs and ask someone to review them.

rel.note: Dishonest wealth dwindles, while steady work can build resources.

units.notes: Fleeting fantasy evokes vapor driven away. The final phrase connects deceptive gain to death.
units.summary: Wealth gained by lying is fleeting and leads toward ruin.
units.principle: Judge gain by its source and destination.
units.insight: A dishonest gain can be surrendered before it does further harm.
units.application: Correct a false claim you have used to obtain an advantage.

rel.note: The pit and stone images likewise show harm returning on the one who sets it in motion.

units.notes: Destroy can convey being swept away. Refusal makes the choice deliberate.
units.summary: Violence can sweep away those who refuse to do justice.
units.principle: People can be brought down by the harm they choose to practice.
units.insight: An entrenched pattern can still be interrupted by taking responsibility for a specific wrong.
units.application: Stop one harmful practice and take a fair step to repair its effects.

rel.note: Integrity guides the upright, while crooked dealing brings ruin.

units.notes: Way means conduct. The exact Hebrew behind guilty is debated.
units.summary: The guilty take crooked paths, while the pure do what is right.
units.principle: Integrity gives conduct a consistent direction.
units.insight: A person can begin to straighten a course by ending one evasion.
units.application: Replace one evasive explanation with a candid account of what you did.

rel.note: The later saying repeats the contrast between the housetop corner and a contentious home.

units.notes: A roof corner was cramped and exposed. Contentious describes a pattern of quarreling.
units.summary: Peace in a cramped place is better than comfort in a home filled with quarrels.
units.principle: A home's peace is worth more than its space or comforts.
units.insight: Both spouses can examine their own contribution to recurring strife.
units.application: Take responsibility for one recurring provocation and choose a calmer way to raise the issue.

rel.note: Showing mercy to the poor is blessed, while despising a neighbor is sin.

units.notes: Soul includes desire. Finding no favor means receiving no goodwill or mercy.
units.summary: A desire for evil can leave even a neighbor without mercy.
units.principle: What the heart wants shapes how it treats neighbors.
units.insight: People closest to us often bear the effects of what we privately cultivate.
units.application: Identify one neighbor you have treated harshly and offer a specific act of kindness.

rel.note: The simple likewise learn from a scoffer's punishment, while the discerning learn from rebuke.

units.notes: The simple are uncommitted and easily led. The scoffer resists correction.
units.summary: The simple can learn from consequences, and the wise learn directly from instruction.
units.principle: Teachability lets people learn earlier.
units.insight: A learner can become wiser without having to repeat another person's failure.
units.application: Take one practical lesson from sound instruction or from a consequence you have witnessed.

rel.note: The LORD likewise tears down the proud person's house while protecting the vulnerable.

units.notes: The NKJV understands the Righteous One as God. Some translations take the subject as a righteous person.
units.summary: The righteous God sees wickedness clearly and judges it justly.
units.principle: God's judgment accords with what He knows and sees.
units.insight: People who cannot see how a wrong will be addressed can still entrust it to God's judgment.
units.application: Bring a wrong before God and choose an upright response while leaving final judgment to Him.

rel.note: Showing kindness to the poor is received by the LORD as service to Him.

units.notes: Shutting the ears pictures a deliberate refusal to hear a plea.
units.summary: Those who refuse to hear the poor may find themselves unheard.
units.principle: Mercy begins by hearing people who lack power to demand help.
units.insight: A person's unanswered plea calls for care, even when we cannot explain their circumstances.
units.application: Listen to a plea you would usually pass over and respond with one practical act.

rel.note: Accepting a concealed payment to pervert justice is explicitly condemned.

units.notes: Behind the back pictures a concealed payment. The first gift is also given privately.
units.summary: Private gifts can quiet anger, and corrupt payments can appear effective too.
units.principle: An effective gesture still needs to be judged by its purpose.
units.insight: A conciliatory gesture can be offered openly about its purpose and without buying a decision.
units.application: Consider whether a gift repairs a relationship or improperly influences a decision before giving it.

rel.note: The same line about ruin for evildoers follows the LORD's strength for the upright.

units.notes: The first line can refer to doing justice or seeing justice done.
units.summary: Justice delights the upright and brings ruin to evildoers.
units.principle: Our response to justice reveals what we value.
units.insight: A fair outcome may be worth welcoming even when it costs an advantage.
units.application: Support one fair outcome even if it does not favor you.

rel.note: Ceasing to hear instruction likewise leads to straying.

units.notes: Wandering suggests drifting off the path. Rest among the dead is an ironic destination.
units.summary: Drifting from understanding can end among the dead.
units.principle: Direction matters even when the drift is gradual.
units.insight: A person can turn back before a small departure becomes habitual.
units.application: Name one step taking you away from sound instruction and reverse it.

rel.note: Excessive consumption likewise leads toward poverty.

units.notes: Wine and oil evoke costly enjoyment. Loving pleasure describes making it a governing aim.
units.summary: Making pleasure the governing aim of life can lead to poverty.
units.principle: Appetite needs limits when it starts directing the whole budget.
units.insight: Enjoyment can have a healthy place alongside limits and responsibilities.
units.application: Reduce one recurring luxury that crowds out a real obligation.

rel.note: The righteous are delivered from trouble that comes to the wicked instead.

units.notes: A ransom secures release or takes another's place. Its precise force here is debated.
units.summary: The wicked can bear the trouble from which the upright are delivered.
units.principle: God can reverse the outcome the wicked intended.
units.insight: God's justice and Christ's gracious suffering can be considered together without confusing the two pictures.
units.application: Refuse retaliation and entrust a wrong to God's justice while acting uprightly.

rel.note: The roof-corner saying makes the same comparison with a less extreme image.

units.notes: The wilderness intensifies the exposed roof image in 21:9. Anger adds to continual quarreling.
units.summary: Even wilderness solitude can seem better than a home ruled by angry quarrels.
units.principle: Household peace depends on how people handle anger and disagreement.
units.insight: Persistent conflict calls for honest attention and safe support where needed.
units.application: Stop one repeated angry exchange and seek a safe setting to address the underlying issue.

rel.note: The ant likewise gathers supplies ahead of need.

units.notes: Oil was a useful household supply. Squandering pictures swallowing what comes in.
units.summary: The wise preserve useful resources, while fools consume what they have.
units.principle: Wisdom makes present resources serve future responsibilities.
units.insight: A small reserve can give a household room to respond to a future need.
units.application: Set aside a portion of one resource for a foreseeable need.

rel.note: Righteousness likewise leads to life.

units.notes: Following means pursuing deliberately. Mercy includes loyal love.
units.summary: Pursuing righteousness and mercy leads toward life and honor.
units.principle: The ends of a life reflect what it deliberately pursues.
units.insight: Good conduct can be pursued for its own sake without calculating immediate recognition.
units.application: Choose one action that combines fair dealing with kindness.

rel.note: Wisdom and counsel likewise provide strength for difficult undertakings.

units.notes: Scaling pictures climbing a fortified wall. The stronghold is what the defenders trusted.
units.summary: Wisdom can overcome what strength alone trusts to protect it.
units.principle: Sound strategy can accomplish what brute force cannot.
units.insight: An obstacle can be approached by reconsidering the method rather than applying more pressure.
units.application: Ask for a wiser approach to one problem you have been trying to solve by force of effort.

rel.note: Guarding the mouth likewise preserves life, while unchecked speech brings ruin.

units.notes: Guarding pictures a sentry at a gate. Soul means the person's life.
units.summary: Guarding speech helps keep one's life from trouble.
units.principle: Watchfulness over words is watchfulness over consequences.
units.insight: A pause can protect both the speaker and the listener.
units.application: Before replying under pressure, decide which words are necessary and truthful.

rel.note: The earlier portrait shows how the scoffer and the wise respond to correction.

units.notes: The name Scoffer describes a settled pattern. Pride is repeated for emphasis.
units.summary: The scoffer acts out of arrogant pride.
units.principle: Pride turns into scoffing when it treats correction with contempt.
units.insight: Recognizing contempt for advice gives a person a chance to become teachable.
units.application: Hear out one criticism you would otherwise dismiss with mockery.

rel.note: The lazy man likewise craves without obtaining what he wants.

units.notes: Hands stand for work. Refuse locates the problem in avoidable unwillingness.
units.summary: Desire can become destructive when a person refuses the work needed to meet it.
units.principle: Wanting a result cannot do the work that produces it.
units.insight: Genuine inability calls for help, while avoidable refusal can be addressed with a manageable step.
units.application: Put one specific period of effort toward a task you are able to do.

rel.note: The generous person is likewise pictured as refreshing others.

units.notes: The subject likely continues the lazy man of 21:25. Gives and does not spare pictures openhandedness.
units.summary: Persistent craving grasps, while righteousness gives freely.
units.principle: A life directed toward others uses resources differently from a life ruled by craving.
units.insight: Generosity can start with a manageable act of sharing.
units.application: Share something useful that you can afford to give without expecting a return.

rel.note: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable, while the prayer of the upright delights God.

units.notes: Abomination names what the LORD detests. Wicked intent makes the offense more serious.
units.summary: The LORD detests sacrifice joined to wickedness, especially when it serves a wicked plan.
units.principle: Worship should express a life willing to obey.
units.insight: A person can turn from a wrong and bring it to God honestly rather than using worship to cover it.
units.application: Set aside an attempt to justify a wrong through religious activity and take a step of repentance.

rel.note: True and deceitful witnesses are contrasted by the effects of their words.

units.notes: The second line is difficult. The Hebrew leaves the object of hears unstated.
units.summary: False testimony comes to ruin, while a carefully heard account can stand.
units.principle: Reliable testimony depends on attending carefully to the facts.
units.insight: A witness can acknowledge limits in what they actually heard or saw.
units.application: Separate direct knowledge from assumption before offering testimony.

rel.note: The prudent examine their way, while folly deceives.

units.notes: Hardening the face pictures brazen defiance. The second line can convey establishing or considering one's way.
units.summary: The wicked put on a bold face, while the upright attend to the course they take.
units.principle: Integrity gives a sounder basis for confidence than a show of defiance.
units.insight: Someone can stop defending a bad course and examine it honestly.
units.application: Check whether your confidence rests on a well-considered course or on refusing to reconsider it.

rel.note: Many human plans stand alongside the LORD's counsel, which prevails.

units.notes: Wisdom, understanding, and counsel name abilities Proverbs usually commends.
units.summary: No wisdom, understanding, or counsel can prevail against the LORD.
units.principle: Human counsel is accountable to God's wisdom.
units.insight: Good advice can be received gratefully and still tested against what God asks.
units.application: Review one recommendation in light of God's instruction before putting it into practice.

rel.note: Responsible human planning likewise stands alongside the LORD's direction.

units.notes: The horse represents military preparation. Deliverance is the victory or rescue needed in battle.
units.summary: Prepare responsibly and trust the LORD for deliverance.
units.principle: Resources serve a purpose, while God remains the source of deliverance.
units.insight: Preparation can go together with prayer and freedom from trying to control the outcome.
units.application: Make the preparations within your responsibility and entrust the outcome to the LORD.

rel.note: The gracious woman retains honor, while the ruthless retain riches.

units.notes: Name means reputation. Loving favor is goodwill earned through character.
units.summary: Choose a good name and trustworthy relationships over riches.
units.principle: Trust is worth more than a gain that would destroy it.
units.insight: A damaged reputation can begin to be repaired through honest conduct.
units.application: Decline a gain that would require breaking someone's trust.

rel.note: The LORD gives light to the eyes of the poor person and the oppressor alike.

units.notes: The shared ground of rich and poor is that the LORD made both.
units.summary: The same LORD made the rich and the poor.
units.principle: Human dignity rests on God's creating work.
units.insight: People can be heard and treated with dignity regardless of what they own.
units.application: Give the same careful hearing to someone with little influence that you would give a wealthy person.

rel.note: The later saying repeats the contrast between taking shelter and passing into danger.

units.notes: Evil can mean danger or trouble. The simple are uncommitted and easily led.
units.summary: The prudent see danger and take shelter, while the simple walk into it.
units.principle: Prudence acts on danger it can foresee.
units.insight: Recognizing danger early can give someone time to seek help or change course.
units.application: Identify one avoidable risk in an upcoming decision and take a practical precaution.

rel.note: The same three benefits appear among Wisdom's gifts.

units.notes: Humility describes a true estimate of oneself. Fear of the LORD means seeing God rightly.
units.summary: Humility and the fear of the LORD are associated with a blessed life.
units.principle: Reverence and humility are worth pursuing independently of material return.
units.insight: Someone of modest means can receive God's care without measuring it by income.
units.application: Practice one act of humility before God without seeking recognition or gain.

rel.note: The father urges the learner to avoid and turn away from the wicked path.

units.notes: Thorns picture painful obstacles. Snares picture hidden traps. Soul means life.
units.summary: Keeping away from crooked ways helps guard life from their traps.
units.principle: The hazards of a path give reason to avoid it early.
units.insight: A boundary can be put in place before a known danger comes close.
units.application: Remove one recurring opportunity that draws you toward crooked conduct.

rel.note: The father passes on instruction he received from a previous generation.

units.notes: Train up refers to early formation. In his way is debated and may refer to the child's nature or calling.
units.summary: Early training in God's way can shape a child for life.
units.principle: Faithful formation gives lasting direction without controlling the future.
units.insight: Parents of wayward children deserve care without being blamed for outcomes beyond their control.
units.application: Model one habit of God's way and practice it alongside a child in your care.

rel.note: Guaranteeing debts can expose even a household's basic possessions to loss.

units.notes: Servant pictures the dependence created by debt. The first line describes an imbalance of power.
units.summary: Debt gives the lender power over the borrower.
units.principle: Borrowing can limit future freedom through obligations already made.
units.insight: A borrower deserves respect, and a person considering debt can weigh the obligations before accepting it.
units.application: Avoid borrowing for a luxury and make a realistic plan to pay what you already owe.

rel.note: Sowing righteousness produces a sure reward, opposite to the harvest of wrongdoing.

units.notes: Sowing and reaping picture a course producing its own fruit. The rod represents power used in anger.
units.summary: Sowing injustice brings sorrow, and the oppressor's power will fail.
units.principle: The means used to dominate others can undermine the one who uses them.
units.insight: People facing oppressive power can act justly without assuming it will stand forever.
units.application: Stop one unfair practice before it produces more harm and begin repairing its effects.

rel.note: Kindness to the poor is counted as service to the LORD.

units.notes: A generous eye notices opportunities to help. Bread is concrete food shared from one's own supply.
units.summary: The person who notices the poor and shares food with them is blessed.
units.principle: Generosity begins with seeing a need and sharing what is available.
units.insight: Small acts of generosity can meet needs that otherwise go unnoticed.
units.application: Share food or help meet a grocery need within your means.

rel.note: Arrogant pride is identified as the posture that gives the scoffer his name.

units.notes: A scoffer treats correction with contempt. Reproach includes the insults that keep strife active.
units.summary: Removing a persistent scoffer can bring an end to quarrels and insults.
units.principle: Peace sometimes requires stopping the conduct that sustains strife.
units.insight: A community can set a clear boundary without treating ordinary disagreement as scoffing.
units.application: Set a clear boundary around repeated mockery in a group you are responsible for.

rel.note: Kings likewise delight in people whose words are upright.

units.notes: Purity of heart concerns sincere motives. Grace on the lips means gracious and fitting speech.
units.summary: Sincere motives and gracious speech can win a ruler's friendship.
units.principle: Trustworthy influence joins inward sincerity to gracious expression.
units.insight: Someone can speak candidly and still choose a courteous manner.
units.application: Say one necessary truth to someone in authority with sincerity and care.

rel.note: The LORD watches both evil and good everywhere.

units.notes: The LORD's eyes picture watchful attention. The faithless break trust.
units.summary: The LORD preserves knowledge and overturns faithless words.
units.principle: Truth is worth keeping under God's watchful care.
units.insight: A deceptive claim can be challenged patiently without assuming its present success will last.
units.application: Correct a misleading claim with the facts you can verify.

rel.note: The lazy man again uses a lion in the streets as an excuse.

units.notes: The lion is a deliberately extreme excuse. The NKJV calls the speaker the lazy man.
units.summary: Laziness can invent dramatic excuses to avoid ordinary work.
units.principle: Avoidance can make imagined obstacles seem decisive.
units.insight: A person can distinguish an excuse from a real barrier that needs help.
units.application: Check one reason you have given for delaying a task and start if the barrier is avoidable.

rel.note: The same pit image is used for the danger posed by the seductress.

units.notes: The mouth represents seductive speech. A deep pit pictures a trap that is hard to escape.
units.summary: Seductive speech can draw a person into the deep trap of adultery.
units.principle: Wisdom judges seductive speech by its destination.
units.insight: Someone who notices an invitation to secrecy can turn away before it gains power.
units.application: End an exchange that invites marital unfaithfulness and seek trustworthy support if needed.

rel.note: Love for a child calls for timely and responsible discipline.

units.notes: Folly bound to the heart pictures a deep tendency. The rod was a tool of correction in the ancient household.
units.summary: Children need loving correction that helps them turn from folly.
units.principle: Discipline serves growth through steady and safe guidance.
units.insight: A parent can correct a specific action while reaffirming care for the child.
units.application: Explain a clear expectation and use a calm, proportionate response when it is broken.

rel.note: The new collection forbids exploiting the poor and names the LORD as their advocate.

units.notes: The first person exploits the poor to gain more. Gifts to the rich here seek an advantage.
units.summary: Exploiting the poor and courting the rich for gain can lead to poverty.
units.principle: Gain pursued through exploitation carries the seeds of loss.
units.insight: Ordinary decisions about pay or gifts can reveal whose advantage is being protected.
units.application: Review one transaction for unfair terms or an attempt to buy favor and correct it.

rel.note: The father also asks for attentive hearing and words kept in the heart.

units.notes: Inclining the ear pictures deliberate attention. Applying the heart engages thought and will.
units.summary: Listen closely to the words of the wise and take their knowledge to heart.
units.principle: Hearing wisdom becomes fruitful when it engages the inner person.
units.insight: A reader can make room for instruction by approaching it as a learner.
units.application: Read one instruction slowly and name the response it calls for.

rel.note: Writing instruction on the heart also pictures keeping it close for use.

units.notes: Within you refers to the inner person. Fixed upon the lips means ready to speak.
units.summary: Keep wise words within so they are ready on your lips.
units.principle: Internalized instruction can serve others through speech.
units.insight: A lesson learned patiently can be available when a conversation suddenly needs it.
units.application: Retain one wise saying and practice explaining it accurately in your own words.

rel.note: Wholehearted trust in the LORD likewise directs the course of life.

units.notes: Today stresses urgency. Even you makes the teaching personal.
units.summary: The words of the wise are taught so the learner will trust the LORD.
units.principle: Wisdom serves trust in the LORD.
units.insight: A practical lesson can become an occasion to rely on God more directly.
units.application: Identify one instruction from the collection and act on it in conscious reliance on the LORD.

rel.note: The opening purpose statement likewise joins instruction, knowledge, and wise counsel.

units.notes: The NKJV reads excellent things. Some read thirty sayings. Parallels to the Instruction of Amenemope are noted in the study, and the nature of the relationship is debated.
units.summary: The teacher has written valuable counsel and knowledge for the learner.
units.principle: Preserved counsel lets a learner test and recall what was taught.
units.insight: Written instruction can be revisited slowly when a decision calls for it.
units.application: Return to a written proverb that bears on a choice you face and read it in context.

rel.note: A faithful witness likewise gives a truthful account.

units.notes: Certainty conveys reliability. The last phrase can refer to those who send to the learner or those who sent the learner.
units.summary: Learn what is true so you can give reliable answers.
units.principle: Reliable speech grows from careful knowledge of the truth.
units.insight: Someone can admit uncertainty rather than give a confident answer beyond what they know.
units.application: Verify one detail before giving an answer someone else will rely on.

rel.note: Oppression of the poor likewise insults their Maker.

units.notes: The city gate served as a place of judgment. Because he is poor names the motive for exploiting someone with little power.
units.summary: Do not exploit the poor or use the courts against the afflicted.
units.principle: Justice protects people whose lack of power makes them easy to exploit.
units.insight: Someone with limited means may need help getting a fair hearing.
units.application: Identify one barrier to a fair hearing for someone with little leverage and help remove it where you can.

rel.note: The mighty Redeemer likewise pleads the cause of the fatherless against those who take their land.

units.notes: Pleading a cause is courtroom language. Plundering the soul means taking the life.
units.summary: The LORD defends the poor and judges those who plunder them.
units.principle: The LORD takes the cause of vulnerable people seriously.
units.insight: A person denied justice can be supported in seeking help and assured that God sees their case.
units.application: Stand beside someone facing exploitation and support a fair hearing for their case.

rel.note: The people we walk with shape the wisdom or folly of our own course.

units.notes: An angry or furious person is someone habitually ruled by temper.
units.summary: Be careful about close companionship with someone habitually ruled by anger.
units.principle: Close company shapes responses under pressure.
units.insight: A person can care about someone and set limits on their influence.
units.application: Choose a close adviser whose way of handling conflict is worth learning.

rel.note: An angry person's repeated strife and wrongdoing show what the learned pattern can produce.

units.notes: Learning someone's ways means taking on their habits. A snare pictures danger to one's life.
units.summary: Habitual anger can be learned from close company and become a trap.
units.principle: Learned reactions have consequences beyond the company that taught them.
units.insight: Someone who has absorbed angry habits can begin practicing a different response.
units.application: Notice one angry habit you have picked up and practice a measured alternative.

rel.note: The earlier warning describes how a guarantee traps the person who makes it.

units.notes: Striking hands sealed a pledge. A surety undertakes to pay another person's debt if they fail to pay.
units.summary: Avoid pledging to pay another person's debt.
units.principle: Generosity and prudent limits can coexist.
units.insight: A person can offer help within their means while declining to cosign.
units.application: Decline a guarantee and consider direct help you can afford to give.

rel.note: Guaranteeing a stranger's debt likewise exposes the guarantor to loss.

units.notes: The bed represents a basic household necessity. The question makes the guarantor's possible loss vivid.
units.summary: A rash guarantee can cost even basic necessities.
units.principle: A pledge is as serious as the loss it can impose.
units.insight: Someone under pressure to cosign can pause and name what their household could lose.
units.application: Before taking on an obligation, identify what you would lose if called upon to pay it.

rel.note: Moving a landmark and entering the fields of the fatherless are likewise forbidden.

units.notes: A landmark is a stone marking a family's land boundary. The earlier generations set it in place.
units.summary: Respect the boundary that protects another person's property.
units.principle: Justice includes preserving what rightly belongs to others.
units.insight: A small encroachment can cause real loss even if the other person cannot easily challenge it.
units.application: Check one boundary or agreement you administer and correct any encroachment.

rel.note: The diligent hand likewise tends toward greater responsibility.

units.notes: Standing before kings means serving in their presence. Excelling combines skill with capable execution.
units.summary: Skillful work can open doors to greater responsibility.
units.principle: Skill and faithful execution prepare people for useful responsibility.
units.insight: A person can value excellent work even when their service receives little notice.
units.application: Choose one skill in your work and improve it through a specific practice.

rel.note: The warning about deceptive food explains the need for care.

units.notes: Consider carefully stresses close attention to the food and host.
units.summary: Pay close attention at a ruler's table.
units.principle: Discernment considers the setting as well as the offer.
units.insight: A prestigious invitation can be considered without feeling obliged to agree to everything around it.
units.application: Before accepting a prestigious invitation, consider what the host may expect.

rel.note: The counsel about honey likewise sets a limit on an attractive food.

units.notes: The knife image is deliberate hyperbole for decisive restraint.
units.summary: Exercise decisive restraint when appetite can take over.
units.principle: Appetite needs restraint where it can override judgment.
units.insight: A limit chosen beforehand can help under pressure.
units.application: Decide on a reasonable limit before entering a setting that encourages excess.

rel.note: The miser's delicacies present a different example of deceptive hospitality.

units.notes: Delicacies are prized dishes. Deceptive food can hide the host's purposes.
units.summary: A ruler's delicacies may conceal expectations.
units.principle: An appealing offer deserves scrutiny when it comes from someone with power.
units.insight: A generous-looking offer can be assessed without assuming bad intent.
units.application: Ask what accepting a desirable offer would commit you to.

rel.note: Haste to become rich is likewise contrasted with faithfulness.

units.notes: Overwork means wearing oneself out. The NKJV urges using judgment to stop.
units.summary: Do not wear yourself out to become rich.
units.principle: Diligence needs a worthy aim and a stopping point.
units.insight: A person can reconsider an exhausting schedule without abandoning responsible work.
units.application: Set one limit on extra work pursued solely for more money.

rel.note: Trusting riches leads to a fall.

units.notes: Setting the eyes means fixing attention and desire. The eagle pictures wealth quickly out of reach.
units.summary: Riches can disappear as quickly as an eagle flies away.
units.principle: Money can serve a purpose without carrying the weight of ultimate security.
units.insight: Financial loss can be met with care and practical help.
units.application: Review one decision that assumes present wealth will always be available.

rel.note: A generous person shares food with the poor freely.

units.notes: Miser literally evokes an evil eye, the opposite of a generous eye.
units.summary: Be wary of delicacies offered by a miser.
units.principle: Hospitality is better weighed by the host's disposition than by the menu.
units.insight: A person can decline hospitality that comes with a known pattern of resentment.
units.application: Consider the pattern behind an offer before accepting it.

rel.note: Kind words can likewise conceal a contrary inward disposition.

units.notes: Thinks likely means calculates. His heart is not with you explains the invitation.
units.summary: The miser's inward calculation can contradict his outward welcome.
units.principle: Words of welcome should agree with the heart that speaks them.
units.insight: Sincere hospitality gives the guest room to receive without hidden pressure.
units.application: Offer only what you can share sincerely, and state any limits honestly.

rel.note: The change from sweet bread to gravel similarly pictures a bitter aftermath.

units.notes: Vomiting pictures the meal's bitter aftermath. Pleasant words are the guest's wasted courtesies.
units.summary: The miser's hospitality can end in regret and wasted courtesies.
units.principle: A gift's aftermath can reveal what its appearance concealed.
units.insight: An unpleasant experience can teach someone to weigh future invitations more carefully.
units.application: Reconsider a recurring arrangement whose apparent benefits leave you feeling manipulated.

rel.note: Correcting a scoffer likewise meets resistance, while the wise welcome rebuke.

units.notes: Speaking in someone's hearing means offering words where they can receive them.
units.summary: Wise words are wasted where a fool treats them with contempt.
units.principle: Instruction needs an opportunity to be heard.
units.insight: A conversation can be paused while leaving room for a future change in willingness.
units.application: Stop pressing unsolicited counsel in one conversation where it is persistently mocked.

rel.note: The earlier command also forbids moving an ancient landmark.

units.notes: An ancient landmark marked inherited land. Entering fields here means encroaching on them.
units.summary: Do not move inherited boundaries or take land from the fatherless.
units.principle: Justice protects another person's property even when taking it would be easy.
units.insight: Someone with little leverage may need help defending what belongs to them.
units.application: Check whether a boundary or agreement you administer protects the vulnerable party's rights.

rel.note: The LORD likewise pleads the cause of the poor against those who plunder them.

units.notes: Redeemer evokes a kinsman who defends a vulnerable relative. Pleading a cause is legal language.
units.summary: The mighty Redeemer pleads the cause of the fatherless against their oppressors.
units.principle: God takes the claims of vulnerable people seriously.
units.insight: A person denied a fair hearing can be reminded that the LORD sees their cause.
units.application: Support a fair hearing for someone whose property or livelihood is being taken unfairly.

rel.note: The opening of the collection joins an inclined ear to an engaged heart.

units.notes: Applying the heart engages thought and will. The ears picture active listening.
units.summary: Give both your attention and your heart to instruction.
units.principle: Learning joins careful hearing with inward commitment.
units.insight: A lesson can be heard more carefully when the learner knows what action it asks for.
units.application: Read one instruction slowly and write down a way you will practice it.

rel.note: Love for a child includes timely, responsible discipline.

units.notes: Correction includes training. The rod was a tool of correction in the ancient household.
units.summary: Give children the correction they need to grow.
units.principle: Loving training serves the child's growth and safety.
units.insight: A parent can wait until calm before giving proportionate correction.
units.application: State a clear expectation and choose a safe response that helps the child learn.

rel.note: Correction likewise aims to drive folly away from the child.

units.notes: Hell renders Sheol, the realm of death. Soul here means the child's life.
units.summary: Loving correction can turn a child away from a path that leads to death.
units.principle: Correction is judged by the good it seeks for the child.
units.insight: The aim of discipline is restoration and growth, which harshness and abuse contradict.
units.application: Use patient guidance to help a child identify a harmful choice and practice a safer one.

rel.note: The father of a wise and righteous child likewise delights.

units.notes: The son's heart is the inner person. The father's heart answers with joy.
units.summary: A child's growing wisdom brings a parent deep joy.
units.principle: Wisdom in a child is worth noticing and celebrating.
units.insight: A parent can express delight in growth without making affection depend on performance.
units.application: Tell a younger person about a specific wise choice you saw them make.

rel.note: The wise heart likewise trains the mouth.

units.notes: Inmost being names the depths of the father. Right things are upright words.
units.summary: Upright words from a child bring a parent deep joy.
units.principle: Words reveal what is growing in the heart.
units.insight: Good speech can be encouraged by naming what made it truthful or fitting.
units.application: Recognize one instance of honest speech in someone you are teaching.

rel.note: The reader is likewise told to refuse envy because the wicked have no lasting prospect.

units.notes: The same Hebrew verb can express envy or zeal. All day describes sustained devotion.
units.summary: Trade envy of sinners for sustained zeal for the fear of the LORD.
units.principle: Reverence redirects what the heart admires and pursues.
units.insight: Envy can be named honestly without letting it choose one's course.
units.application: Name one success you envy and choose a reverent response rather than copying its means.

rel.note: The later saying likewise speaks of a prospect and hope that will not be cut off.

units.notes: Hereafter can mean future or outcome. Whether it points beyond death is debated.
units.summary: Those who fear the LORD have a future and hope.
units.principle: God's future gives a sounder basis for hope than the present advantage of sinners.
units.insight: Hope can steady a person while apparent success favors wrongdoing.
units.application: Bring a discouraging comparison before God and return to one faithful practice.

rel.note: Guarding the heart matters because life flows from it.

units.notes: Guiding the heart pictures steering the inner person onto a road.
units.summary: Listen to wisdom and direct your heart toward the right way.
units.principle: The course of life begins with the direction of the heart.
units.insight: A recurring desire can be examined before it sets the direction of a decision.
units.application: Identify a desire that pulls you off course and redirect it through a specific choice.

rel.note: The company a person keeps helps shape their course.

units.notes: Winebibbers drink heavily. Gluttons are given to excessive eating.
units.summary: Avoid close company organized around heavy drinking or gluttony.
units.principle: Repeated company shapes what a person learns to enjoy.
units.insight: Someone seeking a change can choose companions who support it.
units.application: Choose a setting for companionship that supports the limits you intend to keep.

rel.note: A life governed by costly pleasures likewise tends toward want.

units.notes: Rags picture the want that can follow neglect. Drowsiness links indulgence with inactivity.
units.summary: Habitual indulgence can drain the resources needed for ordinary life.
units.principle: Appetite can consume what work and responsibility need.
units.insight: A person caught in excess deserves honest help and a practical way forward.
units.application: Identify one cost of a repeated excess and seek support for changing the pattern.

rel.note: The opening instruction likewise honors the teaching of both parents.

units.notes: Begot you recalls the father's relationship to the son. Despise includes contempt and neglect.
units.summary: Listen to your father and honor your mother in her old age.
units.principle: Honor is expressed through attention and care across the years.
units.insight: Care for an aging parent can take practical forms suited to the relationship.
units.application: Offer an older parent or caregiver a concrete act of care and listen to what they need.

rel.note: Getting wisdom and understanding likewise has priority over other acquisitions.

units.notes: Buying pictures acquiring at a cost. Refusing to sell pictures keeping what was gained.
units.summary: Acquire truth and wisdom and refuse to trade them away.
units.principle: Truth is worth both acquiring and keeping.
units.insight: A costly truth can be held with patience when a comfortable falsehood seems easier.
units.application: Give time to learning a difficult truth and refuse one advantage that would require denying it.

rel.note: A wise son likewise brings gladness to his father.

units.notes: Greatly rejoice conveys emphatic joy. The paired lines join righteousness with wisdom.
units.summary: A righteous and wise child brings a parent deep joy.
units.principle: Wisdom and righteousness give reason for family joy.
units.insight: Parents can celebrate character even when it receives little public attention.
units.application: Notice and affirm one upright action in a younger person.

rel.note: The preceding verse explains why a wise child gives a parent delight.

units.notes: Her who bore you singles out the mother's bond. The appeal includes both parents.
units.summary: Let both parents rejoice in the wisdom of your life.
units.principle: Upright conduct can bring joy to those who raised us.
units.insight: Specific gratitude can honor the care a mother or father has given.
units.application: Thank a parent or caregiver for one act of care and honor it through a wise choice.

rel.note: The father has likewise taught and led his son in upright paths.

units.notes: Heart includes thought, desire, will, and affection. Observe calls attention to the father's example.
units.summary: Give your heart to wise instruction and attend to the example that accompanies it.
units.principle: Wholehearted learning joins inward commitment with a lived example.
units.insight: A learner can see how instruction works by watching it practiced.
units.application: Bring one divided loyalty before God and practice one upright example you have received.

rel.note: The mouth of the immoral woman is likewise called a deep pit.

units.notes: A deep pit and narrow well picture traps that are hard to escape.
units.summary: Sexual unfaithfulness can trap a person like a deep pit.
units.principle: Judge a sexual invitation by where it leads.
units.insight: A boundary can be set before a compromising encounter becomes a pattern.
units.application: Step away from contact that is drawing you toward unfaithfulness.

rel.note: The woman likewise lies in wait at corners and public places.

units.notes: Lying in wait pictures an ambush. The Hebrew can be read as waiting for prey or acting like a robber.
units.summary: The seductress waits for an opportunity and draws others into unfaithfulness.
units.principle: Anticipating an enticement can help a person refuse it.
units.insight: Someone who recognizes a compromising approach can set distance and seek support.
units.application: Choose a specific boundary before the next opportunity to compromise arises.

rel.note: Strong drink is likewise pictured as provoking brawls.

units.notes: The questions name grief, quarrels, unexplained wounds, and reddened eyes.
units.summary: The portrait of heavy drinking begins with pain, conflict, and bodily harm.
units.principle: The pattern of harm deserves attention before it worsens.
units.insight: Repeated injuries and quarrels can be heard as reasons to offer help rather than ridicule.
units.application: Name one recurring harm linked to drinking and seek support in addressing it.

rel.note: The closing line shows the same pursuit continuing after injury.

units.notes: Lingering and searching describe sustained pursuit. Mixed wine was prepared for drinking.
units.summary: The harms described belong to those who linger over drink and seek more.
units.principle: What someone repeatedly seeks can begin to govern their life.
units.insight: A repeated search for another drink can be discussed candidly and compassionately.
units.application: Tell a trusted person about a recurring drinking pattern you are concerned about.

rel.note: The learner is likewise urged to direct the gaze rather than let it wander.

units.notes: Color, sparkle, and smooth movement describe the wine's attraction.
units.summary: Do not dwell on the attraction that leads you toward drunkenness.
units.principle: Temptation is easier to interrupt before attention becomes pursuit.
units.insight: Avoiding a setting that feeds craving can be a wise boundary.
units.application: Remove one cue or setting that regularly feeds a harmful urge to drink.

rel.note: The sweet beginning and bitter ending of adultery illustrate a similar reversal.

units.notes: At the last marks the contrast with the attractive beginning. The serpent and viper picture painful harm.
units.summary: The attractive beginning of drunkenness can end in a painful bite.
units.principle: A course should be judged by its end as well as its first taste.
units.insight: Remembering the aftermath can restore perspective when the immediate appeal is strong.
units.application: Recall the actual cost of the last harmful episode before returning to the same setting.

rel.note: Being led astray by strong drink is likewise described as folly.

units.notes: Strange things can describe distorted perceptions. Perverse words show the effect on speech.
units.summary: Drunkenness distorts perception and speech.
units.principle: Impaired judgment affects what people see and what they say.
units.insight: Someone can take responsibility for harm done under the influence and seek help preventing a repeat.
units.application: Address one harm caused by impaired speech and take a concrete step toward avoiding a repeat.

rel.note: The preceding verse describes the distorted perception behind the instability.

units.notes: The open sea and masthead picture instability and danger.
units.summary: Drunkenness can leave a person as unsteady as someone lying on a ship's mast.
units.principle: A feeling of ease can coexist with real danger.
units.insight: People who are impaired need protection from immediate hazards.
units.application: Plan a safe way out of a setting where impairment could put you or others at risk.

rel.note: The earlier answer describes the same persistent search for drink.

units.notes: The drinker reports blows he did not feel. His final question reveals the craving to repeat the course.
units.summary: The drinker seeks another drink even after being injured by the pattern.
units.principle: Numbness can hide harm while craving keeps the pattern going.
units.insight: Someone caught in addiction can receive compassionate support and hope for change.
units.application: Tell someone trustworthy about the pattern and seek appropriate support for taking a safer next step.

rel.note: The earlier warning redirects envy of sinners toward the fear of the LORD.

units.notes: Envy can develop into a desire for close company.
units.summary: Refuse to envy evildoers or seek their company.
units.principle: Admiration can shape whose ways we imitate.
units.insight: The appeal of belonging can be separated from the conduct a group expects.
units.application: Decline one invitation that would require you to share in wrongdoing.

rel.note: The troublemaker likewise plans evil in his heart and sows discord.

units.notes: The heart devises, and the lips express what has been planned.
units.summary: The people we are warned against admiring plan violence and talk about harm.
units.principle: Words and plans reveal the moral direction of a group.
units.insight: A group's talk can reveal what joining it would mean for others.
units.application: Listen for what a group regularly encourages before choosing to identify with it.

rel.note: The wise woman builds her house, while folly tears it down.

units.notes: House can mean a dwelling or household. Established means made firm.
units.summary: Wisdom builds a house, and understanding makes it stand.
units.principle: Sound judgment helps make what we build durable.
units.insight: What a person has built can be examined with humility rather than used to condemn them.
units.application: Choose one habit that would strengthen a household or responsibility you are building.

rel.note: Wisdom likewise builds her house and furnishes it for the good of her guests.

units.notes: Rooms and riches picture what fills a house already built and established.
units.summary: Knowledge fills the rooms of a well-built house with valuable and pleasant goods.
units.principle: Wisdom shapes what fills a household as well as what holds it up.
units.insight: Some of a household's richest goods can be cultivated with modest means.
units.application: Choose one lasting good to cultivate in the home through a practice you can sustain.

rel.note: A wise person can overcome a stronghold trusted by powerful defenders.

units.notes: Strength includes the effective power to act, beyond physical force.
units.summary: Wisdom makes a person strong, and knowledge increases that strength.
units.principle: Knowledge makes strength more effective.
units.insight: Learning can give a person more options when force or effort alone is failing.
units.application: Learn one fact or skill that would improve how you handle a difficult task.

rel.note: The same second line associates many counselors with safety.

units.notes: Wise counsel means sound strategic guidance. War supplies a high-stakes example.
units.summary: Wise counsel strengthens preparation, and several advisers can improve safety.
units.principle: High stakes increase the value of tested counsel.
units.insight: People can welcome independent advice before a decision becomes hard to reverse.
units.application: Ask multiple trustworthy advisers to test a serious plan before acting.

rel.note: The fool takes pleasure in expressing his own views and has little delight in understanding.

units.notes: The gate was where public business and judgment took place.
units.summary: The fool has little wise judgment to offer when the community needs it.
units.principle: Public judgment depends on wisdom cultivated beforehand.
units.insight: A person can prepare for responsibility by receiving instruction before being called to speak.
units.application: Learn what a community decision requires before offering an opinion on it.

rel.note: The troublemaker likewise makes devising evil a continual practice.

units.notes: A schemer is literally a master of schemes.
units.summary: Habitually plotting evil gives a person a reputation as a schemer.
units.principle: Repeated intentions become visible in a person's reputation.
units.insight: A harmful plan can be abandoned before it becomes another instance of a settled pattern.
units.application: Abandon one plan designed to harm another person and choose an honest course instead.

rel.note: The scoffer's arrogant posture is named explicitly in the earlier portrait.

units.notes: Devising means planning. Abomination here describes people's revulsion at the scoffer.
units.summary: Plotting folly is sin, and persistent scoffing makes a person offensive.
units.principle: Responsibility begins with what we deliberately plan.
units.insight: A plan can be brought into the open and changed before it is acted upon.
units.application: Name a harmful plan honestly and stop pursuing it.

rel.note: Wisdom and knowledge are described nearby as sources of strength.

units.notes: Faint means lose heart or give way. Adversity is a time of distress.
units.summary: Adversity reveals the limits of our strength.
units.principle: Strength is tested by what it can bear under pressure.
units.insight: Someone overwhelmed by hardship can be helped rather than blamed.
units.application: Identify one source of wise support before a demanding situation arrives.

rel.note: The later instruction likewise calls for action on behalf of people who cannot defend themselves.

units.notes: Drawn toward death and stumbling to slaughter describe people in immediate danger.
units.summary: Act to rescue those being led toward death.
units.principle: Recognizing serious danger brings a responsibility to respond where possible.
units.insight: Someone who cannot intervene alone can seek help from people equipped to act.
units.application: When you see someone in serious danger, seek appropriate help and take a safe step to protect them.

rel.note: The LORD likewise weighs hearts beyond people's favorable assessments of themselves.

units.notes: Weighing hearts pictures exact knowledge of motives. Rendering means repaying according to deeds.
units.summary: God weighs the heart behind claims of ignorance and holds people responsible for their deeds.
units.principle: Deliberate ignorance cannot hide indifference from God.
units.insight: A person can admit they looked away and begin to respond now.
units.application: Examine whether you have avoided learning about a danger you could responsibly help address.

rel.note: The following verse applies the sweetness and goodness of honey to wisdom.

units.notes: Honeycomb gives a familiar example of pleasant food. The comparison is completed in 24:14.
units.summary: Enjoy the sweetness of honey as a picture of what wisdom can give.
units.principle: What is beneficial can also be delightful.
units.insight: Ordinary pleasures can help a learner recognize the goodness of instruction.
units.application: Recall an ordinary good you enjoy and identify a piece of wisdom you can receive with similar gratitude.

rel.note: The same language promises a prospect and hope that will not be cut off.

units.notes: Prospect means a future outcome. The first line completes the honey comparison.
units.summary: Wisdom is sweet to the soul and gives a future worth hoping for.
units.principle: Wisdom offers a good that lasts beyond its first enjoyment.
units.insight: A person discouraged by present setbacks can still look ahead with hope.
units.application: Return to one sound instruction that gives you reason to persevere.

rel.note: Taking the land of vulnerable people is likewise forbidden.

units.notes: Lying in wait evokes an ambush. Resting place is the righteous person's home.
units.summary: Do not ambush the righteous or plunder their home.
units.principle: Another person's place of safety must be respected.
units.insight: A home threatened by wrongdoing deserves practical protection and support.
units.application: Refuse an advantage that would deprive another person of security in their home.

rel.note: The preceding attack on the righteous person's home gives context to the repeated falls.

units.notes: Seven times means repeatedly. The preceding verse concerns an attack on the righteous person's home.
units.summary: The righteous can rise after repeated setbacks, while calamity brings the wicked down.
units.principle: Resilience belongs with God's keeping, even where setbacks are real.
units.insight: Being knocked down does not mean God has abandoned the person who is suffering.
units.application: Take one manageable step toward recovery after a setback and seek help where needed.

rel.note: Gloating over calamity is likewise warned against.

units.notes: Falling and stumbling describe an enemy's trouble. The second line addresses inward gladness.
units.summary: Refuse to rejoice when an enemy stumbles.
units.principle: The character of our response matters even when an enemy has done real harm.
units.insight: Relief at the end of a wrong can coexist with compassion for the person who fell.
units.application: Refuse to share a mocking response to an enemy's trouble and consider a merciful alternative.

rel.note: The wronged person is likewise urged to leave repayment with the LORD.

units.notes: The LORD sees the inward reaction of 24:17. Him at the end refers to the enemy.
units.summary: The LORD sees and is displeased by gloating over an enemy.
units.principle: God's judgment gives no license for personal cruelty.
units.insight: A person can surrender vindictive pleasure without denying what the enemy did.
units.application: Confess any pleasure you have taken in someone's ruin and leave their judgment with God.

rel.note: Reverence and hope give a reason to refuse envy of sinners.

units.notes: Fret can mean become agitated or angry. Envy wants what the wicked appear to have.
units.summary: Do not fret over evildoers or envy their apparent success.
units.principle: Present success gives little evidence of where wickedness leads.
units.insight: Anger about wrongdoing can be acknowledged while attention returns to a faithful response.
units.application: Name an advantage you envy and choose one upright way to respond to it.

rel.note: The same second line contrasts the wicked person's lamp with the light of the righteous.

units.notes: Prospect means a future outcome. An extinguished lamp pictures the end of life and continuity.
units.summary: The wicked have no lasting prospect, and their lamp will go out.
units.principle: A course has to be judged by its end.
units.insight: A person's present advantage can be assessed in light of what will endure.
units.application: Give attention to one good that will outlast an advantage gained through wrongdoing.

rel.note: The king's authority is also held accountable to just judgment.

units.notes: Those given to change likely means people bent on reckless revolt. The wording is debated.
units.summary: Fear the LORD, honor rightful authority, and refuse reckless revolt.
units.principle: Respect for human authority belongs under allegiance to God.
units.insight: A person can raise a just concern without joining destructive agitation.
units.application: Address a concern about authority through an honest and peaceable channel.

rel.note: The settled pursuit of rebellion likewise brings a severe reckoning.

units.notes: Calamity refers to sudden disaster. Both points back to the LORD and the king in 24:21.
units.summary: Reckless rebellion can bring sudden ruin.
units.principle: The consequences of defiance can arrive before its participants expect them.
units.insight: A group's confidence can hide risks that an independent adviser can see.
units.application: Consider the risks and moral grounds of a proposed action before joining it.

rel.note: Favoring the wicked and denying the righteous justice are likewise condemned.

units.notes: These things also belong to the wise introduces a short appendix. Partiality means judging by the person's standing.
units.summary: The further sayings of the wise begin by rejecting partiality in judgment.
units.principle: Judgment should follow the facts rather than a person's status.
units.insight: A fair process helps protect people with less influence.
units.application: Apply the same standard to each person in a dispute you have a role in deciding.

rel.note: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the innocent are detestable to the LORD.

units.notes: Calling the wicked righteous pictures a corrupt verdict. Peoples and nations show the breadth of public outrage.
units.summary: Declaring the guilty righteous brings public condemnation.
units.principle: Truthful judgment protects confidence in justice.
units.insight: People harmed by a false verdict can be supported in seeking a fair review.
units.application: Refuse pressure to describe a known wrong as innocent.

rel.note: The preceding verse shows the reproach brought by calling the wicked righteous.

units.notes: Rebuking the wicked means naming wrongdoing truthfully. The source of the blessing is unstated.
