units.application: Give someone with little influence the same attentive hearing you would give a powerful person.

rel.note: Justice establishes a land, while bribery undermines it.

units.notes: Judging with truth means judging faithfully according to the facts.
units.summary: A king who judges the poor fairly builds a stable reign.
units.principle: Authority is steadied by justice for those with least leverage.
units.insight: An impartial process can protect someone who cannot buy access or influence.
units.application: Check whether a person with limited resources has a fair chance to present their case.

rel.note: Love takes responsibility for timely correction.

units.notes: The rod was a tool of correction in the ancient household. Rebuke corrects through words.
units.summary: Children need loving correction and guidance to grow in wisdom.
units.principle: Discipline combines guidance and consistent, proportionate action.
units.insight: A caregiver can correct conduct calmly while reassuring a child of their care.
units.application: State a clear expectation and follow through with a safe, proportionate response if it is broken.

rel.note: The fall of the wicked likewise gives the righteous room to flourish.

units.notes: The same Hebrew verb connects the increase of the wicked with the increase of transgression.
units.summary: Wrongdoing spreads when the wicked gain influence, but their power can fall.
units.principle: Present influence does not make wrongdoing enduring.
units.insight: A community can keep practicing what is right while harmful conduct appears normal.
units.application: Keep one upright practice where pressure has made dishonesty common.

rel.note: Early formation commonly shapes a child into later life.

units.notes: Correct includes training and guidance. Rest and delight name its ordinary fruit.
units.summary: Loving correction can bring a parent rest and delight as the child grows.
units.principle: Faithful training seeks growth over time.
units.insight: A parent facing difficulties deserves support without blame for outcomes beyond their control.
units.application: Choose one expectation to teach patiently and follow through on it calmly.

rel.note: The earlier saying also stresses the importance of attending to God's instruction.

units.notes: Revelation means a prophetic word from God. Law means God's given instruction.
units.summary: Without God's revelation people cast off restraint, while those who keep His instruction are blessed.
units.principle: God's revealed word gives direction that calls for obedience.
units.insight: A community can respond to God's word by putting it into practice together.
units.application: Identify one clear instruction from Scripture and put it into practice in a shared responsibility.

rel.note: Correction reaches a willing learner more readily than a resistant person.

units.notes: The setting is an ancient household with servants. No answer can mean no response in conduct.
units.summary: Understanding an instruction does not ensure a willing response.
units.principle: Effective correction depends in part on willingness to respond.
units.insight: When words alone have brought no change, an appropriate boundary can clarify what is required.
units.application: Check whether someone understands an expectation, then agree on a fair next step.

rel.note: Answering before hearing the matter likewise brings folly and shame.

units.notes: Hasty words are words spoken before adequate reflection.
units.summary: Hasty speech puts a person in worse prospects than the proverb's familiar fool.
units.principle: Speech needs time for judgment before it goes out.
units.insight: A pause can make room to learn what an immediate reply would miss.
units.application: Wait until you understand the facts before answering a provocative claim.

rel.note: The nearby household saying likewise considers how responsibility is taught and received.

units.notes: Pampering means habitual indulgence. The Hebrew word rendered son is uncertain.
units.summary: Indulgence without clear expectations can encourage presumption.
units.principle: Generosity is steadier when responsibilities are clear.
units.insight: Kindness can be combined with honest expectations about responsibilities.
units.application: Clarify one responsibility you have repeatedly overlooked in the name of kindness.

rel.note: Wrath stirs contention, while patience helps calm it.

units.notes: A furious man is characterized by wrath. Stirring up pictures keeping a conflict active.
units.summary: Habitual anger stirs conflict and multiplies wrongdoing.
units.principle: Uncontrolled anger creates harms beyond the first reaction.
units.insight: A person can seek help changing the pattern before another outburst.
units.application: Interrupt one recurring angry reaction with a planned pause and a measured reply.

rel.note: Haughtiness comes before ruin, and humility comes before honor.

units.notes: Being brought low contrasts with keeping honor. Humble describes the person's inner posture.
units.summary: Pride brings a person low, while humility preserves honor.
units.principle: Honor is better received through humility than grasped through pride.
units.insight: Recognizing one's limits can make room for help and growth.
units.application: Accept one correction without trying to recover status in the conversation.

rel.note: Dishonest testimony remains answerable to justice.

units.notes: The oath calls witnesses to testify and carries a curse. Partnership can include sharing the proceeds or withholding evidence.
units.summary: Sharing in theft can trap a person into withholding truthful evidence.
units.principle: Loyalty to wrongdoing endangers both truth and the person who conceals it.
units.insight: Someone who has been complicit can seek a responsible way to come forward.
units.application: Refuse a share in dishonest gain and report what you know through an appropriate channel.

rel.note: The LORD is also pictured as a strong tower where the righteous find refuge.

units.notes: A snare is a hidden trap. Safe pictures being set high out of reach.
units.summary: Fear of people can trap us, while trust in the LORD gives security.
units.principle: Trust in God gives a firmer ground for action than fear of people's reactions.
units.insight: A person under pressure can seek practical protection and trust God at the same time.
units.application: Name one pressure to compromise and choose a faithful response with whatever support you need.

rel.note: The ruler's heart remains in the LORD's hand.

units.notes: Seeking the ruler's face means seeking favor or a hearing.
units.summary: People seek a ruler's favor, but justice ultimately comes from the LORD.
units.principle: Human decisions remain answerable to God's justice.
units.insight: A person can seek a fair ruling while entrusting what they cannot control to God.
units.application: Pursue a fair process and pray for justice without relying on favoritism.

rel.note: Kindness to an enemy shows how moral opposition can coexist with practical mercy.

units.notes: Abomination means something detestable. The two lines reverse who recoils from whom.
units.summary: The righteous detest injustice, while the wicked detest upright conduct.
units.principle: Moral opposition does not require personal hatred.
units.insight: Opposing wrongdoing can coexist with mercy toward the person who does it.
units.application: Oppose a specific wrong truthfully and refuse a cruel response to the person responsible.

rel.note: The next chapter also identifies a distinct voice and its utterance.

units.notes: Utterance may mean oracle or refer to Massa. The reading of Ithiel and Ucal is debated.
units.summary: Agur's words enter the collection under his own name.
units.principle: Attend to the instruction a speaker actually gives.
units.insight: Wisdom can be received from someone whose life story is largely unknown.
units.application: Read the heading before interpreting the sayings that follow.

rel.note: Wisdom belongs with the humble.

units.notes: Agur uses severe language about his own understanding.
units.summary: Agur begins by acknowledging how little he understands.
units.principle: Humility is part of wisdom.
units.insight: An honest admission of limits can open a person to learning.
units.application: Name a question you cannot answer and seek sound instruction.

rel.note: Knowledge of the Holy One belongs with understanding.

units.notes: The Holy One is God. The confession continues from verse 2.
units.summary: Agur admits the limits of his knowledge of the Holy One.
units.principle: Knowing God calls for humility about what one understands.
units.insight: A believer can admit uncertainty while continuing to seek God.
units.application: Bring a question about God to Scripture with a willingness to learn.

rel.note: The creation poem likewise portrays God's ordering of the heavens, waters, and earth.

units.notes: The questions move from heaven and creation to God's name and His Son's name.
units.summary: The Creator's works exceed human reach, and Agur asks for His Son's name.
units.principle: Human inquiry depends on what God reveals.
units.insight: The question invites wonder at what God has made known through Christ.
units.application: Read Agur's questions alongside John 3:13 and reflect on what Jesus makes known.

rel.note: The LORD is also pictured as a strong tower for the righteous.

units.notes: Pure evokes metal refined of impurities. The shield is God Himself.
units.summary: God's word is pure, and He shields those who trust Him.
units.principle: The trustworthy word directs trust to the One who speaks it.
units.insight: A person can rest in what God has spoken while questions remain.
units.application: Bring one uncertainty before God and attend to what Scripture actually says about it.

rel.note: The LORD detests lying and delights in faithful conduct.

units.notes: Adding means putting human claims alongside God's own words.
units.summary: Do not add to God's words and present the addition as His.
units.principle: Faithful teaching respects the boundary between revelation and interpretation.
units.insight: A teacher can distinguish Scripture from an inference or application.
units.application: Review one explanation and label clearly what is quotation and what is interpretation.

rel.note: The next verse names the requests for truthfulness and sufficient provision.

units.notes: The two requests are specified in verse 8. Before I die gives the prayer a lifelong horizon.
units.summary: Agur asks God for two things to sustain him throughout life.
units.principle: Wisdom can name what it needs from God.
units.insight: A short prayer can express a settled dependence on God.
units.application: Pray through Agur's two requests with your present circumstances in mind.

rel.note: Modest means with reverence for the LORD are preferred to great treasure with turmoil.

units.notes: Allotted food is one's needed portion. Falsehood includes what is hollow or deceptive.
units.summary: Ask God for truthfulness and enough provision.
units.principle: Enough can be a better aim than extremes of wealth or deprivation.
units.insight: Contentment can be practiced while seeking practical help with genuine needs.
units.application: Pray for daily provision and identify one honest way to use what you have.

rel.note: Integrity has greater worth than financial standing.

units.notes: Fullness pictures abundance. Profaning God's name means dishonoring Him.
units.summary: Both abundance and need can bring pressures that test faithfulness.
units.principle: Provision is best received in a way that honors God.
units.insight: A person facing need deserves help, and someone with plenty can practice grateful dependence.
units.application: Name the temptation that most accompanies your circumstances and choose one faithful response.

rel.note: False testimony can wound a neighbor like a weapon.

units.notes: Maligning means slandering. A servant could have little power to answer an accusation.
units.summary: Do not slander someone who has little power to defend themselves.
units.principle: Power differences make truthful testimony especially important.
units.insight: A supervisor can give an accused person a fair hearing.
units.application: Verify an allegation before passing it to someone with authority over the accused.

rel.note: Cursing father or mother is likewise treated as destructive.

units.notes: Generation here describes a kind of people.
units.summary: Contempt and withheld gratitude can both dishonor parents.
units.principle: Honor takes form in speech and practical care.
units.insight: Respect can be expressed alongside necessary boundaries.
units.application: Offer one truthful word of gratitude or act of care to a parent or caregiver.

rel.note: The question exposes the impossibility of self-made purity.

units.notes: Pure in their own eyes describes self-approval. Washing pictures cleansing from wrongdoing.
units.summary: People can call themselves clean while remaining in need of cleansing.
units.principle: Self-approval cannot remove wrongdoing.
units.insight: Conviction can lead to honest confession and mercy.
units.application: Confess a specific wrong rather than defending your general character.

rel.note: Haughty eyes appear among the things the LORD hates.

units.notes: Lofty eyes and lifted eyelids picture disdain.
units.summary: Arrogance can show in the way we look at others.
units.principle: Pride shapes how we see other people.
units.insight: A habitual expression of contempt can be noticed and changed.
units.application: Give a respectful hearing to someone you tend to look down on.

rel.note: An oppressive ruler over the poor is likewise compared to a dangerous animal.

units.notes: Teeth and fangs like weapons picture predatory exploitation.
units.summary: Exploiting the poor is predatory conduct.
units.principle: Power must be accountable for what it takes from others.
units.insight: A person with little leverage may need an advocate to challenge unfair treatment.
units.application: Challenge one practice that takes unfair advantage of people in need.

rel.note: Human desire is likewise compared to a realm that is never full.

units.notes: The leech's repeated Give introduces insatiable appetite. Three then four is a list pattern.
units.summary: The leech pictures an appetite that keeps demanding more.
units.principle: An unchecked appetite does not set its own limits.
units.insight: A repeated demand can reveal that more will never settle the underlying desire.
units.application: Notice one demand you keep renewing after it has already been met.

rel.note: Sheol and Destruction likewise picture insatiability.

units.notes: The grave is Sheol. The four images complete the list begun in 30:15.
units.summary: Four images show what it means never to be satisfied.
units.principle: The images make the persistence of appetite and longing visible.
units.insight: Unfulfilled longing can be acknowledged without blame.
units.application: Distinguish a real unmet need from a desire that keeps enlarging as it is fed.

rel.note: The earlier portrait likewise names contempt for father and mother.

units.notes: The mocking eye represents contempt. Birds feeding on it evoke a body left unburied.
units.summary: Mocking parents leads toward disgrace.
units.principle: Honor concerns inward regard as well as outward conduct.
units.insight: Family wrongs can be addressed without contempt.
units.application: Replace a contemptuous remark with a measured account of the concern.

rel.note: The next verse names the four wonders.

units.notes: Three then four introduces the wonders listed in verse 19.
units.summary: Agur names wonders he cannot fully explain.
units.principle: Wisdom can acknowledge mystery without claiming to solve it.
units.insight: Wonder can coexist with careful attention and honest limits.
units.application: Consider the four examples before deciding what feature they share.

rel.note: The next way also leaves no visible trace, but it ends in denial of adultery.

units.notes: Virgin renders a term for a young woman of marriageable age. The four ways leave no readily traced path.
units.summary: Four elusive ways culminate in the mystery of love between a man and a young woman.
units.principle: The mystery of love can be received with reverence.
units.insight: The spiritual reading invites wonder at Christ's relationship with His Church.
units.application: Read 30:18–20 together, then reflect on Christ's love for His Bride in Ephesians 5:32.

rel.note: Confession and forsaking open the way to mercy, unlike concealment.

units.notes: Eating and wiping the mouth picture removing visible signs of an act.
units.summary: Concealing adultery leaves the wrongdoing intact even when it is denied.
units.principle: Absence of visible evidence does not make a course innocent.
units.insight: A person who has denied a wrong can still confess it and seek mercy.
units.application: Name a wrong you have minimized and take a concrete step to leave it.

rel.note: The next verse gives the first two upheavals.

units.notes: The earth trembling and unable to bear a load is deliberate exaggeration.
units.summary: Agur introduces four upheavals the earth can scarcely bear.
units.principle: Transitions can expose weaknesses in judgment and character.
units.insight: A change in circumstances can call for care about how relationships will bear it.
units.application: Read the four examples together before drawing an application.

rel.note: Luxury for a fool and a servant ruling princes are similarly pictured as mismatches.

units.notes: A servant becoming king reverses expected rank. A fool filled with food has plenty at his disposal.
units.summary: Power and plenty can magnify folly when judgment is lacking.
units.principle: Resources need character capable of using them well.
units.insight: New responsibility can be accompanied by guidance and accountability.
units.application: Seek counsel before taking up a responsibility for which you have little experience.

rel.note: The introductory verse frames these examples as reversals the earth cannot bear.

units.notes: Hateful can also mean unloved. Succeeding the mistress means taking her place.
units.summary: Sudden changes in household standing can unsettle relationships.
units.principle: A change in position calls for judgment about its effects on others.
units.insight: People entering a new role can handle the change with care for those affected.
units.application: Clarify one household expectation when roles change.

rel.note: The learner is likewise invited to observe a small creature and gain wisdom.

units.notes: The list counts four little creatures. Exceedingly wise emphasizes their skill.
units.summary: Small creatures can show remarkable wisdom.
units.principle: Wisdom can work through modest resources.
units.insight: Limited strength can be met with intelligent adaptation.
units.application: Look for one practical skill that makes better use of what you already have.

rel.note: The ant likewise gathers food in summer and harvest.

units.notes: Ants are called a people despite their individual weakness.
units.summary: Ants prepare in summer despite their small strength.
units.principle: Foresight makes use of the right season.
units.insight: A modest preparation now can reduce pressure later.
units.application: Complete one preparation while the opportunity is available.

rel.note: The prudent person recognizes danger and takes shelter.

units.notes: Rock badgers are small animals that shelter in rocky terrain.
units.summary: Rock badgers compensate for weakness by choosing secure shelter.
units.principle: Good judgment takes limitations into account.
units.insight: Acknowledging a vulnerability can help someone take a sensible precaution.
units.application: Put one appropriate protection in place for a risk you cannot meet by strength alone.

rel.note: The ant likewise does its work without an overseer.

units.notes: Ranks pictures ordered groups moving together.
units.summary: Locusts move in order without a king.
units.principle: Order makes collective effort more effective.
units.insight: People can cooperate through clear shared practices.
units.application: Agree on a simple shared procedure for a task involving several people.

rel.note: Skillful work likewise opens opportunities to serve in royal settings.

units.notes: The creature is uncertain. The NKJV reads spider, and other translations read lizard.
units.summary: A small creature's skill gets it into kings' palaces.
units.principle: Skill can open access that size or strength alone cannot.
units.insight: Limited resources can be used well through practice.
units.application: Practice a useful skill suited to a limitation you face.

rel.note: The king is the final example of stately bearing.

units.notes: Majestic pace means a stately stride. The rising count introduces four examples.
units.summary: Four examples introduce the picture of a stately stride.
units.principle: Bearing can express the strength or support behind it.
units.insight: Confidence can be observed without confusing it with self-importance.
units.application: Read the examples as a group and notice what gives each its bearing.

rel.note: A lion's boldness also pictures the confidence of the righteous.

units.notes: The lion supplies the first example of a stately mover.
units.summary: The lion moves boldly and does not retreat before another creature.
units.principle: A confident bearing is strongest when grounded in something real.
units.insight: Steadiness can be distinguished from a show of confidence.
units.application: Consider what gives you a sound basis for courage before a difficult task.

rel.note: A king's honor likewise depends on the people who stand under his rule.

units.notes: The animal rendered greyhound is uncertain, and the wording about the king also varies.
units.summary: The list of stately movers ends with a king supported by his troops.
units.principle: Visible confidence can depend on cooperation as well as personal strength.
units.insight: A person's bearing can reflect the support of those who stand with them.
units.application: Recognize the people whose support enables you to carry a responsibility.

rel.note: Guarding the mouth protects a person from trouble.

units.notes: Putting a hand on the mouth means stopping speech immediately.
units.summary: Stop speaking when pride or an evil plan is driving the words.
units.principle: Self-control can interrupt wrongdoing before it goes further.
units.insight: A pause can give room to admit what is motivating a reply.
units.application: Stop a boast or harmful plan midstream and reconsider what you were about to say.

rel.note: Wrath stirs up strife, while patience helps settle contention.

units.notes: Churning, wringing, and forcing repeat the idea of applying pressure.
units.summary: Pressing anger produces conflict as surely as other pressures produce their effects.
units.principle: The pressure we apply can bring on the quarrel we say we want to avoid.
units.insight: A dispute can cool when someone stops provoking the other person.
units.application: Stop one repeated provocation and return to the issue calmly.

rel.note: The opening appeal places a mother's teaching alongside a father's instruction.

units.notes: Utterance can mean oracle or refer to Massa. Lemuel is otherwise unknown.
units.summary: Lemuel passes on the instruction his mother taught him.
units.principle: Wise leadership can begin with receiving a parent's instruction.
units.insight: A mother's wisdom can shape how authority is exercised long after childhood.
units.application: Recall a sound lesson from a mother or caregiver and apply it to a responsibility you carry.

rel.note: The father likewise appeals personally to his son for his heart.

units.notes: The repeated questions express urgency and affection. Son of my vows points to a bond expressed before God.
units.summary: Lemuel's mother speaks to him with urgent, personal concern.
units.principle: Loving instruction attends to the person as well as the issue.
units.insight: Care can be expressed directly before difficult counsel is given.
units.application: Before giving hard counsel, explain why the person's good matters to you.

rel.note: Adultery can hand over vigor, years, and the fruit of one's work.

units.notes: Strength includes the ruler's vigor and resources. The warning concerns a course that ruins kings.
units.summary: A ruler must guard his strength from sexual indulgence that can ruin his rule.
units.principle: Sexual choices can affect the exercise of entrusted power.
units.insight: People with responsibility can examine private habits for their public costs.
units.application: End a pattern of contact that drains your attention and invites unfaithfulness.

rel.note: The earlier warning describes how strong drink can lead someone astray.

units.notes: The repeated words for kings stress the ruler's office. The two drinks can impair judgment.
units.summary: Kings and rulers need clear judgment free from the influence of drink.
units.principle: Authority gives sobriety a public purpose.
units.insight: Someone responsible for others can set a firm limit around occasions when judgment must be clear.
units.application: Keep a responsibility involving other people's welfare free from anything that would impair your judgment.

rel.note: A king who judges the poor faithfully establishes his throne.

units.notes: The law refers to decrees the ruler must remember. The afflicted include those with little means to defend their rights.
units.summary: Impairment in a ruler can cost the afflicted their rights.
units.principle: A ruler's duty to justice requires clear judgment.
units.insight: People with little power deserve decisions made with full attention and care.
units.application: Postpone or hand off a decision if you cannot give it clear, fair attention.

rel.note: The contrast follows the warning that drink can cause rulers to forget justice.

units.notes: Perishing and bitter of heart describe people in severe distress. Some read the contrast as ironic.
units.summary: The mother contrasts royal sobriety with relief for the severely afflicted.
units.principle: The responsibilities and needs of the people involved shape the comparison.
units.insight: People in distress deserve compassionate care suited to their actual needs.
units.application: Offer appropriate comfort or practical support to someone in severe distress.

rel.note: The preceding verse identifies the perishing and bitterly afflicted as the people in view.

units.notes: Forget links back to the ruler's forgetting in verse 5.
units.summary: The verse pictures a brief easing of misery for the afflicted person.
units.principle: Compassion takes suffering seriously and attends to the kind of relief offered.
units.insight: A moment of relief can be valued alongside continued care for the underlying burden.
units.application: Ask what would actually ease a burden for someone you are helping.

rel.note: The earlier instruction calls for active rescue of those being led toward death.

units.notes: Open your mouth calls for public advocacy. The speechless lack a voice in their case.
units.summary: Speak for those who cannot speak for themselves.
units.principle: Influence carries responsibility to defend vulnerable people.
units.insight: An advocate can help someone be heard without taking over what they can say for themselves.
units.application: Help someone with little leverage present their concern to a person able to act.

rel.note: The LORD Himself pleads the cause of the poor against those who exploit them.

units.notes: Pleading a cause means defending a legal claim. Righteous judgment requires fairness.
units.summary: Judge fairly and defend the rights of the poor and needy.
units.principle: Justice protects the rights of those without influence.
units.insight: Someone who lacks access may need practical help getting a fair hearing.
units.application: Remove one barrier that prevents a vulnerable person from presenting their case.

rel.note: Finding a wife is called a good gift and echoes the language of finding Wisdom in 8:35.

units.notes: The poem begins a twenty-two-verse Hebrew acrostic. Virtuous conveys strength, valor, and worth. Its connection to Lemuel's mother is debated.
units.summary: A woman of strength and worth is more precious than rubies.
units.principle: Character has a worth wealth cannot purchase.
units.insight: The poem celebrates character and gives no checklist by which to shame women, married or single.
units.application: Honor a woman for a specific quality of character you have seen in her.

rel.note: Proven faithfulness is distinguished from claims of loyalty.

units.notes: Safely trusts describes secure confidence. Gain can carry the sense of valuable proceeds.
units.summary: Her husband trusts her judgment and benefits from her faithful stewardship.
units.principle: Faithful stewardship makes trust reasonable.
units.insight: Trust can grow as people give one another room to carry responsibilities well.
units.application: Name a responsibility someone carries well and acknowledge the trust they have earned.

rel.note: Faithful love continues through changing circumstances.

units.notes: Good and evil describe the effects of her conduct toward her husband.
units.summary: Her lifelong loyalty is expressed in doing her husband good.
units.principle: Faithfulness shows itself over time.
units.insight: Steady kindness can matter more to a relationship than occasional grand gestures.
units.application: Practice one small kindness you can sustain toward someone close to you.

rel.note: The materials she seeks become goods she makes and supplies to merchants.

units.notes: Wool and flax supplied material for making cloth. Willingly describes glad hands.
units.summary: She finds the materials she needs and works with willing hands.
units.principle: Mercy expressed outwardly can go together with inward sincerity.
units.insight: Ordinary work can express care and willingness.
units.application: Do one ordinary task willingly and consider what inward motive it expresses.

rel.note: The next verse shows how her provisions reach the people in her care.

units.notes: Merchant ships carried provisions from distant places.
units.summary: She finds provisions for her household with the reach of a merchant ship.
units.principle: Wise care seeks what will genuinely nourish those who depend on it.
units.insight: Good provision can require thoughtful planning and openness to help from elsewhere.
units.application: Look beyond your usual source for a useful provision or insight you can share.

rel.note: The household and maidservants likewise share in the provision of diligent stewardship.

units.notes: Before daylight describes early preparation. The maidservants' portion may mean food or assigned work.
units.summary: She prepares early so everyone in her care receives a portion.
units.principle: Preparation makes room to serve those who depend on us.
units.insight: Attentive care includes the people who carry out the work, and its schedule can vary with circumstances.
units.application: Plan ahead for one need shared by the people in your care.

rel.note: The field and household saying also values ordering work around productive preparation.

units.notes: Considering the field means assessing its value and use. The vineyard is planted from her earnings.
units.summary: She evaluates a field and puts her earnings to productive use.
units.principle: Stewardship weighs a purchase by what it will sustain.
units.insight: Good judgment can direct resources toward patient, useful growth.
units.application: Assess a proposed purchase for its long-term usefulness before committing to it.

rel.note: Wisdom and knowledge likewise increase a person's effective strength.

units.notes: Girding means preparing one's clothing for vigorous work. Strong arms picture readiness.
units.summary: She prepares herself with strength for the work ahead.
units.principle: Readiness helps a person use strength well.
units.insight: Strength can be cultivated in ways suited to a person's actual abilities and circumstances.
units.application: Prepare one skill or resource that will help you meet an upcoming responsibility.

rel.note: Her rising while it is still night is another image of watchful preparation.

units.notes: Perceives literally evokes tasting or testing. The lamp shows care and provision continuing after dark.
units.summary: She knows the value of her work, and her lamp continues to burn.
units.principle: Good stewardship stays attentive to what it produces and what needs sustaining.
units.insight: Watchfulness can be practiced faithfully without making exhaustion a measure of worth.
units.application: Review whether one practice is bearing good fruit and sustain what is useful.

rel.note: The earlier verse shows her seeking the materials used in this work.

units.notes: The distaff holds fibers. The spindle twists them into thread.
units.summary: Her skill includes the patient work of turning fiber into thread.
units.principle: Skill can be expressed in ordinary tasks.
units.insight: Quiet, repetitive work deserves recognition for what it makes possible.
units.application: Give careful attention to a routine task whose result someone relies on.

rel.note: The generous person is likewise blessed for sharing food with the poor.

units.notes: The open hand pictures practical generosity. The repeated line intensifies the action.
units.summary: She uses what her hands have gained to help the poor and needy.
units.principle: Diligence and mercy belong together.
units.insight: Generosity can be measured by whether it reaches a real need.
units.application: Share a useful resource from your work with someone who needs it.

rel.note: The ant likewise uses an available season to prepare for later need.

units.notes: Scarlet describes the household's clothing. A traditional alternative is double garments.
units.summary: She has prepared clothing for her whole household before winter comes.
units.principle: Faithful preparation attends to needs before they arrive.
units.insight: Care for practical needs can be joined with confidence in Christ's protection.
units.application: Prepare for one foreseeable need and thank Christ for the security His sacrifice gives.

rel.note: The later verse moves from actual clothing to the strength and honor that clothe her character.

units.notes: Tapestry refers to woven coverings. Fine linen and purple suggest dignity and costly workmanship.
units.summary: Her skilled work provides coverings and clothing of dignity.
units.principle: Dignity can be expressed through skillful provision.
units.insight: A person who cares for others can also receive ordinary care for themselves.
units.application: Give proper attention to a need of your own that you have been overlooking.

rel.note: The poem ends with her own works also praising her in the gates.

units.notes: Elders met at the city gates to judge and conduct public affairs.
units.summary: Her husband is known among the elders at the gates.
units.principle: Household faithfulness and public responsibility can support one another.
units.insight: People can honor the often unseen support that helps public responsibilities be carried well.
units.application: Thank someone whose quiet work helps you carry a visible responsibility.

rel.note: Skill in work is likewise commended for the opportunities it creates.

units.notes: Linen garments and sashes were marketable goods.
units.summary: Her skilled work supplies merchants and produces income.
units.principle: Well-made goods can serve buyers and sustain the person who makes them.
units.insight: Productive skill can be valued wherever it is practiced.
units.application: Improve one part of your work so the people receiving it can rely on its quality.

rel.note: The fear of the LORD gives strong confidence and refuge.

units.notes: Clothing here pictures character. Rejoicing at the future conveys confidence.
units.summary: Strength and honor clothe her, and she faces the future with joy.
units.principle: Inner strength gives a sounder basis for confidence than appearances.
units.insight: Confidence can grow through faithful preparation and trust in God.
units.application: Prepare for one concern you can address and entrust the rest to God.

rel.note: Gracious speech likewise helps learning gain a hearing.

units.notes: Law means teaching. Kindness describes the manner and substance of her instruction.
units.summary: She speaks wisdom and teaches with kindness.
units.principle: Kindness gives wise instruction a fitting voice.
units.insight: A clear correction can be offered with warmth and patience.
units.application: Explain one needed truth clearly and kindly to someone who can use it.

rel.note: The steward is likewise told to know the condition of what is entrusted to their care.

units.notes: Watching over describes sustained attention. Bread of idleness pictures subsisting in habitual neglect.
units.summary: She keeps watch over her household and attends to its needs.
units.principle: Diligence pays attention to what has been entrusted to one's care.
units.insight: Steady stewardship can include shared work and needed rest.
units.application: Notice one unmet household need and decide together how to address it.

rel.note: The husband's earlier confidence becomes audible praise.

units.notes: Rising expresses respect. Calling her blessed gives public voice within the family to gratitude.
units.summary: Her children and husband rise to honor her.
units.principle: Gratitude deserves expression.
units.insight: Appreciation is more meaningful when it names what someone has actually given.
units.application: Tell someone who has cared for you one specific good their care produced.

rel.note: The husband's praise answers the opening question about a woman of valor.

units.notes: Done well shares the word for strength or valor used in verse 10. These words continue the husband's praise.
units.summary: The husband expresses particular delight in the woman of valor.
units.principle: Faithful praise recognizes a person's particular worth.
units.insight: Affection can praise someone specifically without requiring others to compete.
units.application: Give someone close to you specific, sincere praise for a quality you value.

rel.note: The book opens with fear of the LORD as the beginning of knowledge and closes by honoring a woman who lives it.

units.notes: Passing evokes a breath or vapor. Fear of the LORD is a right view of God.
units.summary: A woman who fears the LORD deserves praise.
units.principle: A right view of God gives lasting worth to a life.
units.insight: The verse honors reverence in women across ages, circumstances, and marital status.
units.application: Praise a specific act of reverence or faithfulness that might otherwise go unnoticed.

rel.note: Attentive care and faithful service are likewise associated with receiving their fruit.

units.notes: Fruit of her hands means the results of her work. The gates are the public setting of community judgment and reputation.
units.summary: Give her the fruit of her work and let her deeds receive public praise.
units.principle: Honor should reach those whose faithful work has earned it.
units.insight: Practical recognition can include credit and a fair share of what a person's work produces.
units.application: Give public credit and appropriate recognition for work someone else has done.
